knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a barrier-regularized support function centered at a constrained analytic center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q\subset\mathbb E be closed and convex with no straight lines, let F be a \nu-self-concordant barrier on Q, let \widehat P\subset\mathbb E be closed and convex, set P=\widehat P\cap Q, and let x_0 be the constrained analytic center of P. For \beta>0, define U_\beta:\mathbb E^*\to\mathbb R by U_\beta(s)=\max_{u\in\widehat P}\{\langle s,u-x_0\rangle-\beta(F(u)-F(x_0))\}. Denote its unique maximizer by u_\beta^*(s).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex domain equipped with a self-concordant barrier and centered at its constrained analytic center, the barrier-smoothed support function is the maximum of the centered linear functional minus beta times the barrier displacement; its unique maximizer is denoted by u_beta^*(s).
assumptions_latex: Q\subset\mathbb E\text{ is closed, convex, and contains no straight lines}
\widehat P\subset\mathbb E\text{ is closed and convex},\quad P=\widehat P\cap Q
x_0\text{ is the constrained analytic center of }P
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_\beta(s):=\max_{u\in\widehat P}\left\{\langle s,u-x_0\rangle-\beta\bigl(F(u)-F(x_0)\bigr)\right\},\quad s\in\mathbb E^*,\qquad u_\beta^*(s):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in\widehat P}(\cdots)\text{ is unique}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rational bounds for omega and omega-star
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bounds have different domains: the omega inequalities hold for all nonnegative arguments, while the omega-star inequalities require the argument to be below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t\ge0\), if \(\omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t)\), then \[\frac{t^2}{2(1+t)}\le \frac{t^2}{2\left(1+\frac23t\right)}\le \omega(t)\le \frac{t^2}{2+t}.\] For \(t\in[0,1)\), if \(\omega_*(t)=-t-\ln(1-t)\), then \[\frac{t^2}{2-t}\le \omega_*(t)\le \frac{t^2}{2(1-t)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonnegative t, omega(t) lies between the stated rational quadratic lower and upper bounds. For t in [0,1), omega-star(t) lies between t squared over 2-t and t squared over 2(1-t).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{t^2}{2(1+t)}\le\frac{t^2}{2(1+\frac23t)}\le\omega(t)\le\frac{t^2}{2+t},\qquad \frac{t^2}{2-t}\le\omega_*(t)\le\frac{t^2}{2(1-t)}\ \text{on their respective domains}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Newton-Step Bound for the Self-Concordant Newton Decrement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain preservation and a one-step Newton-decrement bound for a self-concordant function when the current decrement is below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be self-concordant, let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and suppose \(\lambda_f(x)<1\). Define \[x_+=x-[f''(x)]^{-1}f'(x).\] Then \(x_+\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \[\lambda_f(x_+)\leq\left(\frac{\lambda_f(x)}{1-\lambda_f(x)}\right)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a self-concordant function, a full Newton step from a point whose Newton decrement is less than one remains in the function's domain. The new decrement is at most the square of the ratio of the old decrement to one minus the old decrement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_+\in\operatorname{dom}f\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_f(x_+)\leq\left(\frac{\lambda_f(x)}{1-\lambda_f(x)}\right)^2

children.top_down_role: Ordinary, strong, and homogeneous self-concordance regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-controlled self-concordant barriers used in interior-point analysis.

A standard self-concordant barrier \(F:D	o\mathbb R\) is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier if \[|DF(x)[h]|\le\sqrt

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized third-derivative convention and normalization by positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex \(C^3\) function \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is \(M\)-self-concordant when \[|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}\] for all \(x\in D\) and \(h\in\mathbb R^n\). For \(\alpha>0\), \(\alpha f\) is \((M/\sqrt\alpha)\)-self-concordant. If \(M>0\), choosing \(\alpha=M^2/4\) gives the standard constant \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The general third-derivative constant rescales inversely with the square root of a positive function multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is }M\text{-self-concordant}\Rightarrow\alpha f\text{ is }(M/\sqrt\alpha)\text{-self-concordant}.
knowledge_statements.title: Self-Concordance with a General Constant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Authority-dependent use of the term strongly self-concordant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The label “strongly self-concordant” is not convention-invariant: some authorities use it for self-concordance plus barrier blow-up at finite boundary points, while others impose additional closedness, nondegeneracy, or parameter conditions. Consequently, a theorem using this label must state the derivative, boundary, Hessian, and parameter assumptions explicitly rather than infer them from the name alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong self-concordance has varying definitions, so its operative assumptions must be stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The term strongly self-concordant does not by itself determine a unique mathematical class.}
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Self-Concordance Terminology Boundary

Self-Concordant Function Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional standard, strong barrier, and logarithmically homogeneous self-concordance conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex. A convex \(C^3\) function \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant when \[|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le 2\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}\] for every \(x\in D\) and \(h\in\mathbb R^n\). It is strongly self-concordant as a barrier when it additionally tends to \(+\infty\) at every finite boundary point of \(D\). If \(D\) is a cone and \(f(tx)=f(x)-\nu\log t\) for all \(t>0\), it belongs to the \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard self-concordance bounds the third derivative by the Hessian; strong barrier behavior adds boundary blow-up, while homogeneous self-concordance adds logarithmic scaling on a cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le2(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}\), with the stated boundary or homogeneity conditions distinguishing the subclasses.

notation.meaning: The kth Fréchet derivative of f at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classification fits the container, but “strongly self-concordant” is authority-dependent and boundary blow-up alone may not match the intended convention. A specific definition locator is required.

children.title: Hessian-Induced Local Norms
children.top_down_role: Local primal metrics derived from barrier curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Covariance of the Local Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-coordinate transformation law for Hessian local lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x=Tz+a with T invertible and define g(z)=f(Tz+a). Then \nabla^2g(z)=T^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)T and, for every displacement d, \|d\|_{g,z}=\|Td\|_{f,x}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian local lengths are preserved when both the Hessian and displacement are transformed under invertible affine coordinates.

notation.meaning: Expression of the function in transformed coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Covariance of the Local Norm

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian-Induced Local Inner Product and Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical tangent-space metric at a point with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\in C^2(D)\) and \(x\in D\) with \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), define \[\langle u,v\rangle_x=u^{\mathsf T}H_xv,\qquad\|u\|_x=(u^{\mathsf T}H_xu)^{1/2}=\|H_x^{1/2}u\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Hessian defines a base-point-dependent inner product and tangent norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\cdot\|_x\text{ is a norm induced by }\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_x.

notation.meaning: Primal local norm at the base point.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Induced Local Inner Product and Norm

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Definiteness Boundary for Hessian Local Norms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction among norms, seminorms, and indefinite quadratic forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(H_x\), \((u^{\mathsf T}H_xu)^{1/2}\) is a norm exactly when \(H_x\succ0\). If \(H_x\succeq0\) is singular, it is only a seminorm and vanishes on \(\ker H_x\). If \(H_x\) has a negative eigenvalue, the expression is not a real-valued norm on all directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive definiteness yields a norm, singular semidefiniteness only a seminorm, and indefiniteness no real norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_x\succ0\iff\bigl(u\mapsto\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}H_xu}\bigr)\text{ is a norm}.
knowledge_statements.title: Definiteness Boundary for Hessian Local Norms
Hessian-Induced Local Norms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal local norm generated by a positive-definite barrier Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable on an open convex set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\). The Hessian-induced local inner product and norm at \(x\in D\) are \[\langle u,v\rangle_x=u^{\mathsf T}H_xv,\qquad \|u\|_x=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}H_xu}.\] Thus the local geometry varies with the base point through \(H_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Hessian defines a base-point-dependent inner product and norm on displacement vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|u\|_x=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)u}\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: The Hessian of f at the base point x.

children.title: Dual Local Norms
children.top_down_role: Cotangent metrics associated with barrier Hessians.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical primal-to-dual and dual-to-primal identifications induced by the local Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_x\succ0\), \(\|u\|_x^2=u^{\mathsf T}H_xu\), and \(\|s\|_x^{*2}=s^{\mathsf T}H_x^{-1}s\). Then \[\|H_xu\|_x^*=\|u\|_x,\qquad \|H_x^{-1}s\|_x=\|s\|_x^*.\] Thus \(H_x\) and \(H_x^{-1}\) are mutually inverse isometries between the local primal and dual normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian and inverse Hessian are inverse length-preserving identifications between local tangent and cotangent norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Riesz Isometries
Dual Local Norms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual norm associated with the Hessian local metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), the dual local norm of a covector \(s\in\mathbb R^n\) is \[\|s\|_x^*=\sup_{\|u\|_x\le1}\langle s,u\rangle=\sqrt{s^{\mathsf T}H_x^{-1}s}.\] Consequently, local Cauchy–Schwarz gives \(|\langle s,u\rangle|\le\|s\|_x^*\|u\|_x\), with equality for a nonzero scalar multiple of \(u=H_x^{-1}s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual local norm uses the inverse Hessian and satisfies the corresponding local Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s\|_x^*=\sqrt{s^{\mathsf T}H_x^{-1}s}\) and \(|\langle s,u\rangle|\le\|s\|_x^*\|u\|_x\).

notation.meaning: Dual norm of the Hessian-induced local norm.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dual norm of a positive-definite quadratic norm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-Hessian dual norm and inequality are consistent with the primal local norm, but the record lacks an inspectable source locator.

children.title: Dikin Ellipsoids
children.top_down_role: Interior ellipsoids generated by local barrier metrics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Unit Dikin Radius
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The universal strict-interiority radius cannot be enlarged or closed at one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D=(0,\infty)\) and \(f(x)=-\log x\), one has \(\|h\|_x=|h|/x\). Taking \(h=-x\) gives \[\|h\|_x=1,\qquad x+h=0\notin D.\] Hence replacing the universal condition \(\|h\|_x<1\) by \(\|h\|_x\le1\), or by any larger universal radius, is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the scalar logarithmic barrier, a displacement of local norm exactly one reaches the boundary, so the open unit Dikin guarantee is sharp.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|-x\|_x=1\) while \(x-x=0\notin D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Unit Dikin Radius
Dikin Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit local-metric neighborhood and its barrier-domain containment property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in D\) and \(r>0\), the open Dikin ellipsoid of radius \(r\) is \[E_x(r)=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\|y-x\|_x<r\}.\] If \(f\) is a standard self-concordant barrier on \(D\), then \(E_x(1)\subset D\). Hence every displacement \(h\) satisfying \(\|h\|_x<1\) preserves strict feasibility: \(x+h\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dikin ellipsoid is a Hessian-metric ball; its open unit ball lies inside a self-concordant barrier domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a standard self-concordant barrier on \(D\).

notation.meaning: Open Dikin ellipsoid of radius r centered at x.

children.title: Local Metric Comparison
children.top_down_role: Variation of local metrics across nearby interior points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion from a forward Dikin distance to the reverse-base-point distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a standard self-concordant f, if r=\|y-x\|_x<1, then \|x-y\|_y\le r/(1-r). Consequently, r<1/2 implies \|x-y\|_y<1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A displacement short at one endpoint remains quantitatively controlled at the other endpoint.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x-y\|_y\le\frac{r}{1-r};\qquad r<\frac12\Rightarrow\|x-y\|_y<1.

notation.meaning: Local distance from x to y measured at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Local-Distance Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm and Loewner-order comparison at nearby interior points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D	o\mathbb R\) be standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian. If \(x\in D\), \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r=\|d\|_x<1\), then \(y=x+d\in D\) and, for every \(h\), \[(1-r)\|h\|_x\le\|h\|_y\le(1-r)^{-1}\|h\|_x.\] Equivalently, \[(1-r)^2
abla^2f(x)\preceq
abla^2f(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}
abla^2f(x).\] The universal factors diverge as \(r\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within strict unit local distance, self-concordance compares Hessians and tangent norms by reciprocal factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
(1-r)^2
abla^2f(x)\preceq
abla^2f(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}
abla^2f(x).

notation.meaning: Forward local length of the displacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Concordant Local Metric Comparison
Local Metric Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of self-concordant Hessian metrics at nearby points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be standard self-concordant, let \(x\in D\), and take \(y\in D\) with \(r=\|y-x\|_x<1\). Then, for every \(h\in\mathbb R^n\), \[(1-r)\|h\|_x\le\|h\|_y\le rac{1}{1-r}\|h\|_x.\] Equivalently in Loewner order, \[(1-r)^2
abla^2f(x)\preceq
abla^2f(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}
abla^2f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inside a unit Dikin neighborhood, Hessian norms and Hessians at two points differ by explicit factors determined by their local distance.
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.

notation.meaning: Local distance from x to y measured at x.

children.title: Newton Convergence-Regime Geometry
children.top_down_role: Proximity measures and damped or quadratic Newton regimes.

children.title: Newton Decrement Geometry
children.top_down_role: Barrier-metric measures of proximity to a local minimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori objective-gap bounds for a standard self-concordant objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be convex and standard self-concordant, let \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), and suppose \(f^*=\min_{z\in D}f(z)\) is attained. Define \(\omega(t)=t-\log(1+t)\) for \(t\ge0\) and \(\omega_*(t)=-t-\log(1-t)\) for \(0\le t<1\). Then \[\omega(\lambda(x))\le f(x)-f^*.\] If \(\lambda(x)<1\), then \[f(x)-f^*\le\omega_*(\lambda(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton decrement gives a lower objective-gap bound and, below one, an explicit upper-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is convex and standard self-concordant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\omega(\lambda(x))\le f(x)-f^*\le\omega_*(\lambda(x))\) when \(\lambda(x)<1\), with only the lower inequality asserted otherwise.

notation.meaning: The function minus t minus log(1-t).

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Decrement Objective-Gap Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity and minimizer test encoded by the decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and convex, with \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\). Then \[\lambda(x)=0\iff\nabla f(x)=0.\] Either condition makes \(x\) a global minimizer of \(f\) on \(D\); if \(f\) is strictly convex, the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decrement vanishes exactly at a stationary point, which is globally optimal for a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(x)=0\iff\nabla f(x)=0\Rightarrow x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in D}f(z)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Decrement Optimality Test
Newton Decrement Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent local-norm representations of the Newton decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in D\), write \(g_x=\nabla f(x)\), \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), and \(n_x=-H_x^{-1}g_x\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap bound for iterations above a fixed Newton-decrement threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply x_{k+1}=x_k+n_k/(1+\lambda_k) to a standard self-concordant convex function having a minimizer x^*. For \beta>0, every iteration with \lambda_k\ge\beta decreases the objective by at least \delta_\beta=\beta-\log(1+\beta)>0. Thus the number N_\beta of such iterations satisfies N_\beta\le\left\lfloor\frac{f(x_0)-f(x^*)}{\beta-\log(1+\beta)}\right\rfloor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only finitely many damped iterations can remain above a fixed decrement threshold, with an explicit objective-gap bound.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is standard self-concordant, convex, and has positive-definite Hessian}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_\beta\le\left\lfloor\frac{f(x_0)-f(x^*)}{\beta-\log(1+\beta)}\right\rfloor.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant strict local region and convergence of repeated full Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be convex and standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian, and set \(c=(3-\sqrt5)/2\). If \(\lambda(x_0)<c\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\), then every \(x_k\in D\), \(\lambda(x_{k+1})\le \lambda(x_k)^2/(1-\lambda(x_k))^2<\lambda(x_k)\), and \(\lambda(x_k)\to0\). In particular, the decrement converges quadratically once the iterates are in this strict region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting strictly below the standard nonincrease threshold, repeated full Newton steps remain interior and their decrements converge to zero quadratically.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Newton Can Exit the Barrier Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar self-concordant example showing failure of undamped Newton outside the local regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For f(t)=-\log t+t on (0,\infty), the Newton direction is n(t)=t-t^2 and the full iterate is t^+=2t-t^2. Hence t^+\le0 for every t\ge2. The Newton decrement is \lambda(t)=|t-1|, so domain exit occurs when \lambda(t)\ge1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full Newton step sufficiently far from the minimizer can leave the barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\ge2\Rightarrow t^+=2t-t^2\le0\notin(0,\infty),\qquad \lambda(t)=|t-1|\ge1.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact range in which the standard full-Newton decrement majorant proves contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full Newton step with \(0\le\lambda<1\), the standard majorant is \[\lambda_+\le q(\lambda):=\frac{\lambda^2}{(1-\lambda)^2}.\] It certifies \(\lambda_+\le\lambda\) exactly when \[0\le\lambda\le\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}.\] Above this threshold the majorant alone does not prove contraction; this is not a claim that the actual step diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual decrement majorant proves contraction only through the golden-ratio-derived threshold.
assumptions_latex: The standard full-step self-concordant decrement majorant applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\lambda)\le\lambda\iff0\le\lambda\le(3-\sqrt5)/2.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The universal Dikin feasibility guarantee is strict: \(\|h\|_x<1\) ensures \(x+h\in D\), but radius one cannot be included. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differential Identities for the Negative Log-Determinant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and directional derivative formulas on the positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(X)=-\ln\det X\). For every \(X\in\mathcal P_n\) and \(\Delta\in\mathbb S^{n\times n}\), \(F\) is convex, \(F'(X)=-X^{-1}\), and
\[\langle F''(X)\Delta,\Delta\rangle_F=\|X^{-1/2}\Delta X^{-1/2}\|_F^2=\langle X^{-1}\Delta X^{-1},\Delta\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}\!\left((X^{-1/2}\Delta X^{-1/2})^2\right),\]
while
\[D^3F(X)[\Delta,\Delta,\Delta]=-2\langle I_n,(X^{-1/2}\Delta X^{-1/2})^3\rangle_F=-2\operatorname{tr}\!\left((X^{-1/2}\Delta X^{-1/2})^3\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative log-determinant is convex on the positive-definite cone. Its gradient is −X⁻¹; its Hessian quadratic form is the squared Frobenius norm of X⁻¹ᐟ²ΔX⁻¹ᐟ²; and its third directional derivative is −2 times the trace of the cube of that matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is convex},\quad F'(X)=-X^{-1},\quad \langle F''(X)\Delta,\Delta\rangle_F=\|X^{-1/2}\Delta X^{-1/2}\|_F^2,\quad D^3F(X)[\Delta,\Delta,\Delta]=-2\operatorname{tr}((X^{-1/2}\Delta X^{-1/2})^3)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Barriers Need Not Be Logarithmically Homogeneous
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of the general class from its logarithmically homogeneous sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(D=(-1,1)\), \[F(x)=-\log(1-x)-\log(1+x)=-\log(1-x^2)\] is a self-concordant barrier, but \(D\) is not a cone and no \(\nu\) makes \(F(tx)=F(x)-\nu\log t\) valid throughout its domain. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance under invertible affine reparameterization without imposing conic homogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and let \(T(z)=Az+b\) be an affine bijection from an open convex set \(D'\) onto \(D\). Then \[G(z)=F(Az+b)\] is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D'\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=F\circ T\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D'\).

General Self-Concordant Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier definition without cone homogeneity or self-scaling assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex. A function \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier if it is convex, three times continuously differentiable, tends to \(+\infty\) along every sequence approaching \(\partial D\), and satisfies \[|D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\le2\bigl(D^2F(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2},\qquad |DF(x)[h]|\le\sqrt\nu\bigl(D^2F(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{1/2}\] for all \(x\in D\) and \(h\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general self-concordant barrier combines boundary blow-up, the cubic derivative inequality, and a gradient bound with parameter ν.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier precisely under the stated boundary and differential inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-Concordant Barrier for the Negative Log-Determinant Epigraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit barrier and its parameter for a matrix-function epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[E=\{(H,\tau)\in\mathbb S^{n\times n}\times\mathbb R:\ H\in\mathcal P_n,\ \tau\ge-\ln\det H\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a pointed convex cone with nonempty interior, and let \(F\) be a \(\vartheta\)-normal barrier for \(K\). Its dual barrier is self-scaled on the dual cone exactly when the original barrier is self-scaled.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Scaled Barrier Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional classification on irreducible and reducible symmetric cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_m\) be a symmetric cone decomposed into irreducible symmetric cones, with Jordan determinants \(\det_i\) and ranks \(r_i\). Every self-scaled barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\), up to addition of a constant and the standard normalization convention, has the form
\[
F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=c-\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i\log\det_i(x_i),\qquad \alpha_i\ge 1.
\]
Conversely, every such function is self-scaled. Its logarithmic-homogeneity and self-concordance parameter is \(\nu=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i r_i\). Consequently, a regular cone admits a self-scaled barrier only if it is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-scaled barriers occur exactly on symmetric cones and are weighted sums of the irreducible cones’ standard log-determinant barriers, up to normalization and an additive constant.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional closed, pointed, full-dimensional cone.
\(F\) satisfies the self-scaled-barrier axioms under their standard normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=c-\sum_i\alpha_i\log\det_i\), with \(\alpha_i\ge1\), and existence forces \(K\) to be symmetric.

notation.meaning: Jordan rank of the factor K_i

review_flags: Exact self-scaled classification theorem and normalization require an authoritative source.
standard_field_rationale: classical classification of self-scaled barriers on symmetric cones

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the classification leaf and its mathematical role, but the exact coefficient bound, normalization convention, converse, parameter formula, and claim that existence forces symmetry require a specific authoritative classification theorem and locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique scaling-point characterization of self-scaled barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes self-scaled barriers through existence and uniqueness of an interior scaling point satisfying gradient and barrier-value identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a pointed convex cone with nonempty interior, and let \(F\) be a \(\vartheta\)-normal barrier for \(K\). Then \(F\) is a \(\vartheta\)-self-scaled barrier if and only if, for every \(x,w\in\operatorname{int}K\), there exists a unique \(z\in\operatorname{int}K\) such that \(-F'(z)=F''(w)x\) and \(F(w)=\tfrac12\bigl(F(x)+F(z)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theta-normal barrier is self-scaled exactly when every pair of interior points x and w determines a unique interior point z whose negative gradient equals the Hessian-scaled point and whose barrier value satisfies the stated midpoint identity.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is a pointed convex cone with }\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is }\vartheta\text{-self-scaled}\iff \forall x,w\in\operatorname{int}K\ \exists!z\in\operatorname{int}K:\ -F'(z)=F''(w)x\ \land\ F(w)=\frac{F(x)+F(z)}{2}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the model-specific logarithmic barrier on the domain where all displayed logarithms are finite and records its associated parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed data $a_i,b_i,v$, on the domain
\[
H\succ0,\qquad \tau+\ln\det H>0,\qquad (b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle)^2-\langle Ha_i,a_i\rangle>0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),

define

\]
The associated barrier parameter is $\nu=m+n+1$.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-order universal upper bound and its path-following consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every proper cone \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), there is a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier whose parameter satisfies \(\nu\le Cn\), where \(C\) is universal. When this barrier and its first two derivatives are available through an exact barrier oracle, a standard short-step method reaches relative duality-gap accuracy \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) in
\[

children.title: Existence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Domain features obstructing standard barrier existence guarantees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failures of the standard nondegenerate conic barrier model and their canonical reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone. If \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}K=\varnothing\), no standard ambient-space barrier can have domain \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}K\); one must first work in \(L=\operatorname{span}K\). If \(K\cap(-K)\ne\{0\}\), translations along its lineality space leave the cone invariant, so a logarithmically homogeneous barrier cannot supply a positive-definite barrier Hessian in those directions. Passing to the quotient \(L/(K\cap(-K))\) produces the pointed effective cone to which proper-cone barrier existence theory applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Empty ambient interior requires restriction to the cone's span, while lineality requires quotienting before a nondegenerate barrier metric is available.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
A standard barrier is required to have an open domain in its effective space and a positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}K=\varnothing\text{ or }K\cap(-K)\ne\{0\}\Longrightarrow\text{the unreduced standard barrier model is unavailable}.
review_flags: The conclusion concerns the standard nondegenerate barrier definition; boundary-divergent convex functions with degenerate Hessians are not classified as standard barriers here.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambient-Interior and Lineality Obstructions
Existence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient-space failures caused by empty interior or cone lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The usual conic barrier framework requires a proper cone. If a closed convex cone \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) has empty interior, no barrier with open domain \(\operatorname{int}K\) exists in the ambient space. If \(K\) contains a nonzero line \(\mathbb{R}d\), then any convex function compatible with translations along the lineality space cannot have a positive-definite Hessian on \(\mathbb{R}^n\); consequently it cannot induce the nondegenerate local norm required of a standard self-concordant barrier. These failures may be removed by passing to \(\operatorname{span}K\) and quotienting its lineality space before constructing a barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Empty interior prevents an ambient barrier domain, while lineality makes the barrier metric degenerate; relative-span and quotient reductions are required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A standard ambient-space barrier requires \(\operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing\) and \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\).
review_flags: Needs a source distinguishing ambient barriers, relative-interior barriers, and quotient constructions.
standard_field_rationale: nonempty interior and pointedness are the standard regular-cone hypotheses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugacy with the sign convention natural for dual cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a closed Legendre-type barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\), where \(K\) is proper, and define its dual barrier by
\[
F_*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle s,x\rangle-F(x)\},\qquad s\in\operatorname{int}K^*.
\]
Whenever the supremum is attained, its unique maximizer \(x\) satisfies \(s=-\nabla F(x)\), and
\[
F_*(s)=-\langle s,x\rangle-F(x).
\]
If \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier, then \(F_*\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\), and the transformation is involutive under this sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The signed Fenchel conjugate is a barrier on the dual cone; primal and dual points correspond through the negative barrier gradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinitesimal isometry between paired primal and dual barrier metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At paired points \(s=-
abla F(x)\), put \(H=
abla^2F(x)\) and \(H_* =
abla^2F_*(s)=H^{-1}\). For every tangent vector \(h\), \[D(-
abla F)(x)h=-Hh,\qquad \|-Hh\|_{s,F_*}=\|h\|_{x,F}.\] Thus the differential of the negative-gradient correspondence is an isometry between the paired Hessian metrics.

Under the signed Legendre correspondence, let \(s=-\nabla F(x)\) and let \(F_*\) be the dual barrier. Then

Consequently, for every primal tangent vector \(h\) and dual covector \(u\),
\[
\|h\|_x^2=\langle h,\nabla^2F(x)h\rangle,
\qquad

=\langle u,\nabla^2F(x)^{-1}u\rangle.
\]
Thus the conjugate Hessian is the inverse primal metric at paired points.

children.title: Affine-Section Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier restriction to affine slices of convex domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a self-concordant barrier to a nonempty affine section, formulated intrinsically on that section.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\), and let \(H=x_0+L\) be an affine subspace such that \(D_H:=D\cap H\neq\varnothing\). Regard \(D_H\) as an open convex set in the affine space \(H\). Then the restriction
\[
F_H=F|_{D_H}
\]
is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D_H\). For \(x\in D_H\) and \(h,k\in L\), its intrinsic derivatives are
\[
DF_H(x)[h]=DF(x)[h],\qquad D^2F_H(x)[h,k]=D^2F(x)[h,k],
\]
with the analogous restriction for the third derivative. Thus self-concordance, the barrier inequality, and boundary blow-up are inherited on the affine section without an additional recession-direction hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a self-concordant barrier to a nonempty affine section preserves its parameter, with all derivatives restricted to the section's tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on the open convex set \(D\).
\(H=x_0+L\) is an affine subspace and \(D\cap H\neq\varnothing\).
The section is equipped with its intrinsic affine-space topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F|_{D\cap H}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\cap H\).

notation.meaning: affine section with tangent subspace L
nonempty intrinsic domain D intersected with H

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Affine-Section Barrier Restriction
Affine-Section Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a barrier to a nonempty affine section.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\), and let \(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be injective. For \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), suppose
\[
S=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^p:Az+b\in D\}
\]
is nonempty and contains no direction along which the image remains interior while approaching the boundary of \(S\). Then
\[
G(z)=F(Az+b),\quad \nabla G(z)=A^{\mathsf T}\nabla F(Az+b),\quad
\nabla^2G(z)=A^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(Az+b)A
\]
defines a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on the affine section \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a barrier to a nonempty affine section preserves its parameter; gradients and Hessians follow the affine chain rule.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on the open convex set \(D\).
\(A\) is injective and \(S=\{z:Az+b\in D\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=F\circ(A\cdot+b)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(S\).

notation.meaning: transpose of the affine section map

review_flags: The precise barrier blow-up condition for possibly unbounded affine parameterizations needs a source.
standard_field_rationale: self-concordance is preserved under injective affine substitution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is reasonable for an affine-section construction, and the chain-rule formulas are correct. The additional condition about a direction whose image remains interior while approaching the boundary is not mathematically precise, and no source establishes that it is the appropriate barrier blow-up hypothesis. The exact theorem cannot be accepted without a source-supported formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States differential transfer and the precise nondegenerate barrier specialization for affine inverse images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D\), let \(T(z)=Az+b\), and let \(S=T^{-1}(D)
eq\varnothing\). For \(G=F\circ T\), \[D^kG(z)[h_1,\ldots,h_k]=D^kF(Tz)[Ah_1,\ldots,Ah_k],\qquad k=1,2,3.\] Hence the differential self-concordance and barrier-parameter inequalities are preserved. If \(A\) is injective, then \(G\) has positive-definite Hessian and diverges along every sequence in \(S\) converging to \(\partial S\); consequently \(G\) is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine composition preserves self-concordant differential inequalities, and an injective affine pullback gives a barrier with the same parameter on the inverse-image domain.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on the open convex set \(D\).
For the genuine-barrier conclusion, \(A\) is injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under injectivity, \(F\circ T\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(T^{-1}(D)\).

u\log	au\) on \(\operatorname{int}K\), \(S=A^{-1}(\operatorname{int}K)\), and \(G(x)=F(Ax)\), then \[G(	au x)=G(x)-

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Pullback Preserves Logarithmic Homogeneity
Inverse-Image Barrier Pullbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier calculus for affine inverse images of open convex domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex set \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(T(z)=Az+b\). On the nonempty inverse image
\[
S=T^{-1}(D)=\{z:Az+b\in D\},
\]
the pullback \(G=F\circ T\) satisfies
\[
D^2G(z)[h,h]=D^2F(Tz)[Ah,Ah],\qquad
D^3G(z)[h,h,h]=D^3F(Tz)[Ah,Ah,Ah].
\]
Therefore the self-concordance differential inequality is preserved. If the pullback Hessian is positive definite and every sequence approaching \(\partial S\) has its image approach \(\partial D\), then \(G\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine pullback preserves the self-concordance inequality; it is a genuine barrier when the pulled-back Hessian is nondegenerate and boundary approach is preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\circ T\) preserves self-concordance and is a \(\nu\)-barrier under metric nondegeneracy and boundary properness.
review_flags: Needs an authoritative affine-composition theorem specifying sufficient barrier-boundary conditions.
standard_field_rationale: directional derivatives under affine composition preserve the self-concordance inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the inverse-image pullback leaf, and the directional derivative identities correctly preserve the differential self-concordance inequality. The sufficient conditions for barrier blow-up and preservation of the same barrier parameter require a precise affine-composition theorem and locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric Characterization of the Injective Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the exact rank condition and local-norm representation for a nondegenerate affine pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(z)=F(Az+b)\) and \(H(z)=\nabla^2F(Az+b)\succ0\). Then \[\nabla^2G(z)=A^{\mathsf T}H(z)A\succ0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\ker A=\{0\}.\] In this regime, \[\|h\|_{G,z}=\|Ah\|_{F,Az+b},\qquad \|s\|_{G,z,*}^2=s^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}H(z)A)^{-1}s.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pullback metric is positive definite exactly when the linear map is injective; its local norm is the target norm of the mapped direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}H(z)A\succ0\) exactly when \(A\) has full column rank.

notation.meaning: Target barrier Hessian at the affine image.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Characterization of the Injective Regime
Injective Pullback Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-algebraic condition for a nondegenerate pulled-back barrier metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H(y)=\nabla^2F(y)\succ0\) on \(D\), and let \(G(z)=F(Az+b)\). The pulled-back Hessian is
\[
\nabla^2G(z)=A^{\mathsf T}H(Az+b)A.
\]
For every \(z\) in the inverse-image domain, this matrix is positive definite if and only if \(\ker A=\{0\}\). Indeed,
\[
h^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2G(z)h=(Ah)^{\mathsf T}H(Az+b)(Ah)>0
\]
for every nonzero \(h\) exactly when \(Ah\ne0\). Hence injectivity is the precise condition under which affine pullback retains a genuine local norm on the parameter space without quotienting null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine pullback has a positive-definite barrier Hessian exactly when the linear part is injective, assuming the original Hessian is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(G(z)=F(Az+b)\) is defined on a nonempty inverse-image domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(Az+b)A\succ0\) for all admissible \(z\) if and only if \(\ker A=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: nullspace of the pullback linear map

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x)=Ax+b\), \(N=\ker A\), \(S=T^{-1}(D)\), and \(G=F\circ T\). Then \(S+N=S\), \(G(x+n)=G(x)\) for \(n\in N\), and \(G\) descends to \(\bar G:S/N\to\mathbb R\). If \(\nabla^2F(Tx)\succ0\), then \[\langle[h],[k]\rangle_x=(Ah)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(Tx)(Ak)\] is a well-defined positive-definite inner product on the quotient tangent space. Boundary divergence of \(\bar G\) remains a separate requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient pullback is constant along the map kernel and acquires a nondegenerate metric after quotienting, but quotienting alone does not prove the barrier property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=\bar G\circ\pi\), and the induced quotient Hessian is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the product construction and its intrinsic derivative and local-norm structure while leaving parameter accounting to its sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_i\) be self-concordant barriers on \(\operatorname{int}C_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,r\), and define \[F(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=\sum_{i=1}^rF_i(x_i)\] on \(C_1	imes\cdots	imes C_r\). Then \(F\) is a self-concordant barrier, \[
abla F(x)=(
abla F_i(x_i))_{i=1}^r,\qquad 
abla^2F(x)=\operatorname{diag}(
abla^2F_i(x_i))_{i=1}^r,\] and \[\|h\|_{F,x}^2=\sum_{i=1}^r\|h_i\|_{F_i,x_i}^2.\] Consequently, barrier-oracle evaluations are componentwise; external constraints may still couple the enclosing Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing barriers gives a barrier on a finite Cartesian product with blockwise derivatives and an additive squared local norm, although external constraints can recouple solver equations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_i\) is a self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}C_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Product Barrier and Block Metric
Cartesian-Product Barrier Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional product rule for self-concordant barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,r\), let \(F_i:\operatorname{int}C_i\to\mathbb{R}\) be a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier. On \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_r\), define
\[F(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=\sum_{i=1}^r F_i(x_i).\]
The derivatives of \(F\) are block-separable, its Hessian is block diagonal, and \(F\) diverges whenever a component approaches its boundary. Consequently, \(F\) is a self-concordant barrier for \(C\), with barrier parameter at most \(\sum_{i=1}^r\nu_i\) under the standard parameter convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing component barriers produces a barrier on the Cartesian product, with block-diagonal Hessian and additive parameter bound.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is a convex set with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\sum_{i=1}^rF_i\) is a \(\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^r\nu_i\bigr)\)-self-concordant barrier for \(\prod_{i=1}^rC_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite Cartesian-product rule and additive parameter bound are standard, precise, and appropriately classified as a property, but the record has no inspectable source locator.

assumptions_latex: Each \(D_i\) is a nonempty open connected subset of a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is additively block-separable up to a constant if and only if every off-diagonal Hessian block vanishes identically.

notation.meaning: Mixed Hessian block between component coordinates i and j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact smooth criterion for additive separability in fixed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=D_1\times\cdots\times D_r\) be an open connected product and \(F\in C^2(D)\). Then \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=c+\sum_iF_i(x_i)\) for component functions \(F_i\) if and only if \(\nabla^2_{ij}F(x)=0\) for every \(i\neq j\) and every \(x\in D\). The assertion concerns the displayed block coordinates; an invertible change of variables can alter apparent separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected product domain, a twice-differentiable function is additively block-separable exactly when all mixed Hessian blocks vanish in the chosen coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Hessian Separability Criterion

assumptions_latex: The proposed blocks are the displayed scalar coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is not a Cartesian product and \(\partial_{12}^2G=(1-x_1-x_2)^{-2}\neq0\), so \(G\) is not additively separable in these coordinates.

notation.meaning: Standard logarithmic barrier for its three strict inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular coupled-domain example outside product-barrier calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(D=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2:x_1>0,\ x_2>0,\ x_1+x_2<1\}\), the standard barrier \(G(x)=-\log x_1-\log x_2-\log(1-x_1-x_2)\) has \(\partial^2G/(\partial x_1\partial x_2)=(1-x_1-x_2)^{-2}>0\). The domain is not a Cartesian product in the displayed coordinates, so neither its geometry nor this barrier admits the proposed additive two-block decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A triangular domain and its standard logarithmic barrier have genuinely coupled geometry and nonzero mixed curvature, so product-barrier calculus does not apply in the displayed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Domain Counterexample
Reducibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separability fails when the feasible geometry does not decompose into independent factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A barrier of the form \(F(x_1,x_2)=F_1(x_1)+F_2(x_2)\) has zero mixed derivative block and a Cartesian-product domain. Hence it cannot represent genuinely coupled feasible geometry. For example, on
\[D=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x_1+x_2>0\},\qquad G(x)=-\log(x_1+x_2),\]
one has \(\partial^2G/(\partial x_1\partial x_2)=1/(x_1+x_2)^2\neq0\). Thus \(G\) is not additively separable in the displayed coordinates, and product-barrier calculus applies only after an actual product decomposition or an appropriate linear reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product calculus does not cover coupled domains: their barriers can have nonzero mixed curvature and cannot be written as sums of component barriers.

children.title: Lifted Convex Barrier Calculus
children.top_down_role: Barrier constructions for lifted nonlinear convex representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-Self-Concordant Barrier for the Negative-Logarithm Epigraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit barrier construction for the lifted epigraph of the negative-logarithm function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_1:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x>0,\ t\ge -\ln x\}, with \operatorname{int}(Q_1)=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x>0,\ t>-\ln x\}. Define F_1:\operatorname{int}(Q_1)\to\mathbb{R} by F_1(x,t):=-\ln x-\ln(\ln x+t). Then F_1 is a 3\text{-self-concordant barrier for }Q_1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the epigraph Q1 of the negative-logarithm function, F1(x,t) = -log(x) - log(log(x) + t), defined on the interior of Q1, is a 3-self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1\text{ is a }3\text{-self-concordant barrier for }Q_1.

children.title: Lifted-Representation Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barriers for extended formulations with auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier Use in an Extended Formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a barrier in lifted variables from a barrier on the projected set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E,Y\) be finite-dimensional, let \(Q\subset E\times Y\) be convex with nonempty interior, and let \(C=\{x\in E:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\). If \(G\) is a self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}Q\), an interior-point formulation may retain \((x,y)\) and use \(G(x,y)\) directly. Every feasible lift certifies \(x\in C\), but \(G\) does not by itself determine a barrier depending only on \(x\); eliminating \(y\) requires additional fiberwise hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted barrier is used on the extended variables, and a feasible lift certifies projected membership; a projected barrier does not follow automatically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\in Q\Rightarrow x\in C\), while no barrier on \(C\) follows without an additional elimination theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Use in an Extended Formulation
Lifted-Representation Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier representation obtained by retaining auxiliary variables in an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subset E\times Y\) be a closed convex set with nonempty interior, let \(C=\{x\in E:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\), and let \(G\) be a self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}Q\). The lifted representation treats \((x,y)\) as the optimization variable and uses \(G(x,y)\) directly. It is a barrier for the extended feasible set, while feasibility of its projection certifies \(x\in C\). Without additional fiberwise minimization hypotheses, \(G\) does not by itself define a barrier depending only on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier for an extended formulation is used in the lifted variables; obtaining a barrier solely on the projection requires additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset E\times Y\) is closed, convex, and has nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\in Q\Longrightarrow x\in C\), but a projected barrier \(F(x)\) is not determined without further fiber conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between a barrier in lifted variables and a barrier on the projection matches the representation leaf. The spaces should be explicitly finite-dimensional for the stated self-concordant setting, and the claim needs an authoritative lifted-formulation source.

children.title: Perspective Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier families associated with perspective transformations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perspective-Form Barrier Candidate and Scaling Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the perspective-domain construction and states exactly what follows without compatibility assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex set \(C\) with nonempty interior and a function \(F\) finite on \(\operatorname{int}C\), define \[C^\pi=\{(x,t):t>0,\ x/t\in\operatorname{int}C\},\qquad F^\pi_\alpha(x,t)=F(x/t)-\alpha\log t,\quad \alpha>0.\] Then, for \(\lambda>0\), \[F^\pi_\alpha(\lambda x,\lambda t)=F^\pi_\alpha(x,t)-\alpha\log\lambda.\] The formula inherits divergence when the normalized point approaches \(\partial C\), and it diverges as \(t\downarrow0\) when the normalized points remain in a region where \(F\) is bounded below. Convexity and self-concordance require additional compatibility conditions on \(F\) and \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective homogenization has an exact logarithmic scaling law, but its convexity, complete boundary behavior, and self-concordance are not automatic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^\pi_\alpha(\lambda x,\lambda t)=F^\pi_\alpha(x,t)-\alpha\log\lambda\), with barrier status requiring separate verification.

notation.meaning: Open perspective homogenization of the base domain.
Coefficient of the logarithmic scale term.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective-Form Barrier Candidate and Scaling Law
Perspective Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective-form candidate on the homogenization of a convex barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset E\) be convex with nonempty interior and let \(F:\operatorname{int}C\to\mathbb{R}\). Its perspective-domain homogenization is
\[C^{\pi}=\{(x,t):t>0,\ x/t\in\operatorname{int}C\}.\]
For \(\alpha>0\), the associated perspective-form function is
\[F^{\pi}_{\alpha}(x,t)=F(x/t)-\alpha\log t.\]
This formula diverges when \(t\downarrow0\) through bounded normalized points and inherits divergence when \(x/t\) approaches \(\partial C\). Convexity and self-concordance of \(F^{\pi}_{\alpha}\), however, require compatibility conditions on \(F\) and \(\alpha\); they do not follow from the barrier property alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective homogenization uses the barrier at the normalized point plus a logarithmic scale term; self-concordance requires extra compatibility conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset E\) is convex with nonempty interior.
\(F\) is finite on \(\operatorname{int}C\) and diverges at \(\partial C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{\pi}_{\alpha}(x,t)=F(x/t)-\alpha\log t\) is the perspective-form candidate on \(C^{\pi}\), subject to separate convexity and self-concordance verification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is clearly labeled as a perspective-form candidate rather than an automatic self-concordant barrier, which is appropriate. Because the exact compatibility hypotheses and admissible parameter range are deliberately left unresolved and no source is cited, the record requires sourcing before review can establish the intended mathematical version.

children.title: Epigraph Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier families for epigraph-based convex representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Slack Does Not Automatically Preserve Self-Concordance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a smooth convex counterexample to unconditional self-concordance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=e^x\) and \(g(x,t)=-\log(t-e^x)\) on \(D=\{(x,t):t>e^x\}\). For fixed \(t>1\), the restriction to the \(x\)-line satisfies at \(x=0\) \[g''(0)=\frac{t}{(t-1)^2},\qquad g'''(0)=\frac{t(t+1)}{(t-1)^3},\qquad \frac{|g'''(0)|}{(g''(0))^{3/2}}=\frac{t+1}{\sqrt t}>2.\] Hence \(g\) violates the standard self-concordance inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the exponential epigraph, the bare logarithmic-slack function is not self-concordant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\log(t-e^x)\) is not a standard self-concordant function on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Slack Does Not Automatically Preserve Self-Concordance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the generic convex construction while separating barrier divergence and self-concordance requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be open and convex, let \(F\) be a convex barrier on \(C\), and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex. On \(D=\{(x,t):x\in C,\ t>f(x)\}\), define \[G(x,t)=F(x)-\log(t-f(x)).\] Then \(G\) is convex and diverges whenever \(t-f(x)\downarrow0\). Divergence along every approach to \(\partial D\) additionally requires control of simultaneous base-boundary approach and slack growth. Self-concordance is not implied by convexity of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative logarithm of epigraph slack gives a convex candidate, but full boundary divergence and self-concordance require additional hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is open and convex and \(F\) is a convex barrier on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) is convex and diverges as the epigraph slack tends to zero; no unconditional self-concordance conclusion follows.
knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic-Slack Epigraph Barrier Candidate
Epigraph Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic slack construction for the strict epigraph of a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex on an open convex set \(C\), and let \(F\) be a convex barrier for \(C\). On the strict epigraph
\[D=\{(x,t):x\in C,\ t>f(x)\},\]
the logarithmic-slack construction is
\[G(x,t)=F(x)-\log\bigl(t-f(x)\bigr).\]
The function \(G\) is convex and diverges when either \(x\) approaches the barrier boundary or \(t-f(x)\downarrow0\). Self-concordance of \(G\) is not automatic for an arbitrary convex \(f\); it requires derivative-control or compatibility assumptions relating \(f\) to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the negative logarithm of epigraph slack gives a convex boundary-divergent function, but self-concordance needs additional regularity conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is open and convex, and \(F\) is a convex barrier for \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,t)=F(x)-\log(t-f(x))\) is convex and boundary-divergent on \(D\), while self-concordance requires further hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic slack function is convex under the stated assumptions, and representation is a suitable content kind. The unqualified claim that it diverges whenever x approaches the base boundary does not control simultaneous growth of the slack, and the exact self-concordance conditions are unsourced.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted lifted barrier for the ℓp epigraph cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lifted logarithmic construction restricted by the auxiliary-variable hyperplane defining the norm epigraph representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and define \[\Psi_\alpha(\tau,x,z)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\left[\ln\!\left(\alpha(x^{(i)})^2\tau^{2(1-\alpha)}-(z^{(i)})^2\right)+\ln x^{(i)}+\ln\tau\right].\] Restricting \(\Psi_\alpha\) to \(\sum_{i=1}^n x^{(i)}=\tau\), with \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfying the lifted constraints defining \(\mathcal H_P\), gives a barrier for \(\mathcal H_P\) viewed in the variables \((\tau,z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For alpha strictly between zero and one, the displayed lifted logarithmic function yields a barrier for the ℓp epigraph cone after restriction to the auxiliary hyperplane sum x_i=tau and the lifted feasibility constraints.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ satisfies the lifted constraints defining }\mathcal H_P
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left.\Psi_\alpha(\tau,x,z)\right|_{\sum_i x^{(i)}=\tau}\text{ yields a barrier for }\mathcal H_P\text{ in }(\tau,z).

children.title: Projection Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limitations arising when lifted interiors are projected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Fibers Can Destroy the Marginal Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a minimal counterexample to unrestricted fiberwise barrier minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\mathbb R_+^2\), \(G(x,y)=-\log x-\log y\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^2\), and project onto \(C=\mathbb R_+\). For every \(x>0\), \[\inf_{y>0}G(x,y)=-\log x+\inf_{y>0}(-\log y)=-\infty.\] Thus a self-concordant lifted barrier can have an identically \(-\infty\) marginal on the interior of its projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the standard two-dimensional orthant barrier over an unbounded auxiliary coordinate produces minus infinity, not a projected barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=\inf_{y>0}G(x,y)=-\infty\) for every \(x>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Fibers Can Destroy the Marginal Barrier

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary Conditions for Fiberwise Barrier Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the local limitations of obtaining a projected barrier by minimizing over lift fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\) and \[F(x)=\inf\{G(x,y):(x,y)\in\operatorname{int}Q\}.\] Projection alone does not preserve barrier structure. A finite differentiable marginal requires suitable fiberwise finiteness, attainment, interior minimizers, and nondegeneracy. If the infimum is \(-\infty\) or unattained, or minimizing lifts escape to infinity or approach \(\partial Q\) while \(x\) remains controlled, then finiteness, differentiability, boundary divergence, or self-concordance may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovering a barrier by minimizing a lifted barrier over fibers requires additional attainment and regularity conditions; projection alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset E\times Y\) is convex with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of fiberwise finiteness, interior attainment, or nondegeneracy can prevent \(F\) from being a self-concordant barrier on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Necessary Conditions for Fiberwise Barrier Recovery
Projection Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of recovering a barrier by minimizing a lifted barrier over projection fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\) and consider the marginal candidate
\[F(x)=\inf\{G(x,y):(x,y)\in\operatorname{int}Q\}.\]
Recovering a differentiable barrier on \(C\) requires, at minimum, finite attained fiber minima, interior minimizers, and sufficient nondegeneracy to control their variation. If the infimum is unattained or equals \(-\infty\), then \(F\) is not a finite barrier. If minimizing lifts can approach \(\partial Q\) or escape to infinity while \(x\) remains controlled, differentiability, boundary divergence, or self-concordance may fail. Projection alone therefore does not preserve barrier structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fiberwise minimization yields a projected barrier only under attainment, interiority, finiteness, and nondegeneracy; projection by itself preserves none of these.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset E\times Y\) is convex with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of finite interior attainment or fiber nondegeneracy can prevent \(F(x)=\inf_yG(x,y)\) from being a self-concordant barrier for \(C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately describes a failure boundary, but its asserted minimum requirements and listed failure modes depend on a precise partial-minimization theorem. No theorem locator or sourced counterexamples are provided, so the mathematical scope cannot be certified.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical barriers for semidefinite, Lorentz, and product cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the canonical barriers and assigned parameters for positive-semidefinite and Lorentz cones, together with the additive construction for their direct products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf K=\mathbf S_+^{k_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbf S_+^{k_p}\times\mathbf L^{k_{p+1}}\times\cdots\times\mathbf L^{k_m}\). The canonical barrier for \(\mathbf S_+^k\) is \(S_k(X)=-\ln\det X\) on \(\operatorname{int}\mathbf S_+^k\), with \(\theta(S_k)=k\). For \(\mathbf L^k=\{x\in\mathbb R^k:x_k\geq(\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}x_j^2)^{1/2}\}\), the canonical barrier is \(L_k(x)=-\ln(x_k^2-\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}x_j^2)=-\ln(x^TJ_kx)\) on \(\operatorname{int}\mathbf L^k\), where \(J_k=\operatorname{diag}(-1,\ldots,-1,1)\), with \(\theta(L_k)=2\). The canonical barrier of \(\mathbf K\) is the direct sum \(K(X)=\sum_{i=1}^pS_{k_i}(X_i)+\sum_{i=p+1}^mL_{k_i}(X_i)\), and its parameter is \(\theta(K)=\sum_{i=1}^pk_i+2(m-p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-semidefinite cone has the negative log-determinant canonical barrier with parameter equal to the matrix size. The Lorentz cone has the negative logarithm of its defining quadratic form as canonical barrier, with parameter two. For a direct product of these cones, both the barrier and its parameter are obtained by summing those of the factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K(X)=\sum_{i=1}^p-\ln\det X_i-\sum_{i=p+1}^m\ln(X_i^TJ_{k_i}X_i),\qquad \theta(K)=\sum_{i=1}^pk_i+2(m-p)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter-two logarithmic barrier for the two-dimensional Lorentz cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical cone-barrier formula. Its finite domain is the interior \(y>|z|\) of the closed cone \(Q_2\), not the boundary of \(Q_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Q_2=\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^2:y\geq |z|\}.
\]
On
\[
\operatorname{int}Q_2=\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^2:y>|z|\},
\]
define
\[
\Phi(y,z)=-\ln(y^2-z^2).
\]
Then \(\Phi\) is a self-concordant barrier for \(Q_2\) with parameter \(\mu=2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the interior y greater than the absolute value of z of the two-dimensional Lorentz cone, minus the logarithm of y squared minus z squared is a self-concordant barrier with parameter two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(y,z)=-\ln(y^2-z^2)\text{ is a self-concordant barrier for }Q_2\text{ with parameter }\mu=2.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative-Orthant Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical logarithmically homogeneous barrier for the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the cone \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\) with interior \(\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), the canonical logarithmic barrier is
\[F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i.\]
It has \(\nabla^2F(x)=\operatorname{Diag}(x_1^{-2},\ldots,x_n^{-2})\succ0\), diverges when any coordinate tends to zero, and satisfies \(F(tx)=F(x)-n\log t\) for \(t>0\). Under the standard convention, \(F\) is an \(n\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative sum of coordinate logarithms is the canonical orthant barrier and has logarithmic-homogeneity degree and barrier parameter equal to the dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) is an \(n\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the extended-real barrier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit Fenchel dual of the canonical orthant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fenchel conjugate of \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\) is \(F^*(y)=\sup_{x>0}\{y^{\mathsf T}x-F(x)\}=-n-\sum_i\log(-y_i)\) for \(y\in\mathbb R_{--}^n\), and is \(+\infty\) otherwise. The maximizing point is \(x=-y^{-1}\), so \(\nabla F(x)=-x^{-1}\) maps \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\) bijectively onto \(\mathbb R_{--}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Up to the constant minus n, the conjugate is the same logarithmic barrier on the negative orthant.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_A(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(a_i^{\mathsf T}x)\) is an \(m\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic barrier induced by a strict homogeneous inequality representation.

source_refs.source_title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\]
be full-dimensional, and assume \(\operatorname{span}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}=\mathbb{R}^n\). On \(\operatorname{int}K=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x>0\ \forall i\}\), define
\[F_A(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(a_i^{\mathsf T}x).\]
Then \(F_A\to+\infty\) at every boundary point, \(\nabla^2F_A(x)=\sum_i a_ia_i^{\mathsf T}/(a_i^{\mathsf T}x)^2\succ0\), and \(F_A(tx)=F_A(x)-m\log t\). It is an \(m\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing logarithms of positive inequality slacks yields an inequality-representation barrier whose parameter equals the number of listed inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Inequality Barriers

source_witnesses.source_title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_A=\Phi\circ A\), \(\nabla F_A=-A^{\mathsf T}(Ax)^{-1}\), and \(\nabla^2F_A=A^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Diag}((Ax)^{-2})A\).

notation.meaning: Componentwise reciprocal of the positive slack vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral inequality barriers as linear pullbacks of the canonical orthant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi(z)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log z_i\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^m\). Then \(\operatorname{int}K=\{x:Ax\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\}\) and \(F_A(x)=\Phi(Ax)\). Moreover, \(\nabla F_A(x)=-A^{\mathsf T}(Ax)^{-1}\) and \(\nabla^2F_A(x)=A^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Diag}((Ax)^{-2})A\). The pullback Hessian is positive definite exactly when \(\ker A=\{0\}\), equivalently when the row normals span \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral inequality barrier is the orthant barrier pulled back through the slack map, with gradient and Hessian obtained by the chain rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthant Pullback Formulation

source_refs.source_title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed polyhedral cone, duplicating or adding redundant valid inequalities changes the logarithmic barrier and its construction parameter. Already for \(K=\mathbb{R}_+\), the single inequality \(x\geq0\) gives \(F_1(x)=-\log x\) with parameter \(1\), whereas listing the same inequality \(r\) times gives
\[F_r(x)=-r\log x\]
with parameter \(r\). Both representations define exactly \(K\), but their gradients, Hessians, local norms, and least admissible barrier parameters differ. Removing duplicated inequalities therefore reduces the parameter of this inequality-barrier construction; more generally, redundant inequalities make the constructed barrier representation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant or duplicated inequalities leave a cone unchanged but alter its logarithmic barrier, curvature, local norm, and parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Cone Representation Dependence

source_witnesses.source_title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory

assumptions_latex: Each description contains exactly one defining inequality for every facet and contains no redundant row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two barriers differ only by an additive constant, so their derivatives, local norms, and construction parameters agree.

notation.meaning: Permutation matching the two facet lists.
Positive rescaling of a facet normal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance class of irredundant facet logarithmic barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two irredundant facet descriptions of the same full-dimensional polyhedral cone, the normals can be indexed so that \(\widetilde a_i=c_i a_{\pi(i)}\) with \(c_i>0\). Hence \(\widetilde F(x)=-\sum_i\log(\widetilde a_i^{\mathsf T}x)=F(x)-\sum_i\log c_i\). Positive row rescaling and reordering therefore preserve the gradient, Hessian, local norms, and construction parameter; substantive dependence arises from adding redundant or duplicated inequalities or otherwise changing the listed slack family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Irredundant facet descriptions give the same logarithmic barrier up to an additive constant, whereas redundant or duplicated rows create substantive representation dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Description Invariance

children.title: Facial Degeneracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Barrier behavior near lower-dimensional polyhedral faces.

assumptions_latex: For the face-limit assertion, \(K\) is full-dimensional, \(G\) is a proper face, and \(x_k\in\operatorname{int}K\) converges to \(\bar x\in\operatorname{relint}G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ambient inequality barrier diverges on approach to a proper face; when \(\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\), it must be replaced by a barrier on \(\operatorname{relint}K\) in the reduced space.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities vanishing identically on the face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of ambient polyhedral logarithmic barriers on proper faces and lower-dimensional cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(a_i^{\mathsf T}x)\) where all displayed slacks are positive, and let \(I(G)=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=0\text{ for every }x\in G\}\). If interior points \(x_k\) converge to \(\bar x\in\operatorname{relint}G\) for a proper face \(G\), at least one slack indexed by \(I(G)\) tends to zero and \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\). If \(K\) has empty interior in the ambient space, the ambient strict-slack domain is empty; implicit equalities must be separated and a barrier constructed on \(\operatorname{relint}K\) within \(\operatorname{span}K\) or the appropriate affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polyhedral logarithmic barrier diverges toward proper faces and has no ambient domain for a lower-dimensional cone; such a cone requires a relative-interior reduced-space barrier.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Facial Barrier Boundary
Facial Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an ambient polyhedral logarithmic barrier on lower-dimensional cones and proper faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^Tx\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and define \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(a_i^Tx)\) wherever every displayed slack is positive. For a proper face \(G\) of \(K\), let \(I(G)=\{i:a_i^Tx=0\text{ for all }x\in G\}\). If \(x_k\in\operatorname{int}K\) converges to \(\bar x\in\operatorname{relint}G\), then \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\). If \(\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\) in \(\mathbb R^n\), this ambient barrier has no domain; a barrier must instead be constructed on \(\operatorname{relint}K\) within \(\operatorname{span}K\), after representing implicit equalities separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithmic barrier diverges near every proper face and is undefined for a cone with empty ambient interior; lower-dimensional cones require a relative-interior formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a proper face reached from interior points of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\); if \(\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\), the ambient barrier formulation fails.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semi-invariance of the canonical Lorentz-cone barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical logarithmic barrier on the interior of the Lorentz cone under Lorentz transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf L_k\) denote the Lorentz cone and let \(J_k\) be its defining quadratic-form matrix. For \(x\in\operatorname{int}\mathbf L_k\), define \(\mathcal L_k(x)=-\ln(x^T J_kx)\). If \(L\) is a Lorentz transformation, then there exists a constant \(c(L)\), independent of \(x\), such that \(\mathcal L_k(Lx)=\mathcal L_k(x)+c(L)\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}\mathbf L_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a Lorentz transformation, the canonical logarithmic barrier of the Lorentz cone changes by an additive constant that depends on the transformation but not on the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c(L)\in\mathbb R\;\forall x\in\operatorname{int}\mathbf L_k:\quad \mathcal L_k(Lx)=\mathcal L_k(x)+c(L)

children.title: Lorentz-Cone Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier geometry for standard second-order cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Lorentz-Cone Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical logarithmically homogeneous barrier for the real Lorentz cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\ge 1\), the Lorentz cone is \(L_{d+1}=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d:t\ge\lVert x\rVert_2\}\), with interior characterized by \(t>\lVert x\rVert_2\). Its canonical barrier is \[F_L(t,x)=-\log\!\left(t^2-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\right).\] This function is a \(2\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier: it is convex and smooth on \(\operatorname{int}L_{d+1}\), diverges at the boundary, and satisfies \(F_L(\alpha t,\alpha x)=F_L(t,x)-2\log\alpha\) for every \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative logarithm of the Lorentz quadratic form is the canonical parameter-two barrier on the interior of a second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_L\) is a \(2\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(L_{d+1}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-dual interior map and Fenchel conjugate of the canonical Lorentz barrier.
