children.title: Central-Path Limit Points
children.top_down_role: Accumulation behavior of central trajectories near optimality.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual semidefinite programs are strictly feasible.
The displayed central-path points exist for every \(\mu>0\).
For some \(\mu_0>0\), the trajectory \(\{(X(\mu),y(\mu),S(\mu)):0<\mu\leq\mu_0\}\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point \((X^*,y^*,S^*)\) is primal-dual optimal and satisfies \(X^*S^*=0\); if it is unique, the path converges to it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit-point characterization for a bounded strictly feasible semidefinite primal-dual central path.

source_refs.locator: 5.5 Existence of the central path - a constructive proof p. 124

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a primal-dual semidefinite program with strictly feasible primal and dual points. For each \(\mu>0\), let \((X(\mu),y(\mu),S(\mu))\) be primal-dual feasible and satisfy
\[X(\mu)S(\mu)=\mu I,\qquad X(\mu)\succ0,\quad S(\mu)\succ0.\]
Assume that for some \(\mu_0>0\), the trajectory \(\{(X(\mu),y(\mu),S(\mu)):0<\mu\leq\mu_0\}\) is bounded. Every accumulation point \((X^*,y^*,S^*)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\) is primal-dual optimal and satisfies \(X^*S^*=0\). If the central path has a unique accumulation point, then the entire path converges to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every accumulation point of a bounded strictly feasible semidefinite central path is an optimal complementary primal-dual solution; if that accumulation point is unique, the path converges to it.
knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Limit Points

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X^*\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(\mathcal S^*\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) be the primal and dual optimal slack sets. If \(X^*\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal X^*)\) and \(S^*\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal S^*)\), then their minimal containing faces are
\[F_P=\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(X^*)\},\]
\[F_D=\{S\succeq0:\operatorname{range}(S)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(S^*)\}.\]
Hence the ranges, or equivalently the kernels, of relative-interior central-path limits identify the primal and dual optimal faces.

children.title: Limiting Analytic Centers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Analytic Center of an SDP Optimal Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition on the minimal PSD face containing a nonempty semidefinite optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X^*\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) be a nonempty convex optimal set and let \(F_P\) be its minimal containing PSD face. A relative analytic center is a maximizer, when one exists, of
\[\max_{X\in\mathcal X^*\cap\operatorname{ri}F_P}\log\det_{F_P}X,\]
where \(\det_{F_P}\) is the determinant on the supporting subspace of \(F_P\). When the maximizer is unique, it is the analytic center of \(\mathcal X^*\) relative to \(F_P\). The analogous definition applies to the dual optimal-slack set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative analytic center maximizes the restricted log determinant over the optimal set within its minimal PSD face.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X^*\) is a nonempty convex subset of \(\mathbb S_+^n\).
The determinant is restricted to the supporting subspace of the minimal containing face.
Existence and uniqueness are asserted only when the displayed maximization has a unique maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X^{\mathrm{ac}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{X\in\mathcal X^*\cap\operatorname{ri}F_P}\log\det_{F_P}X.

notation.meaning: minimal PSD face containing the primal optimal set
determinant on the supporting subspace of the face

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Analytic Center of an SDP Optimal Set
Limiting Analytic Centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analytic-center selection by the semidefinite central path on optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume a strictly feasible primal-dual semidefinite program has nonempty bounded optimal sets. Let \(F_P\) and \(F_D\) be their minimal containing faces, and define \(\det_{F_P}\) and \(\det_{F_D}\) as determinants restricted to the supporting subspaces of those faces. If the corresponding restricted log-determinant maximizers are unique, then the primal-dual central path converges as \(\mu\downarrow0\) to \((X^{\mathrm{ac}},S^{\mathrm{ac}})\), where
\[X^{\mathrm{ac}}=\arg\max_{X\in\mathcal X^*\cap\operatorname{ri}F_P}\log\det_{F_P}X,\qquad S^{\mathrm{ac}}=\arg\max_{S\in\mathcal S^*\cap\operatorname{ri}F_D}\log\det_{F_D}S.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under boundedness and uniqueness, the central path selects the relative analytic centers of the primal and dual optimal faces.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual semidefinite program is strictly feasible.
Both optimal sets are nonempty and bounded.
The restricted log-determinant maximizers are unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X(\mu)\to X^{\mathrm{ac}}\) and \(S(\mu)\to S^{\mathrm{ac}}\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: minimal primal and dual optimal faces
determinant restricted to the support of face \(F\)

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Complementarity Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-maximal complementarity of relative-interior semidefinite optimal limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X^*\) and \(\mathcal S^*\) be the primal and dual optimal slack sets of a semidefinite program. If a central-path limit satisfies \(X^*\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal X^*)\) and \(S^*\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal S^*)\), then
\[\operatorname{rank}X^*=\max_{X\in\mathcal X^*}\operatorname{rank}X,\qquad \operatorname{rank}S^*=\max_{S\in\mathcal S^*}\operatorname{rank}S.\]
Together with \(X^*S^*=0\), this makes \((X^*,S^*)\) maximally complementary. The stronger equality \(\operatorname{rank}X^*+\operatorname{rank}S^*=n\) requires strict complementarity and is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative-interior central-path limits have maximal primal and dual ranks; full rank-sum equality additionally requires strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*\) and \(S^*\) have maximal ranks within their respective optimal sets.

notation.meaning: primal and dual optimal slack sets

children.title: Nonconvergent Path Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degenerate settings with unstable or nonunique limiting behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvergent Path Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of central-path existence when bounded barrier subproblems are absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Boundedness or level-boundedness cannot be omitted from a general central-path convergence assertion. Consider
\[\inf\{x_1:x_1>0,\ x_2>0\}.\]
Its infimum is \(0\), and its optimal set in the closed cone is \(\{(0,x_2):x_2\geq0\}\). For every \(\mu>0\), the logarithmic-barrier objective
\[x_1-\mu\log x_1-\mu\log x_2\]
has no minimizer because it tends to \(-\infty\) as \(x_2\to\infty\). Hence no barrier central point exists, so convergence and limiting-face identification are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without level-bounded barrier subproblems, a conic problem may have optimal solutions while its logarithmic central path does not exist.
assumptions_latex: No constraint bounds the recession coordinate \(x_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The logarithmic-barrier subproblem has no minimizer for any \(\mu>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows nonexistence of barrier minimizers, but it has no citation and addresses failure of path existence rather than nonconvergence of an existing path. A source and clarification that this boundary includes nonexistence, or evidence for an actual nonconvergent path, are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Narrow Norm-Based Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong Frobenius-norm centrality region for semidefinite short-step methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0<\theta<1\), the narrow Frobenius neighborhood of the semidefinite central path is
\[\mathcal N_F(\theta)=\left\{(X,S):X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n},\ \left\|X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}-\mu I\right\|_F\leq\theta\mu,\ \mu=\frac{\langle X,S\rangle}{n}\right\}.\]
Membership implies
\[(1-\theta)\mu I\preceq X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}\preceq(1+\theta)\mu I,\]
so every complementarity eigenvalue remains uniformly close to \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A narrow neighborhood bounds the Frobenius centrality residual by θμ, thereby keeping every complementarity eigenvalue close to μ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((X,S)\in\mathcal N_F(\theta)\) implies \((1-\theta)\mu I\preceq X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}\preceq(1+\theta)\mu I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\mu^{-1}X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}\) and \(d_i=\lambda_i(W)-1\). Then \[\max_i|d_i|\leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^2\right)^{1/2}\leq\sqrt n\max_i|d_i|.\] Hence the spectral box \(\max_i|d_i|\leq\theta/\sqrt n\) is contained in \(\mathcal N_F(\theta)\), and \(\mathcal N_F(\theta)\) is contained in the box \(\max_i|d_i|\leq\theta\). The dimension factor is sharp: for even \(n\), the diagonal matrix having \(n/2\) eigenvalues \(1+a\) and \(n/2\) eigenvalues \(1-a\), where \(0<a<1\), has extremal deviation \(a\) and Frobenius deviation \(a\sqrt n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frobenius centrality lies between the largest spectral deviation and its square-root-dimension multiple, and a balanced diagonal family attains the dimension factor.

knowledge_statements.title: Wide Central Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided spectral neighborhood allowing nonuniform semidefinite complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constants \(0<\gamma\leq1\leq\Gamma\), define the wide two-sided central neighborhood by
\[\mathcal N_W(\gamma,\Gamma)=\left\{(X,S):X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n},\ \gamma\mu I\preceq X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}\preceq\Gamma\mu I,\ \mu=\frac{\langle X,S\rangle}{n}\right\}.\]
Equivalently, every eigenvalue of the symmetric complementarity product lies in \([\gamma\mu,\Gamma\mu]\). Unlike a narrow norm neighborhood, this condition permits order-one relative spectral dispersion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wide neighborhood keeps complementarity eigenvalues between fixed multiples of μ while allowing substantially nonuniform centrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma\mu\leq\lambda_i(X^{1/2}SX^{1/2})\leq\Gamma\mu\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Central Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-spectral centrality neighborhood used in wide-neighborhood analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0<\gamma<1\), define the one-sided semidefinite central neighborhood by
\[\mathcal N^-(\gamma)=\left\{(X,S):X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n},\ X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}\succeq\gamma\mu I,\ \mu=\frac{\langle X,S\rangle}{n}\right\}.\]
Equivalently, \(\lambda_{\min}(X^{1/2}SX^{1/2})\geq\gamma\mu\). No individual upper spectral bound is imposed; only the trace identity \(\sum_i\lambda_i=n\mu\) limits large eigenvalues collectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-sided neighborhood prevents complementarity eigenvalues from becoming too small but imposes no separate upper bound on each eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((X,S)\in\mathcal N^-(\gamma)\iff\lambda_{\min}(X^{1/2}SX^{1/2})\geq\gamma\mu\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(W)\geq\gamma\Longrightarrow\lambda_{\max}(W)\leq n-(n-1)\gamma\), and the constant is sharp.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp individual upper eigenvalue bound induced by the one-sided lower bound and complementarity trace identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\mu^{-1}X^{1/2}SX^{1/2}\), so \(\operatorname{tr}W=n\). If \(W\succeq\gamma I\), then \[\lambda_{\max}(W)\leq n-(n-1)\gamma.\] This is sharp: \(W=\operatorname{diag}(n-(n-1)\gamma,\gamma,\ldots,\gamma)\) is positive definite, has trace \(n\), and attains equality. Thus the one-sided definition chooses no upper threshold, although normalization forces this dimension-dependent envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower threshold and fixed trace impose a sharp dimension-dependent upper envelope, attained by concentrating the remaining trace in one eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Trace-Induced Upper Envelope

knowledge_statements.title: Wide-Neighborhood Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible Newton stepping with neighborhood-preserving backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a feasible \((X_k,y_k,S_k)\in\mathcal N_W(\gamma,\Gamma)\), a target factor \(0<\sigma_k<1\), and a reduction constant \(0<\eta<1\). Set \(\mu_k=\langle X_k,S_k\rangle/n\), and compute a primal-dual Newton direction for the feasibility equations and the centered complementarity target \(\sigma_k\mu_k I\). Choose the largest \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) such that
\[X_k+\alpha_k\Delta X_k\succ0,\quad S_k+\alpha_k\Delta S_k\succ0,\quad (X_{k+1},S_{k+1})\in\mathcal N_W(\gamma,\Gamma),\]
and \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-\eta\alpha_k)\mu_k\). Update all variables and stop when \(n\mu_k\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a centered feasible Newton direction, backtrack to retain positivity and the wide neighborhood, and stop when the duality gap reaches ε.
assumptions_latex: The current iterate is primal-dual feasible and belongs to \(\mathcal N_W(\gamma,\Gamma)\).
The Newton system has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate remains feasible and neighborhood-contained, with \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-\eta\alpha_k)\mu_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mehrotra Predictor–Corrector Iteration for a Semidefinite–Quadratic–Linear Cone Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One primal–dual interior-point iteration for a product of semidefinite, quadratic, and nonnegative-orthant cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an approximate primal-dual point $(y,F,f,f^{(0)},Z,z,z^{(0)})$ and residual mapping $H$, compute a predictor direction from $J\Delta=-H$ with $\mu=0$, where $J=DH$ and $(A*B)\operatorname{svec}X=\tfrac12\operatorname{svec}(AXB+BXA)$. Compute separate primal and dual maximal boundary steps $\alpha^{\rm pred},\beta^{\rm pred}$ using, respectively, a block-symmetric eigenvalue calculation for the semidefinite cone, quadratic equations for the quadratic cones, and ratio tests for the positive orthant. With the resulting boundary points, set
\[
\mu=\frac{\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}(Z^{\rm pred}F^{\rm pred})+(z^{\rm pred})^Tf^{\rm pred}+((z^{(0)})^{\rm pred})^T(f^{(0)})^{\rm pred}\bigr)^3}{\nu\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}(ZF)+z^Tf+(z^{(0)})^Tf^{(0)}\bigr)^2},\qquad \nu=\sum_{k=1}^M n_k+\sum_{k=1}^L(p_k+1)+p_0.
\]
Re-solve the Newton system after replacing its complementarity residuals by the $\mu$-relaxed semidefinite, quadratic-cone, and orthant complementarity equations augmented with predictor-product second-order corrections. Finally, choose separate corrector step lengths
\[
\alpha,\beta\leq \min\{1,\tau\,\alpha_{\max}\},\ \min\{1,\tau\,\beta_{\max}\},\qquad 0<\tau<1,
\]
and update the primal and dual variables. The new iterate remains in the cone interiors; a unit primal or dual step also preserves the corresponding equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: From an approximate primal-dual point, solve the Newton equations with zero centering to obtain a predictor direction. Determine separate primal and dual distances to the boundary of each cone, use the predicted boundary points in Mehrotra’s centering formula, add the predictor-product second-order corrections, and solve again for a corrector direction. Update with separate steps bounded by one and by a fixed fraction of the corresponding cone-boundary distance. These steps preserve the cone inequalities, and a unit step preserves the relevant primal or dual equalities.
assumptions_latex: J=DH\text{ is the Newton-system Jacobian at the current approximate primal-dual point}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The predictor-corrector update satisfies the cone inequalities; if }\alpha=1\text{ or }\beta=1,\text{ it also satisfies the corresponding primal or dual equality constraints.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative boundary and first exit for a spectral-radius relaxed central neighborhood on a symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal N_\theta:=\{z\in\operatorname{int}K:\rho(z-e)\leq\theta\}\). Its boundary relative to \(\operatorname{int}K\) is \[\{z\in\operatorname{int}K:\rho(z-e)=\theta\}.\] For a continuous trial curve \(z:[0,\bar\alpha]\to\operatorname{int}K\) starting in \(\mathcal N_\theta\), let \[\alpha_*:=\sup\{a\in[0,\bar\alpha]:z(t)\in\mathcal N_\theta\text{ for every }t\in[0,a]\}.\] If \(\alpha_*<\bar\alpha\), then \(\rho(z(\alpha_*)-e)=\theta\). Any trial point satisfying \(\rho(z(\alpha)-e)>\theta\) is outside the neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the relaxed central neighborhood by \(\mathcal N_\theta=\{z\in\operatorname{int}K:\rho(z-e)\leq\theta\}\). Its relative boundary is \(\partial_K\mathcal N_\theta=\{z\in\operatorname{int}K:\rho(z-e)=\theta\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\mathcal N_F^J(\theta):=\{z\in\operatorname{int}K:\|z-e\|_{J,F}\leq\theta\},\qquad \|u\|_{J,F}^2:=\operatorname{tr}(u\circ u).\] If \(z=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i(z)c_i\) is a Jordan spectral decomposition, then \[\|z-e\|_{J,F}^2=\sum_{i=1}^r(\lambda_i(z)-1)^2.\] Consequently the neighborhood is independent of the Jordan frame used to represent \(z\).

children.title: Spectral Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Loss of neighborhood membership through exceptional eigenvalue behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with identity \(e\), symmetric cone \(K\), and spectral radius \(\rho\).
The inequality \(\rho(z-e)\leq\theta\) is evaluated for \(z\in V\); cone membership is not assumed when \(\theta>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta<1\) implies \(z\in\operatorname{int}K\); \(\theta=1\) permits \(z\in\partial K\); and \(\theta>1\) does not imply \(z\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp interiority threshold for an ambient spectral-radius test around the Jordan identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho(z-e)\leq\theta<1\), then every Jordan eigenvalue of \(z\) lies in \([1-\theta,1+\theta]\), so \(\lambda_{\min}(z)>0\), \(z\in\operatorname{int}K\), and \(z\) is invertible. The threshold is sharp: for a primitive idempotent \(c\), \(z=e-c\) satisfies \(\rho(z-e)=1\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(z)=0\), hence \(z\in\partial K\). For every \(\theta>1\), choosing \(0<\varepsilon<\theta-1\) and \(z=e-(1+\varepsilon)c\) gives \(\rho(z-e)=1+\varepsilon<\theta\) but a negative eigenvalue, so the ambient radius inequality alone does not imply \(z\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius below one guarantees interiority; radius one permits singularity, and above one the ambient spectral test no longer guarantees cone membership.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Spectral Interiority Threshold

assumptions_latex: \(z\) lies in the closure of a rank-\(r\) symmetric cone and is normalized so that exact centrality is \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\theta<1\) the neighborhood stays interior; at \(\theta=1\), singular scaled complementarity can enter its closure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp interiority threshold for two-sided spectral neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho(z-e)\leq\theta<1\), then \(\lambda_{\min}(z)\geq1-\theta>0\), so \(z\in\operatorname{int}K\) and its inverse exists. The threshold \(\theta=1\) is sharp: for any primitive idempotent \(c\), the element \(z=e-c\) satisfies \(\rho(z-e)=1\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(z)=0\), hence \(z\in\partial K\). For \(\theta>1\), the spectral-radius inequality alone does not imply membership in \(K\), because a permitted eigenvalue may be negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius below one guarantees interiority; at radius one singular complementarity appears, and above one the spectral bound no longer ensures cone membership.

children.title: Unsymmetrized Primal-Dual Directions
children.top_down_role: Direct complementarity linearizations without symmetric scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsymmetrized Primal-Dual Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Raw matrix-product Newton direction for semidefinite complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((X,S)\), choose \(\sigma\in[0,1]\) and solve the primal and dual feasibility linearizations together with the unsymmetrized complementarity equation \[\Delta X S+X\Delta S=\sigma\mu I-XS.\] If a solution exists, choose the largest prescribed fraction-to-boundary step \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) for which \(X+\alpha\Delta X\succ0\) and \(S+\alpha\Delta S\succ0\), then output \((X^+,S^+)=(X+\alpha\Delta X,S+\alpha\Delta S)\). Stop when the selected feasibility residuals and \(\mu\) meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The raw primal-dual direction Newton-linearizes the nonsymmetric matrix equation XS equals sigma mu times the identity, then takes a positivity-preserving step.
assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) are primal-dual semidefinite iterates satisfying their current linear constraints.
The centering parameter is \(\sigma\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu:=\langle X,S\rangle/n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direction is obtained by solving feasibility linearizations together with \(\Delta X S+X\Delta S=\sigma\mu I-XS\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Residual After the Raw Newton Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order remainder of the unsymmetrized complementarity linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Delta XS+X\Delta S=\sigma\mu I-XS\), then the full raw Newton update satisfies \[(X+\Delta X)(S+\Delta S)-\sigma\mu I=\Delta X\Delta S.\] More generally, for a step \(\alpha\), \[(X+\alpha\Delta X)(S+\alpha\Delta S)=(1-\alpha)XS+\alpha\sigma\mu I+\alpha^2\Delta X\Delta S.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The raw Newton equation cancels the first-order complementarity residual, leaving the product of the increments as the full-step remainder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (X+\Delta X)(S+\Delta S)-\sigma\mu I=\Delta X\Delta S.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Residual After the Raw Newton Update

children.title: Matrix Symmetrization Operator Families
children.top_down_role: Operator choices for semidefinite complementarity linearization.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Symmetrization Operator Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monteiro-Zhang-type symmetrization family for semidefinite complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonsingular \(P\), define \[H_P(M):=\tfrac12\left(PMP^{-1}+P^{-T}M^TP^T\right)=\operatorname{sym}(PMP^{-1}).\] For primal-dual matrices \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), symmetric increments \(\Delta X,\Delta S\in\mathbb S^n\), centering parameter \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), and average complementarity \(\mu:=\langle X,S\rangle/n\), the associated symmetrized complementarity equation is \[H_P(\Delta X S+X\Delta S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS).\] Its two sides lie in \(\mathbb S^n\). Different admissible choices of \(P\), including identity, primal, dual, and common-metric scalings, generate a family of primal-dual directions while retaining the same primal and dual feasibility linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugating a matrix product and averaging it with its transpose produces a symmetric complementarity equation; varying the conjugating matrix yields different direction families.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), and \(\Delta X,\Delta S\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_P(M)\in\mathbb S^n\), and applying \(H_P\) to the complementarity linearization yields a symmetric Newton equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range and Kernel of Matrix Symmetrization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic range, kernel, and information loss of the Monteiro–Zhang symmetrization operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(P\), the map \(H_P(M)=\operatorname{sym}(PMP^{-1})\) is a surjective linear map from \(\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) onto \(\mathbb S^n\). Its kernel is \[\ker H_P=\{P^{-1}KP:K^T=-K\}.\] Therefore \(H_P(M)=H_P(N)\) exactly when \(P(M-N)P^{-1}\) is skew-symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The operator retains the symmetric part in transformed coordinates and discards exactly the transformed skew-symmetric part.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{range}(H_P)=\mathbb S^n,\qquad\ker H_P=P^{-1}\mathbb K^nP,\quad\mathbb K^n:=\{K:K^T=-K\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Range and Kernel of Matrix Symmetrization

children.title: Primal Variable Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaled coordinate systems for primal cone variables.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) is an invertible scaling matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal common-metric coordinate is \(\bar X=W^{-1}XW^{-1}\), with inverse reconstruction \(X=W\bar XW\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence representation of the primal semidefinite variable in a common metric.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal variable is represented in the metric determined by \(W\) as \[\bar X:=W^{-1}XW^{-1}.\] This congruence is bijective on \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\), with inverse \(X=W\bar XW\), and it preserves positive definiteness. A primal increment is transported by the same linear congruence, \(\Delta\bar X=W^{-1}\Delta XW^{-1}\), when \(W\) is held fixed during the Newton linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite scaling maps the primal matrix and its Newton increment into common-metric coordinates by inverse congruence.

children.title: Common-Space Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Representations placing primal-dual quantities in a shared metric space.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Space Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesterov-Todd-type common coordinate for positive-definite primal-dual matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(W^{-1}XW^{-1}=WSW\), define the common-space representative \[D:=W^{-1}XW^{-1}=WSW.\] The original variables are recovered by \(X=WDW\) and \(S=W^{-1}DW^{-1}\). Cyclicity of trace gives \(\langle X,S\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(D^2)\). With \(\mu:=\langle X,S\rangle/n\), exact centrality \(XS=\mu I\) corresponds to \(D=\sqrt\mu I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suitable scaling embeds primal and dual matrices as the same positive-definite representative, whose squared trace equals their complementarity gap.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) satisfies the common-metric scaling equation \(W^{-1}XW^{-1}=WSW\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both variables embed as one matrix \(D=W^{-1}XW^{-1}=WSW\), and \(\langle X,S\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(D^2)\).

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and explicit construction of the common-metric scaling for a positive-definite primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), the equation \(QSQ=X\) has the unique positive-definite solution \[Q=S^{-1/2}(S^{1/2}XS^{1/2})^{1/2}S^{-1/2}.\] Consequently, \(W:=Q^{1/2}\) is the unique \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) satisfying \(W^{-1}XW^{-1}=WSW\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every positive-definite primal-dual matrix pair has a unique positive-definite common-metric scaling in the stated orientation.
assumptions_latex: Matrix square roots denote the unique positive-definite square roots.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!\,W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n:\ W^{-1}XW^{-1}=WSW.\)

notation.meaning: square of the common-metric scaling matrix

children.title: Coordinate Equivalence Classes
children.top_down_role: Relationships among scaled representations preserving the same direction geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Equivalence Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal equivalence of common-metric matrix coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D,\widetilde D\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), define \(D\sim\widetilde D\) when there exists an orthogonal matrix \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) such that \(\widetilde D=U^TDU\). This is an equivalence relation. For every \(\mu>0\), equivalent representatives have the same eigenvalues and satisfy \[\|\widetilde D-\sqrt\mu I\|_F=\|D-\sqrt\mu I\|_F,\qquad \rho(\widetilde D/\sqrt\mu-I)=\rho(D/\sqrt\mu-I).\] Thus spectral and Frobenius central-neighborhood membership depends only on the equivalence class \([D]\), not on the selected orthonormal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common-coordinate matrices related by orthogonal similarity form an equivalence class and have identical spectral and Frobenius centrality measures.
assumptions_latex: \(D,\widetilde D\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) are positive-definite common-coordinate representatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orthogonal changes \(\widetilde D=U^TDU\) preserve eigenvalue-based and Frobenius centrality measures.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of positive-definite common-coordinate representatives under orthogonal similarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D,\widetilde D\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), there exists an orthogonal matrix \(U\) such that \(\widetilde D=U^TDU\) if and only if \(D\) and \(\widetilde D\) have the same eigenvalues with multiplicity. Thus each orthogonal-similarity class is determined uniquely by its unordered positive eigenvalue multiset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two positive-definite common-coordinate matrices are orthogonally equivalent exactly when their eigenvalue multisets agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\sim\widetilde D\iff\operatorname{spec}(D)=\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde D)\text{ with multiplicity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Classification of Coordinate Classes

children.title: Scaling Singularity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation breakdown near singular scaling maps.

assumptions_latex: \(X,S\) range over positive semidefinite matrices approaching the boundary of their cones.
\(W\) is required to be positive definite and to define both primal and dual congruence coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(X\) or \(S\) becomes singular, no invertible common scaling can represent it by a positive-definite common matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of invertible common coordinates at the semidefinite cone boundary.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The congruence coordinates \(\bar X=W^{-1}XW^{-1}\) and \(\bar S=WSW\) require an invertible \(W\). If a sequence has \(\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\to0\) or \(\lambda_{\min}(S_k)\to0\), any limiting representation with a positive-definite common matrix cannot retain both an invertible scaling and an invertible inverse scaling. At a singular limit, the common-coordinate bijection on \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\) therefore fails; before the limit, growth of \(\kappa_2(W_k)\) signals numerical ill-conditioning of at least one coordinate transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common-metric coordinates require invertibility; approaching singular primal or dual matrices destroys the positive-definite common representation and can make the scaling ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Singularity Boundaries

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Condition Number Does Not Prevent Scaling Blow-Up
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample separating absolute scale magnitude from spectral condition number near the cone boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t=t\) and \(S_t=1\) for \(t>0\) in the one-dimensional positive-semidefinite cone. The common scaling is \(W_t=t^{1/4}\), and \[W_t^{-1}X_tW_t^{-1}=W_tS_tW_t=\sqrt t.\] Although \(\kappa_2(W_t)=1\) for every \(t\), \(\|W_t^{-1}\|_2=t^{-1/4}\to\infty\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar common scaling can have condition number one while its inverse diverges near the cone boundary, so condition number alone does not detect every singular limit.
assumptions_latex: The one-dimensional positive-semidefinite cone is identified with \(\mathbb R_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(W_t)=1\quad\text{and}\quad\|W_t^{-1}\|_2\to\infty\text{ as }t\downarrow0.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Condition Number Does Not Prevent Scaling Blow-Up

children.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Invariance
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria governing symmetric primal-dual representations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 9.6 Scaling, Primal-Dual Symmetry, and Scale Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines symmetry jointly through duality interchange and equivariance under cone automorphisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-dual algorithm \(PDA\) is symmetric if, for every input \((\mathcal L,b,c,x^0,s^0;K,K^*)\), it satisfies both: (i) \(\{(x^k,s^k)\}=PDA(\mathcal L,b,c,x^0,s^0;K,K^*)\) if and only if \(\{(s^k,x^k)\}=PDA(\mathcal L^\perp,c,b,s^0,x^0;K^*,K)\); and (ii), for every \(T\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\), the first sequence is produced if and only if \(\{(T(x^k),T^{-*}(s^k))\}=PDA(T(\mathcal L),T(b),T^{-*}(c),T(x^0),T^{-*}(s^0);K,K^*)\). The corresponding dual form of (ii) is also required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual algorithm is symmetric when swapping the primal and dual problems swaps its iterate sequences, and applying any cone automorphism to the input applies the associated primal and inverse-adjoint transformations to every iterate; the dual scaling statement must also hold.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal L,b,c,x^0,s^0;K,K^*)\text{ is any valid primal-dual input}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PDA\text{ is symmetric exactly when it is equivariant under primal-dual interchange and under }(x,s)\mapsto(Tx,T^{-*}s),\text{ including the dual counterpart.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classification of Nonsingular Linear Rank Preservers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general linear-preserver theorem for the full real matrix space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonsingular linear transformation \(T:\mathbb R^{n\times n}\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) preserves rank if and only if either \(T(X)=UXV\) for all \(X\), or \(T(X)=UX^TV\) for all \(X\), for some nonsingular matrices \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible linear map on real square matrices preserves rank exactly when it is multiplication on the left and right by invertible matrices, possibly after transposition.
assumptions_latex: T:\mathbb R^{n\times n}\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ is a nonsingular linear transformation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\operatorname{rank}T(X)=\operatorname{rank}X\ \forall X\bigr)\iff \left[\exists U,V\text{ nonsingular}:T(X)=UXV\ \forall X\right]\lor\left[\exists U,V\text{ nonsingular}:T(X)=UX^TV\ \forall X\right].

children.title: Primal-Dual Scaling-Point Geometry
children.top_down_role: Common-metric scaling points and primal-dual interchange.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\), unit \(e\), and quadratic representation \(P\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic representation of the Euclidean Jordan algebra.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-cone formulation using the quadratic representation and self-dual identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x,s\in\operatorname{int}K\), a primal-dual scaling point is an element \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(P(w)s=x\). Its associated common-metric representative is
\[
v:=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\in\operatorname{int}K.
\]
Thus the primal point is transported by \(P(w^{-1/2})\), the dual slack by the inverse-adjoint scaling \(P(w^{1/2})\), and both images coincide. Under primal-dual interchange \((x,s)\mapsto(s,x)\), the scaling point becomes \(w^{-1}\), while the common representative \(v\) is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaling point defines reciprocal primal and dual metric transformations that send an interior primal-dual pair to the same interior point.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Scaling-Point Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but no cited source with an inspectable locator supports the scaling identity, common point, or interchange claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a common self-adjoint scaling that identifies each interior primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conic convex problem over \(K\) admits a symmetric \(v\Leftrightarrow\)-space construction if there exists \(G\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) such that, for every \((x,s)\in\operatorname{int}(K)\oplus\operatorname{int}(K^*)\), the equation \(T(x)=T^{-*}(s)\), \(T\in G\), has a unique self-adjoint solution \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic problem admits a symmetric scaling-space construction when some family of cone automorphisms contains, for every interior primal-dual pair, exactly one self-adjoint scaling that maps the primal point to the inverse-adjoint image of the dual point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(x,s)\in\operatorname{int}(K)\oplus\operatorname{int}(K^*)\ \exists!\,T\in G:\ T=T^*\text{ and }T(x)=T^{-*}(s).

children.title: V-Space Scaling Frameworks
children.top_down_role: Abstract common-space representations of scaled complementarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-space representation of symmetric-cone points, directions, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\), and let \(x,s,w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfy \(P(w)s=x\). Define
\[v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s,\qquad d_x=P(w^{-1/2})\Delta x,\qquad d_s=P(w^{1/2})\Delta s.\]
Then
\[\Delta x=P(w^{1/2})d_x,\qquad \Delta s=P(w^{-1/2})d_s,\qquad \langle x,s\rangle=\langle v,v\rangle.\]
Thus primal and dual complementarity equations can be represented in one Jordan algebra using the common point \(v\) and the common-space directions \(d_x,d_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaling point maps primal and dual variables and directions into one Jordan algebra, preserving complementarity as the squared norm of their common representative.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s,\quad \langle x,s\rangle=\|v\|^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Common V-Space Coordinates and Pairing

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled variables satisfy \(v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\), with directions represented in the same space by \(d_x\) and \(d_s\).

notation.meaning: Scaled primal and dual direction components.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard V-space formulation of symmetric-cone primal-dual scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-space representation for points and tangent directions on a symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The scaling point \(w\) defines a common vector space, or V-space, by
\[
v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s,
\qquad d_x=P(w^{-1/2})\Delta x,
\qquad d_s=P(w^{1/2})\Delta s.
\]
The inverse transformations are \(\Delta x=P(w^{1/2})d_x\) and \(\Delta s=P(w^{-1/2})d_s\). Consequently, a scaled complementarity equation can be posed entirely in \(V\), for example as \(L_v(d_x+d_s)=r_c\), where \(L_vz=v\circ z\) and \(r_c\in V\) is the prescribed complementarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: V-space scaling maps primal and dual points and directions into one Jordan algebra, where scaled complementarity is expressed with a common multiplication operator.
knowledge_statements.title: V-Space Scaling Frameworks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-space representation fits the container, but the particular scaled complementarity equation and inverse transformations require a direct source with a specific locator.

children.title: Primal-Dual Symmetry Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria for interchangeable primal-dual representations.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-dual interchange sends \((x,s,w)\) to \((s,x,w^{-1})\) and preserves the common scaled point.

notation.meaning: Scaling point for the primal-dual pair.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic symmetry criterion for self-dual symmetric-cone scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic criterion for exact primal-dual symmetry in common scaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scaling construction is primal-dual symmetric when the interchange
\[
\mathcal I(x,s,w,\Delta x,\Delta s)
=(s,x,w^{-1},\Delta s,\Delta x)
\]
preserves its common-coordinate equations. Equivalently, its point scaling must satisfy
\[
P(w)s=x,
\qquad P(w^{-1})x=s,
\qquad P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s=v,
\]
and its direction equations must be invariant under \((d_x,d_s)\mapsto(d_s,d_x)\). Any residual rule used in those equations must depend on \(x\) and \(s\) only through symmetric common-space quantities such as \(v\), \(v\circ v\), and the duality product \(\langle x,s\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact primal-dual symmetry requires inversion of the scaling point, interchange of scaled direction components, and unchanged common-space residual equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Symmetry Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic identities alone are not equivalent to invariance of all direction and residual equations. A direct source is needed to state sufficient symmetry criteria and delimit the admissible residual rules reliably.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An equivalence between existence of the symmetric scaling construction and homogeneous self-dual cone geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conic convex optimization problem over \(K\) admits a symmetric \(v\Leftrightarrow\)-space construction if and only if \(K\) is a homogeneous self-dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic convex problem has a symmetric scaling-space construction exactly when its cone is homogeneous and self-dual.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is the cone of a conic convex optimization problem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(K\text{ admits a symmetric }v\Leftrightarrow\text{-space construction}\bigr)\iff\bigl(K\text{ is homogeneous and self-dual}\bigr).

children.title: Scale-Invariant Direction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Direction properties preserved under compatible variable rescaling.

assumptions_latex: \((\Delta x,\Delta s)\) is represented by \(d_x=P(w^{-1/2})\Delta x\) and \(d_s=P(w^{1/2})\Delta s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The common-metric squared length is \(\|d_x\|^2+\|d_s\|^2\) and is unchanged by reciprocal primal-dual rescaling.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: common-metric invariance of scaled symmetric-cone directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction geometry induced by reciprocal quadratic-representation scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the common-metric norm of a primal-dual direction by
\[
\|(\Delta x,\Delta s)\|_w^2
:=\langle\Delta x,P(w^{-1})\Delta x\rangle
+\langle\Delta s,P(w)\Delta s\rangle
=\|d_x\|^2+\|d_s\|^2.
\]
If the pair is represented using reciprocal primal and dual scalings that yield the same common coordinates, then \((d_x,d_s)\) and hence this norm are unchanged. In particular, primal-dual interchange replaces \(w\) by \(w^{-1}\) and exchanges the two summands without altering the direction length or angles computed in the common space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After reciprocal scaling, direction lengths and angles are computed in one Euclidean metric and remain unchanged under primal-dual interchange.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Invariant Direction Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed norm is plausible, but the broader claim of invariance under reciprocal rescaling is not precisely parameterized or supported by a cited source. The primal-dual interchange case should be distinguished from arbitrary rescaling.

children.title: Symmetry Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cone or barrier regimes lacking fully symmetric primal-dual scaling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of standard self-duality outside the Lorentz norm cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge2\), \(1<p<\infty\), and \(p^{-1}+q^{-1}=1\), define \(K_p=\{(t,z):t\ge\|z\|_p\}\). Under the standard Euclidean pairing, \(K_p^*=K_q\). Thus \(p\ne2\) gives \(K_p\ne K_p^*\), so the standard-pairing Lorentz-cone identification and its canonical Jordan scaling formulas cannot be transferred unchanged to \(K_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-Euclidean p-norm cone is dual to the q-norm cone rather than itself, so the standard Lorentz-cone scaling formulas do not apply unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Duality uses the standard Euclidean pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_p^*=K_q,\qquad p\ne2\Longrightarrow K_p\ne K_p^*.
review_flags: Standard-pairing non-self-duality alone is not asserted to classify the cone up to arbitrary linear isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Cone Standard-Pairing Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural obstruction to Nesterov–Todd self-scaled geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a finite-dimensional regular cone. Existence of a self-scaled barrier in the Nesterov--Todd sense implies that \(K\) is a symmetric cone. Hence a nonsymmetric regular cone does not possess the canonical self-scaled primal-dual metric and scaling-point identities merely because it admits an ordinary self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nesterov–Todd self-scaled barrier geometry is restricted to symmetric cones; ordinary barrier existence does not provide it on a nonsymmetric cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is closed, convex, pointed, full-dimensional, and finite-dimensional.
Self-scaled barrier has the Nesterov--Todd meaning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsymmetric}\Longrightarrow K\text{ admits no Nesterov--Todd self-scaled barrier}.
knowledge_statements.title: Self-Scaled Symmetry Boundary

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(p\neq2\), the standard symmetric-cone Nesterov--Todd construction does not apply canonically to \(K_p\).

notation.meaning: The epigraph cone of the p-norm.
Dual cone under the standard pairing.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: non-self-dual norm cones delimit symmetric-cone scaling theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of canonical symmetry outside self-dual homogeneous cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The symmetric-cone scaling calculus requires a self-dual homogeneous cone equipped with a compatible Euclidean Jordan algebra. For the norm cones
\[
K_p=\{(t,z):t\geq\|z\|_p\},
\]
one has \(K_p^*=K_q\) under the standard inner product. When \(p\neq2\), \(K_p\neq K_p^*\), and these cones lack the Lorentz-cone Jordan structure used at \(p=2\). Therefore the identities \(P(w)s=x\), reciprocal scaling by \(w^{-1}\), and a canonical common point \(v\) cannot be asserted from symmetric-cone theory; a different barrier-dependent primal-dual scaling framework is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-self-dual, non-Jordan cones such as p-norm cones with p unequal to two fall outside the canonical symmetric-cone scaling construction.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the dual-cone identity and the claims about absence of symmetric-cone Jordan structure and canonical Nesterov–Todd scaling require a direct, inspectable source.

children.title: Nesterov–Todd Scaling Points
children.top_down_role: Intrinsic scaling points associated with primal-dual cone pairs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nesterov–Todd Scaling Point and Common Coordinate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior scaling point for a primal-dual pair on a symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,s\in\operatorname{int}K\), the Nesterov–Todd scaling point is \(w=x\#s^{-1}\). Equivalently, it is the interior point satisfying \(P(w)s=x\). Under primal-dual interchange its reciprocal satisfies \(w^{-1}=s\#x^{-1}\). The associated common coordinate is \(v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Nesterov–Todd point maps the dual slack to the primal point, has a reciprocal under primal-dual interchange, and places both variables at one common scaled point.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a symmetric cone in a Euclidean Jordan algebra.
knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov–Todd Scaling Point and Common Coordinate

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\) and quadratic representation \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Nesterov--Todd scaling point is \(w=x\#s^{-1}\), equivalently the unique \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(P(w)s=x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard symmetric-cone definition of the Nesterov-Todd scaling point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean-Jordan-algebra definition for interior points of a symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Nesterov--Todd scaling point of \((x,s)\) is
\[
w:=x\#s^{-1}
=P(x^{1/2})\bigl(P(x^{-1/2})s^{-1}\bigr)^{1/2}
\in\operatorname{int}K.
\]
It is characterized intrinsically by
\[
P(w)s=x.
\]
Its inverse is the scaling point for the interchanged pair, namely \(w^{-1}=s\#x^{-1}\). The induced common point is \(v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\), so the scaling treats primal and dual variables symmetrically after the self-dual identification of \(K\) with its dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Nesterov-Todd point is the Jordan geometric mean of the primal point and inverse dual slack, characterized by mapping the slack to the primal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov–Todd Scaling Points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and geometric-mean characterization are standard and fit the leaf, but no source or locator supports the formula, uniqueness characterization, and interchange identity.

children.title: Cone Geometric Means
children.top_down_role: Geometric-mean structures underlying symmetric-cone scaling.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intrinsic Geometric Mean on a Symmetric Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric mean of two interior elements of a symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a,b\in\operatorname{int}K\), define \(a\#b=P(a^{1/2})\bigl(P(a^{-1/2})b\bigr)^{1/2}\). It is the unique \(g\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(P(g)a^{-1}=b\), and it obeys \(a\#b=b\#a\), \(a\#a=a\), and \((a\#b)^{-1}=a^{-1}\#b^{-1}\). For the positive-definite matrix cone, \(a\#b=a^{1/2}(a^{-1/2}ba^{-1/2})^{1/2}a^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric-cone geometric mean is an intrinsic interior midpoint characterized by a quadratic-representation equation and specializing to the usual positive-definite matrix mean.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the symmetric cone of a Euclidean Jordan algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\#b\text{ is the unique }g\in\operatorname{int}K\text{ such that }P(g)a^{-1}=b.

notation.meaning: Jordan geometric mean of a and b.

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Geometric Mean on a Symmetric Cone

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The geometric mean \(a\#b\) is the unique \(g\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(P(g)a^{-1}=b\).

notation.meaning: Jordan geometric mean of two interior cone elements.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard geometric mean on a symmetric cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic geometric mean on the interior of a symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone geometric mean of \(a\) and \(b\) is
\[
a\#b:=P(a^{1/2})\bigl(P(a^{-1/2})b\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
It lies in \(\operatorname{int}K\), is symmetric, and obeys
\[
a\#b=b\#a,
\qquad a\#a=a,
\qquad (a\#b)^{-1}=a^{-1}\#b^{-1}.
\]
Equivalently, \(g=a\#b\) is the unique interior solution of \(P(g)a^{-1}=b\). For positive-definite matrices with the symmetrized matrix Jordan product, this formula reduces to the usual positive-definite matrix geometric mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cone geometric mean is the unique symmetric-cone midpoint solving a quadratic-representation equation and generalizes the positive-definite matrix geometric mean.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Geometric Means

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the container, but the symmetry, inversion, uniqueness, and matrix-specialization claims have no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Common Metric Construction
children.top_down_role: Shared local metrics induced by scaling-point geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric and reciprocal common coordinates induced by an interior scaling point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x,s\in\operatorname{int}K\), let \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfy \(P(w)s=x\), and set \(M=P(w)\). Then \(M\) is a self-adjoint positive-definite cone automorphism, \(M^{-1}=P(w^{-1})\), and \(Ms=x\). The reciprocal local inner products are \(\langle u,z\rangle_x=\langle u,M^{-1}z\rangle\) and \(\langle p,q\rangle_s=\langle p,Mq\rangle\). Moreover, \(P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\), so the reciprocal square-root maps place the primal and dual points in one common coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic representation of the scaling point maps the dual point to the primal point and defines reciprocal positive-definite metrics with a common scaled coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a symmetric cone in a Euclidean Jordan algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=P(w)\succ0,\quad M^{-1}=P(w^{-1}),\quad Ms=x,\quad P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s.
knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov–Todd Common Metric Operator

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the quadratic representation of the underlying Euclidean Jordan algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operator \(M=P(w)\) is self-adjoint positive definite, satisfies \(Ms=x\), and has inverse \(M^{-1}=P(w^{-1})\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quadratic-representation metric induced by Nesterov-Todd scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric operator induced by the Nesterov–Todd scaling point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set
\[
M:=P(w),
\qquad M^{-1}=P(w^{-1}).
\]
Then \(M\) is self-adjoint and positive definite on \(V\), maps \(K\) onto itself, and satisfies \(Ms=x\). The corresponding primal and dual local inner products are
\[
\langle u,z\rangle_{x}:=\langle u,M^{-1}z\rangle,
\qquad
\langle p,q\rangle_{s}:=\langle p,Mq\rangle.
\]
Their square-root coordinate maps are reciprocal: \(P(w^{-1/2})\) acts on primal vectors and \(P(w^{1/2})\) acts on dual vectors, placing both in the same Euclidean metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic representation of the scaling point is a positive-definite cone automorphism mapping the dual slack to the primal point and defining reciprocal local metrics.
knowledge_statements.title: Common Metric Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but self-adjointness, positive definiteness, cone-automorphism behavior, and the stated reciprocal metric construction require direct source support.

children.title: Scaling-Point Uniqueness
children.top_down_role: Regimes supporting a distinguished intrinsic scaling point.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra with symmetric cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists exactly one \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) such that \(P(w)s=x\), namely \(w=x\#s^{-1}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniqueness characterization of the symmetric-cone geometric mean
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior uniqueness theorem for symmetric-cone Nesterov–Todd scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x,s\in\operatorname{int}K\). Then the equation
\[
P(w)s=x
\]
has exactly one solution \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\). That solution is
\[
w=x\#s^{-1}
=P(x^{1/2})\bigl(P(x^{-1/2})s^{-1}\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently the positive-definite cone automorphism \(P(w)\), its positive square-root factors, and the common scaled point \(v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\) are uniquely determined by the ordered interior pair \((x,s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every interior primal-dual pair on a symmetric cone determines one and only one Nesterov-Todd scaling point and common metric.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Point Uniqueness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is standard and appropriately classified, but an existence-and-uniqueness theorem requires an authoritative citation with a theorem, section, or page locator.

children.title: Scaling-Point Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Boundary behavior near singular or noninterior primal-dual pairs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Obstruction to Interior Nesterov–Todd Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexistence and algebraic failure of ordinary scaling at singular cone points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(P(w)\) is a cone automorphism and maps \(\operatorname{int}K\) onto itself and \(\partial K\) onto itself. Consequently, if exactly one of \(x,s\in K\) is interior, no \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfies \(P(w)s=x\). If either input is singular, formulas requiring its Jordan inverse or inverse square root are undefined. Any scaling obtained only after restriction to a common face is a face-relative extension, not the ordinary interior scaling on \(K\). In the scalar cone \(K=\mathbb R_+\), \(P(w)s=w^2s\); taking \(s=0\) and \(x>0\) gives the explicit obstruction \(w^2s=0\ne x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interior scaling automorphism cannot map a boundary point to an interior point; singular inputs also invalidate inverse-based formulas, as already seen on the nonnegative ray.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a symmetric cone in a Euclidean Jordan algebra.
\(x,s\in K\), with at least one input singular for the stated failure cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl|\{x,s\}\cap\operatorname{int}K\bigr|=1\implies\nexists w\in\operatorname{int}K:\ P(w)s=x.

notation.meaning: Quadratic-representation cone automorphism generated by w.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Obstruction to Interior Nesterov–Todd Scaling

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a symmetric cone in a Euclidean Jordan algebra \(V\).
At least one of \(x,s\in K\) lies on \(\partial K\), while the other lies in \(\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfies \(P(w)s=x\); the ordinary Nesterov--Todd scaling point is therefore undefined.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cone automorphisms preserve interior and boundary strata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary failure of the interior geometric-mean construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\), the map \(P(w)\) is a cone automorphism and therefore maps \(\operatorname{int}K\) onto \(\operatorname{int}K\) and \(\partial K\) onto \(\partial K\). Hence, if exactly one of \(x\) and \(s\) is interior, the equation \(P(w)s=x\) has no interior solution. Moreover, when either point is singular, the formula \(w=x\#s^{-1}\) may be undefined because the Jordan inverse or inverse square root does not exist. Boundary extensions, when available on a common face, are not the ordinary interior Nesterov--Todd scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard scaling point degenerates at the cone boundary: an interior quadratic representation cannot map a boundary point to an interior point.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Point Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification is appropriate and the exactly-one-interior case is plausible, but the boundary-preservation and common-face extension claims lack a cited source.

children.title: Nesterov–Todd Symmetric-Cone Directions
children.top_down_role: Search directions induced by the Nesterov–Todd scaling point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed residual-sign convention for an NT primal-dual direction in common Jordan coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a Euclidean Jordan algebra with unit \(e\), rank \(r\), symmetric cone \(K\), and quadratic representation \(P\). For \(x,s\in\operatorname{int}K\), let \(w\) satisfy \(P(w)s=x\), and set \(v=P(w^{-1/2})x=P(w^{1/2})s\). With \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^*y-s\), \(\mu=\langle x,s\rangle/r\), and \(0\le\sigma\le1\), solve \[AP(w^{1/2})d_x=r_p,\qquad A^*\Delta y+P(w^{-1/2})d_s=r_d,\qquad v\circ(d_x+d_s)=\sigma\mu e-v\circ v.\] Recover \[\Delta x=P(w^{1/2})d_x,\qquad\Delta s=P(w^{-1/2})d_s.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The NT direction solves feasibility and centered complementarity in common Jordan coordinates and maps both scaled directions back.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra with unit \(e\), rank \(r\), and cone of squares \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\text{ satisfies the displayed NT Newton equations under the stated residual convention}.

notation.meaning: Jordan quadratic representation at the NT scaling point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solvability Boundary for the NT Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient uniqueness conditions and the singular-operator boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strict interiority makes \(P(w^{1/2})\), \(P(w^{-1/2})\), and \(L_v:h\mapsto v\circ h\) invertible. If \(A\) has full row rank, the displayed scaled KKT system has a unique solution. More generally, uniqueness holds exactly when its KKT operator is nonsingular; loss of interiority can make the scaling undefined, while constraint redundancy can make the multiplier nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict interiority supplies invertible scaling operators, and full row rank is a sufficient uniqueness condition.
assumptions_latex: For the sufficient condition, \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}A=m\Longrightarrow\text{the displayed NT system has a unique solution}.
knowledge_statements.title: Solvability Boundary for the NT Direction

assumptions_latex: \(A:V\to\mathbb R^m\) defines the conic pair \(Ax=b\), \(A^*y+s=c\) over a symmetric cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the displayed scaled Newton system and applying the inverse scalings produces the Nesterov--Todd primal-dual search direction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard scaled Newton system for Nesterov-Todd symmetric-cone directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-or-infeasible Newton direction in Nesterov–Todd common coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given residuals \(r_p=b-Ax\) and \(r_d=c-A^*y-s\), solve for \((d_x,\Delta y,d_s)\) from
\[
A P(w^{1/2})d_x=r_p,
\qquad
A^*\Delta y+P(w^{-1/2})d_s=r_d,
\qquad
L_v(d_x+d_s)=\sigma\mu e-v\circ v.
\]
Recover
\[
\Delta x=P(w^{1/2})d_x,

delta s=P(w^{-1/2})d_s,
\]
where \(delta s\) denotes \(\Delta s\). Choose a step length preserving \(x+\alpha\Delta x\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(s+\alpha\Delta s\in\operatorname{int}K\); stop when the feasibility residuals and \(\mu\) meet their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Nesterov-Todd direction solves primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and centered complementarity equations in common scaled coordinates, then maps the direction back.
knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov–Todd Symmetric-Cone Directions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the direction leaf, but the exact scaled Newton system is convention-sensitive and unsupported. The recovery display incorrectly writes “delta s” instead of \(\Delta s\), and the assumptions do not introduce the Jordan unit \(e\) or explicitly specify the Euclidean Jordan algebra structure and its rank.

children.title: Blockwise Nesterov–Todd Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling organization across product symmetric cones.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorwise Nesterov–Todd Scaling on Product Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-product assembly of Nesterov–Todd scaling, coordinates, and admissible steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\prod_{i=1}^r V_i\) be a product of Euclidean Jordan algebras with symmetric cone \(K=\prod_{i=1}^r K_i\), and let \(x=(x_i),s=(s_i)\in\operatorname{int}K\). For every block set \(w_i=x_i\#s_i^{-1}\) and \(v_i=P_i(w_i^{-1/2})x_i=P_i(w_i^{1/2})s_i\). Then \(w=(w_i)\), \(P(w)=\operatorname{diag}(P_i(w_i))\), and the scaled direction components are formed blockwise. Affine feasibility equations may couple the blocks, and one common step length must keep every updated block in \(\operatorname{int}K_i\). The ordinary construction is unavailable if any required block inverse is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nesterov–Todd scaling decomposes factor by factor on a product symmetric cone, while feasibility equations and the accepted step can remain globally coupled.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\prod_{i=1}^r V_i\) is a product of Euclidean Jordan algebras with cone \(K=\prod_{i=1}^r K_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w=(x_i\#s_i^{-1})_{i=1}^r,\qquad P(w)=\operatorname{diag}(P_i(w_i)).

notation.meaning: Common scaled point of block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorwise Nesterov–Todd Scaling on Product Cones

assumptions_latex: \(V=V_1\times\cdots\times V_r\) is a product of Euclidean Jordan algebras with symmetric cone \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The product scaling is \(w=(x_i\#s_i^{-1})_{i=1}^r\), and its metric is the block-diagonal operator \(P(w)=\operatorname{diag}(P_i(w_i))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct-product decomposition of Euclidean Jordan algebra scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent Nesterov–Todd scaling on factors of a product symmetric cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each block \(i=1,\ldots,r\), compute
\[
w_i=x_i\#s_i^{-1},
\qquad
v_i=P_i(w_i^{-1/2})x_i=P_i(w_i^{1/2})s_i.
\]
Assemble \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_r)\) and the block-diagonal metric
\[
P(w)=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(P_1(w_1),\ldots,P_r(w_r)\bigr).
\]
Scale direction components independently by \(d_{x,i}=P_i(w_i^{-1/2})\Delta x_i\) and \(d_{s,i}=P_i(w_i^{1/2})\Delta s_i\), solve the globally coupled feasibility equations together with blockwise complementarity equations, and select a common step length that keeps every updated block in \(\operatorname{int}K_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a product cone, compute scaling points and complementarity coordinates independently by block, while feasibility equations and the accepted step length remain globally coupled.
knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Nesterov–Todd Scaling

children.title: Alizadeh–Haeberly–Overton Direction
children.top_down_role: Directly symmetrized semidefinite primal-dual direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Alizadeh–Haeberly–Overton Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: AHO direction for a standard-form semidefinite primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(X,S\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Define \(r_p=b-\mathcal A(X)\), \(r_d=C-\mathcal A^*y-S\), and \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\). For \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), an AHO direction is a triple \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\in\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\) satisfying \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[\frac{X\Delta S+\Delta X S+\Delta S X+S\Delta X}{2}=\sigma\mu I-\frac{XS+SX}{2}.\] A subsequent step length is chosen so that \(X+\alpha\Delta X\succ0\) and \(S+\alpha\Delta S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The AHO direction corrects primal and dual feasibility while directly symmetrizing the linearized semidefinite complementarity equation; its step length is restricted to preserve positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triple \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\) solves the directly symmetrized primal-dual Newton system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order remainder after a full AHO complementarity step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal J(X,S):=(XS+SX)/2\). If an AHO direction satisfies \[\tfrac12(X\Delta S+\Delta XS+\Delta SX+S\Delta X)=\sigma\mu I-\mathcal J(X,S),\] then \[\mathcal J(X+\Delta X,S+\Delta S)-\sigma\mu I=\tfrac12(\Delta X\Delta S+\Delta S\Delta X).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full AHO Newton step removes the linearized Jordan complementarity residual and leaves the symmetrized quadratic product of the increments.
assumptions_latex: The displayed AHO complementarity equation holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal J(X+\Delta X,S+\Delta S)-\sigma\mu I=\mathcal J(\Delta X,\Delta S).

knowledge_statements.title: Helmberg–Kojima–Monteiro Direction Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal- and dual-oriented HKM specializations of the Monteiro–Zhang symmetrization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \((X,y,S)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Define \(r_p=b-\mathcal A(X)\), \(r_d=C-\mathcal A^*y-S\), \(\mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n\), and \(H_P(M)=\tfrac12(PMP^{-1}+P^{-T}M^TP^T)\) for invertible \(P\). For \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), the two HKM orientations are obtained from \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[H_P(X\Delta S+\Delta X S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS)\] by choosing \(P=X^{-1/2}\) or \(P=S^{1/2}\), with \((\Delta X,\Delta y,\Delta S)\in\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\). A subsequent step length is restricted so that both updated matrix variables remain positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The HKM family corrects feasibility and uses either a primal-derived or dual-derived square-root transformation to symmetrize the semidefinite complementarity Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each indicated choice of \(P\) defines an HKM-oriented primal-dual search direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Kojima–Shindoh–Hara Direction Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potential-reduction semidefinite directions expressed through scaled complementarity linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=P(X,S)\) be the invertible scaling prescribed by a KSH potential-reduction variant, and define \(H_P(M)=\tfrac12(PMP^{-1}+P^{-T}M^TP^T)\). Its direction is a symmetric solution of \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[H_P(X\Delta S+\Delta X S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS),\qquad \mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n.\] The scaling and centering parameter are selected so that a positive step decreases the designated primal-dual potential while preserving \(X+\alpha\Delta X\succ0\) and \(S+\alpha\Delta S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KSH directions combine a scaled, symmetrized complementarity Newton equation with feasibility correction and a step selected to reduce a primal-dual potential.
assumptions_latex: The chosen KSH variant specifies a primal-dual potential and centering rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed system determines the KSH-type Newton direction for the prescribed scaling variant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed system is only a generic Monteiro–Zhang symmetrization. No source identifies the KSH-specific scaling, potential, or centering rule, so the named family and claimed potential decrease cannot be verified.

children.title: Monteiro–Tsuchiya Direction Family

knowledge_statements.title: Monteiro–Tsuchiya Direction Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling-parameterized semidefinite directions within the Monteiro–Zhang calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an invertible Monteiro–Tsuchiya scaling \(P=P(X,S)\), define \(H_P(M)=\tfrac12(PMP^{-1}+P^{-T}M^TP^T)\). Given residuals \(r_p,r_d\), its primal-dual direction is a symmetric solution of \[\mathcal A(\Delta X)=r_p,\qquad \mathcal A^*(\Delta y)+\Delta S=r_d,\] \[H_P(X\Delta S+\Delta X S)=\sigma\mu I-H_P(XS),\qquad \mu=\langle X,S\rangle/n.\] An admissible member of the family must use its prescribed scaling rule and a step size keeping both updated matrices positive definite; different admissible scaling parameters produce different family members.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monteiro–Tsuchiya directions are scaling-dependent symmetrized Newton directions that share feasibility equations but differ through their prescribed complementarity scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(P(X,S)\) is an invertible scaling allowed by the selected family member.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system defines a scaling-indexed family of interior semidefinite primal-dual directions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic scaled Newton system does not identify the Monteiro–Tsuchiya scaling rule or admissible parameter set. A source defining the named family is required before its mathematical formulation can be reviewed.

knowledge_statements.title: Paired Primal-Dual Barrier Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton direction using compatible Legendre primal and dual barrier oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a proper cone, let \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb R\) be a Legendre barrier, and let \(F_*\) be its conjugate barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\). For \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), choose \(\mu>0\) and linearize the paired centrality equations \[s+\mu\nabla F(x)=0,\qquad x+\mu\nabla F_*(s)=0\] together with the primal and dual affine constraints. The Newton direction solves the resulting coupled linear system; a step is accepted only while both updated points remain in their cone interiors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible primal and dual barrier gradients define paired centrality equations whose joint Newton linearization supplies a nonsymmetric-cone search direction.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed, pointed, full-dimensional convex cone.
\(F\) and \(F_*\) are compatible Legendre barriers on the primal and dual interiors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled linearization defines a paired primal-dual barrier direction.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the primal cone.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For general Legendre barriers, the two displayed centrality equations require a precise conjugacy convention and scaling relation; compatibility is not defined. An authoritative nonsymmetric-cone source is needed to determine the correct hypotheses and formulas.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Newton Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block Newton representation for conic feasibility and barrier centrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, and consider \(Ax=b\) and \(A^*y+s=c\), where \(x\in E\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(s,c\in E^*\). Define \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^*y-s\), and let \(r_c:E\times E^*\times(0,\infty)\to E^*\) be differentiable in \((x,s)\). A primal-dual Newton architecture solves \[\begin{bmatrix}A&0&0\\0&A^*&I\\D_xr_c&0&D_sr_c\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\\\Delta s\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_p\\r_d\\-r_c(x,s;\mu)\end{bmatrix}.\] For a specified block partition, if the square pivot operator used in an elimination is nonsingular, the corresponding Schur-complement system is equivalent to the unreduced system and recovers the same Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual Newton system couples linearized primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and centrality. A Schur-complement reduction is equivalent only when its specified square pivot operator is nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
\(r_c\) is differentiable in \((x,s)\) at the current interior pair.
Each stated reduction uses a specified square nonsingular pivot operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unreduced block system and every valid specified Schur-complement reduction recover the same Newton direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Start Primal-Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual path-following initialized at a strictly feasible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional, let \(K\subset E\) be a proper cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E^*\) define \(Ax=b\) and \(A^*y+s=c\). Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(s_0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\) satisfying \(Ax_0=b\) and \(A^*y_0+s_0=c\), repeat: choose a positive target central parameter; compute \((\Delta x_k,\Delta y_k,\Delta s_k)\) satisfying \[A\Delta x_k=0,
\qquad A^*\Delta y_k+\Delta s_k=0\] together with the selected Newton centrality equation; and choose \(\alpha_k>0\) so that the updated pair remains in \(\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*\) and in the prescribed central neighborhood. Terminate when \(\langle x_k,s_k\rangle\) meets the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from strict primal-dual feasibility, each accepted Newton step satisfies homogeneous feasibility equations, preserves both cone interiors and the chosen central neighborhood, and is tested using the duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset E\) is a proper cone in a finite-dimensional space.
A strictly primal-dual feasible initial point is available.
The selected centrality Newton system is solvable and each accepted step preserves the prescribed neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate remains primal and dual feasible until the stopping test is met.
