knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Primal-Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correcting primal-dual path-following from an interior but infeasible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional, let \(K\subset E\) be a proper cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E^*\) define the conic pair. Initialize \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(s_0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\), without requiring affine feasibility. At iteration \(k\), define \(r_p=b-Ax_k\), \(r_d=c-A^*y_k-s_k\), and a differentiable centrality residual \(r_c\). Compute \((\Delta x_k,\Delta y_k,\Delta s_k)\) from \[A\Delta x_k=r_p,\qquad A^*\Delta y_k+\Delta s_k=r_d,\qquad Dr_c[\Delta x_k,\Delta s_k]=-r_c+q_k.\] Choose an interior step according to the specified residual-centrality merit rule. Terminate when the primal residual, dual residual, and duality gap meet their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible-start method computes one coupled Newton direction for primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and centrality, then selects an interior step using a specified merit rule and stops when all requested tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset E\) is a proper cone in a finite-dimensional space.
The selected centrality residual, correction term, and globalization rule are specified by the method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(r_p\), \(r_d\), and \(\langle x,s\rangle\) satisfy their prescribed stopping tolerances.

The identity does not imply that a full step preserves cone interiority or centrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common residual-correction step multiplies both affine feasibility residuals by one minus the step length; an admissible full step eliminates them.

children.title: Fraction-to-Boundary Control
children.top_down_role: Interiority safeguards based on distance to cone boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Fraction-to-Boundary Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step truncation retaining a prescribed fraction of the maximal joint interior step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional, let \(K\subset E\) be a proper cone, let \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and let \((\Delta x,\Delta s)\in E\times E^*\). Define \[\alpha_{\max}=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:x+t\Delta x\in K,\ s+t\Delta s\in K^*\text{ for every }t\in[0,\alpha]\}.\] Given \(\tau\in(0,1)\), set \(\alpha=\min\{1,\tau\alpha_{\max}\}\) when \(\alpha_{\max}<\infty\), and set \(\alpha=1\) when \(\alpha_{\max}=\infty\). Then update \((x^+,s^+)=(x,s)+\alpha(\Delta x,\Delta s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The step is the smaller of one and a fixed fraction of the maximal joint cone-feasible step; an unbounded feasible ray permits a full step. The update therefore remains strictly interior.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset E\) is a proper cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(x^+\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(s^+\in\operatorname{int}K^*\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate primal and dual step-length variant of fraction-to-boundary interiority control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\alpha_p^{\max}=\sup\{a\geq0:x+t\Delta x\in K\ \forall t\in[0,a]\},\qquad \alpha_d^{\max}=\sup\{a\geq0:s+t\Delta s\in K^*\ \forall t\in[0,a]\}.\] For a finite maximum set \(\alpha_p=\min\{1,\tau_p\alpha_p^{\max}\}\) and \(\alpha_d=\min\{1,\tau_d\alpha_d^{\max}\}\), and use value \(1\) when the corresponding maximum is infinite. Then \(x+\alpha_p\Delta x\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(s+\alpha_d\Delta s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\). A method requiring one common primal-dual step may use \(\min\{\alpha_p,\alpha_d\}\); separate steps alone do not guarantee preservation of coupled affine or centrality equations.

children.title: Damped Interior Steps

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Interior Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracked primal-dual update preserving interiority and sufficient merit decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional, let \(K\subset E\) be a proper cone, and define the open domain \(\mathcal D=\operatorname{int}K\times\mathbb R^m\times\operatorname{int}K^*\). Given \(z=(x,y,s)\in\mathcal D\), a direction \(d=(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\), a merit function \(\Phi:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) differentiable at \(z\), and constants \(\beta,c\in(0,1)\), start with \(\alpha=1\). Replace \(\alpha\) by \(\beta\alpha\) until \(z+\alpha d\in\mathcal D\) and \[\Phi(z+\alpha d)\leq\Phi(z)+c\alpha D\Phi(z)[d].\] Set \(z^+=z+\alpha d\). If \(D\Phi(z)[d]<0\), openness of \(\mathcal D\) and differentiability of \(\Phi\) at \(z\) imply that the backtracking test is satisfied for all sufficiently small positive \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an interior primal-dual iterate, the procedure repeatedly contracts a descent step until the new cone variables remain interior and the merit function satisfies the Armijo decrease condition.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset E\) is a proper cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backtracking terminates with \(z^+\in\mathcal D\) satisfying the Armijo decrease condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\), let \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\), and let \((\Delta x,\Delta s)\) satisfy the Newton equations and affine constraints. Return the first accepted trial point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Interior Armijo Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an accepted sufficiently short trial step for an interior descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D=\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*\), \(z\in\mathcal D\), and let \(d\) be a search direction. Suppose \(\Psi:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(z\) and \(\Psi'(z;d)<0\). For \(0<\eta,\beta<1\), there exists \(j<\infty\) such that \(\alpha=\beta^j\) satisfies \(z+\alpha d\in\mathcal D\) and \[\Psi(z+\alpha d)\leq\Psi(z)+\eta\alpha\Psi'(z;d).\] Hence geometric interior Armijo backtracking terminates finitely.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists j<\infty\) such that \(\alpha=\beta^j\) is interior and satisfies the Armijo inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Interiority Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp barrier-local step boundary for guaranteed primal interiority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be self-concordant on \(\operatorname{int}K\). The Dikin guarantee gives \[\|h\|_x<1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x+h\in\operatorname{int}K.\] No universal guarantee remains at radius one. Indeed, for \(K=\mathbb R_+\), \(F(x)=-\log x\), \(x=1\), and \(h=-1\), one has \(\|h\|_x=1\) but \(x+h=0\notin\operatorname{int}K\). Thus an undamped Newton trial reaching unit local norm may hit the cone boundary, where the barrier and Newton model cease to be defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local barrier steps shorter than one are safely interior; at unit length this guarantee is sharp, as a scalar logarithmic-barrier example shows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict bound \(\|h\|_x<1\) is a general interiority guarantee, whereas \(\|h\|_x\leq1\) is not.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp barrier-local step boundary for guaranteed dual interiority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_*\) be a self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\), and let \(\|\cdot\|_{F_*,s}\) be its Hessian local norm. Then \[\|q\|_{F_*,s}<1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad s+q\in\operatorname{int}K^*.\] The strict inequality is sharp: for \(K^*=\mathbb R_+\), \(F_*(s)=-\log s\), \(s=1\), and \(q=-1\), one has \(\|q\|_{F_*,s}=1\) but \(s+q=0\notin\operatorname{int}K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual step of local norm below one remains interior, whereas a unit-local-norm step can reach the dual-cone boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The universal dual-interiority guarantee requires \(\|q\|_{F_*,s}<1\); replacing it by a non-strict bound is invalid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Commutation, Spectral Bound, and Conditioning of \(\Xi_A\Xi_B^{-1}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and spectral properties of SDP symmetrization operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,B\in\mathcal S^n\). If \(AB=BA\), then \(\Xi_A\Xi_B=\Xi_B\Xi_A\). If \(A,B\in\mathcal P_+\), then \[\lambda_{\min}\!\left(\Xi_A\Xi_B^{-1}+\Xi_B^{-1}\Xi_A\right)>\lambda_{\min}\!\left(\mathcal S_I(AB^{-1})\right).\] If, in addition, \(AB=BA\), then \[\operatorname{cond}(\Xi_A\Xi_B^{-1})<4\operatorname{cond}(AB^{-1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Commuting symmetric matrices induce commuting Xi operators. For positive-definite A and B, a strict minimum-eigenvalue bound holds for the symmetrized operator product; if A and B also commute, its condition number is less than four times that of AB inverse.
assumptions_latex: A,B\in\mathcal P_+,\ AB=BA\ \text{for the conditioning conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AB=BA\Rightarrow\Xi_A\Xi_B=\Xi_B\Xi_A;\quad \lambda_{\min}(\Xi_A\Xi_B^{-1}+\Xi_B^{-1}\Xi_A)>\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal S_I(AB^{-1}));\quad AB=BA\Rightarrow\operatorname{cond}(\Xi_A\Xi_B^{-1})<4\operatorname{cond}(AB^{-1}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomiality of the MT semilong-step path-following algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract also records that an analogous bound for the entire Monteiro–Zhang family is not known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma\in(0,1/\sqrt2)\) and \(\bar\sigma\in(0,1)\). In Framework MT-PD, suppose \((X^0,y^0,S^0)\in\mathcal N_\infty(\gamma)\), \(\sigma_k:=\sigma\), and \[\alpha_k:=\max\{\alpha\in[0,1]:(X^k,y^k,S^k)+\alpha(\Delta X^k,\Delta y^k,\Delta S^k)\in\mathcal N_\infty(\gamma)\}.\] Then every iterate lies in \(\mathcal N_\infty(\gamma)\) and, for all \(k\geq0\), \[X^k\bullet S^k\leq(1-\eta)^k(X^0\bullet S^0),\qquad \eta:=\frac{\sigma(1-\sigma)\gamma(1-\sqrt2\gamma)^2}{40n[\gamma^2+(1-\bar\sigma)^2]}.\] If \(\max\{\gamma^{-1},(1-\sqrt2\gamma)^{-1},\sigma^{-1},(1-\sigma)^{-1}\}\) is independent of \(n\), the method terminates in at most \(\mathcal O(nL)\) iterations. No corresponding semilong-step result with this complexity is known for the whole MZ family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting in the infinity neighborhood and taking the largest step that remains in it, the MT semilong-step method stays in the neighborhood and contracts complementarity geometrically by at least the stated eta. With dimension-independent conditioning of the parameters, it terminates in O(nL) iterations; the same guarantee is not known for the entire MZ family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\geq0:\ (X^k,y^k,S^k)\in\mathcal N_\infty(\gamma),\quad X^k\bullet S^k\leq(1-\eta)^k(X^0\bullet S^0);\quad \max\{\gamma^{-1},(1-\sqrt2\gamma)^{-1},\sigma^{-1},(1-\sigma)^{-1}\}=\mathcal O(1)\Rightarrow\text{iterations}=\mathcal O(nL).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictor–Corrector Neighborhood Invariants and Iteration Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence and iteration complexity of the stated primal-dual SDP predictor–corrector algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\tau\in(0,1/15]\). For every even \(k\ge 0\), \((X^k,y^k,S^k)\in\mathcal N_F(\tau)\), \(\alpha_k=1/\mathcal O(\sqrt n)\), and \(X^{k+1}\bullet S^{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)(X^k\bullet S^k)\). For every odd \(k\ge 0\), \((X^k,y^k,S^k)\in\mathcal N_F(2\tau)\) and \(X^{k+1}\bullet S^{k+1}=X^k\bullet S^k\). Consequently, the algorithm terminates after at most \(\mathcal O(\sqrt n\,L)\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the neighborhood parameter is positive and at most 1/15, even predictor steps remain in the narrower neighborhood and reduce complementarity by the stated step factor, while odd corrector steps remain in the doubled neighborhood and preserve complementarity. The algorithm therefore terminates in O(sqrt(n) L) iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Scaling Prediction

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual iterate with residuals \(r_p=Ax-b\), \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\), solve \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}=-r_p,\qquad A^T\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=-r_d,\qquad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=-XSe.\] Let \(\alpha_p^{\mathrm{aff}}\) and \(\alpha_d^{\mathrm{aff}}\) be the largest steps in \([0,1]\) preserving nonnegativity of the corresponding primal and dual slacks. children.title: Adaptive Centering Selection
children.top_down_role: Data-driven centering regimes derived from predicted progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthant-cone Mehrotra centering rule using affine-predicted complementarity, with explicit clipping for numerical ratios outside the nominal interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu=x^Ts/n>0\), let \(\widehat\rho=\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu\), and set \(\rho=\min\{1,\max\{0,\widehat\rho\}\}\). For an exponent \(p>0\), choose \(\sigma=\rho^p\) and use \(\sigma\mu\) as the centered complementarity target in the corrector equations. The customary Mehrotra rule uses \(p=3\). Thus a small predicted ratio requests little centering, whereas a ratio near one requests strong centering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip the predicted-to-current complementarity ratio to zero through one, raise it to a positive power—customarily three—and use the result as the corrector's centering weight.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\) is supplied by the affine-scaling prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\sigma\leq1\), and \(\sigma\) is nondecreasing in the clipped predicted-reduction ratio.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra centering parameter selected from predicted complementarity reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu=x^Ts/n>0\) and let \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\) be the complementarity predicted by the affine-scaling step. Choose an exponent \(p>0\) and set \[\sigma=\min\left\{1,\max\left\{0,\left(\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}}{\mu}\right)^p\right\}\right\}.\] Use \(\sigma\mu\) as the complementarity target in the corrector equation. The customary Mehrotra choice is \(p=3\): strong predicted reduction makes \(\sigma\) small, while weak predicted reduction increases centering.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before a correction pass, retain the previously accepted accumulated direction \(d\). After every added correction, form the complete trial point \(z^+(\alpha)\) from the accumulated direction. If the test fails, shorten \(\alpha\) or discard the newest correction and repeat the test. Testing only the newest correction vector or only the average duality gap is insufficient to establish neighborhood membership.

children.title: Overcorrection Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar orthant example showing why the boundary step must be recomputed for the complete accumulated direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+\) and let the current point be \(x=1\). Suppose a previously admissible direction is modified by an additional correction so that the complete accumulated direction becomes \(d_x=-2\). Accepting the unit step without recomputing its cone-boundary limit gives \(x^+=x+d_x=-1\notin K\). Thus admissibility of an earlier direction or of a correction equation does not imply admissibility of their accumulated direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An added correction can turn an admissible step into one that leaves the cone unless the boundary limit is recomputed for the complete direction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthant-cone example showing that an interior corrected point can preserve average complementarity while leaving any prescribed narrow infinity-norm neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+^2\), \(x=s=(1,1)\), and \(\mu=x^Ts/2=1\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), set \(x^+=(\varepsilon,2-\varepsilon)\) and \(s^+=(1,1)\). Then \(x^+,s^+\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(\mu^+=(x^+)^Ts^+/2=1\), but \(\|X^+s^+-\mu^+e\|_\infty=1-\varepsilon\). Hence, for every \(\theta\in(0,1)\), choosing \(\varepsilon<1-\theta\) violates \(\|X^+s^+-\mu^+e\|_\infty\leq\theta\mu^+\) despite preserving interiority and average complementarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Heuristic Prescription Does Not Imply Polynomiality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between practical Mehrotra rules and predictor-corrector methods carrying proved polynomial iteration bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The practical combination of an affine predictor, adaptively selected centering parameter, second-order correction, and aggressive fraction-to-boundary step does not by itself assert an invariant central neighborhood or a uniform potential or gap decrease. Therefore those rules alone do not entail an iteration bound polynomial in the barrier parameter \(\nu\) and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). A polynomial analysis requires additional explicitly stated neighborhood, step-size, and progress invariants. This is an absence-of-implication statement, not a proof that a Mehrotra implementation has superpolynomial behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The practical Mehrotra prescription alone supplies no polynomial iteration theorem; such a theorem needs additional invariant-neighborhood and progress conditions, but this does not prove nonpolynomial behavior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local quadratic upper model for the primal potential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the change in the primal log-determinant potential under a step of scaled spectral norm below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0\succ0\) and \(x_1\succ0\), and suppose the primal potential \(\phi(\cdot,\underline z)\) is defined at both points. If
\[
\left\|Q_{x_0^{-1/2}}(x_1-x_0)\right\|_2<1,
\]
then
\[
\phi(x_1,\underline z)-\phi(x_0,\underline z)
\le
\left\langle\nabla_x\phi(x_0,\underline z),x_1-x_0\right\rangle
+
\frac{\left\|Q_{x_0^{-1/2}}(x_1-x_0)\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2}
{2\left(1-\left\|Q_{x_0^{-1/2}}(x_1-x_0)\right\|_2\right)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive step whose scaled spectral norm is below one, the increase of the primal potential is at most its first-order change plus an explicit quadratic remainder controlled by the scaled Frobenius and spectral norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(x_1,\underline z)-\phi(x_0,\underline z)\le\langle\nabla_x\phi(x_0,\underline z),x_1-x_0\rangle+\frac{\|Q_{x_0^{-1/2}}(x_1-x_0)\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{2(1-\|Q_{x_0^{-1/2}}(x_1-x_0)\|_2)}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Both constructions combine a logarithm of a positive objective-bound gap with a cone barrier: \[\Phi_p(x)=\rho\log g_p(x;L)+F(x),\qquad \Phi_d(y,s)=\rho\log g_d(y;U)+F_*(s).\] However, validity of \(L\) and \(U\) alone gives no universal ordering between \(\Phi_p\) and \(\Phi_d\). Indeed, decreasing a valid \(L\) enlarges \(g_p\) arbitrarily, while increasing a valid \(U\) enlarges \(g_d\) arbitrarily, without changing either feasible point. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower bound for the log-determinant below the Jordan identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A trace and norm estimate for an element lying strictly between zero and the identity of a rank-r Euclidean Jordan algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in J\), where \(J\) is a Euclidean Jordan algebra of rank \(r\) with identity \(e\). If \(0\prec x\prec e\), then
\[
\log\det x\ge \operatorname{tr}x-r-\frac{\|x-e\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{2\bigl(1-\|x-e\|_2\bigr)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric-cone element strictly between zero and the identity, its log-determinant is bounded below by its trace minus the rank and a quadratic deviation term whose denominator depends on the spectral distance from the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \log\det x\ge \operatorname{tr}x-r-\frac{\|x-e\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{2(1-\|x-e\|_2)}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a \(\vartheta\)-normal barrier for \(K\). children.title: Linear-Scaling Potential Methods
children.top_down_role: Potential reduction organized around linear scaling.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a regular cone admitting a logarithmically homogeneous barrier \(F\).
The conic problem has a strictly feasible primal-dual point, and the selected potential \(\Phi\) is bounded below on every nonterminal level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iteration satisfies \(\Phi(z_{k+1})\leq \Phi(z_k)-\delta\); termination returns the first iterate meeting the prescribed gap tolerance.

notation.meaning: invertible linear scaling at the current point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic cone-preserving linear-scaling potential-reduction template; no particular symmetric-cone scaling is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an interior point \(z_0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and potential \(\Phi\), iteration \(k\) chooses an invertible linear scaling \(W_k\) that maps the local barrier geometry at \(z_k\) to fixed reference coordinates. It computes a feasible scaled direction \(d_k\) satisfying the prescribed primal-dual linearized equations and \(D\Phi(z_k)[W_k^{-1}d_k]<0\). A step length \(\alpha_k>0\) is selected so that \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kW_k^{-1}d_k\) remains interior and \(\Phi(z_{k+1})\leq\Phi(z_k)-\delta\), where \(\delta>0\) is the method's decrease constant. Stop when the normalized duality gap is at most \(\varepsilon\), and output \(z_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the local geometry linearly, compute a feasible potential-decreasing direction, take an interior step with uniform decrease, and stop when the normalized duality gap reaches tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Scaling Potential Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unspecified scaling, direction system, and potential assumptions do not establish existence of a uniform decrease constant or termination. An authoritative source for a precise linear-scaling potential method is required.

children.title: Projective-Scaling Potential Methods
children.top_down_role: Potential reduction organized around projective scaling.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a regular cone and \(\ell\in\operatorname{int}K^*\) defines the section \(S=\{x\in\operatorname{int}K:\ell(x)=1\}\).
The potential \(\Phi\) is defined on the normalized primal-dual feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted projective updates remain interior, preserve the chosen normalization, and reduce \(\Phi\) until the gap stopping test is met.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic normalized-section formulation of projective potential reduction on a regular cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a strictly feasible normalized point \(z_0\). At iteration \(k\), choose a cone-preserving invertible map \(T_k\) and form the projective normalization \(\Pi_k(z)=T_kz/\ell(T_kz)\) whenever \(\ell(T_kz)>0\). In the normalized section, compute a feasible direction \(d_k\) with negative directional derivative for \(\Phi\). Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) so that \(w_{k+1}=\Pi_k(z_k)+\alpha_kd_k\) is interior and \(\Phi(w_{k+1})\leq\Phi(\Pi_k(z_k))-\delta\). Lift \(w_{k+1}\) through \(\Pi_k^{-1}\), choosing the representative satisfying the affine conic constraints. Stop when the normalized duality gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize onto a projective cone section, decrease the potential there, lift the new point back to the affine constraints, and stop at the requested gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Projective-Scaling Potential Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Projective normalization is generally many-to-one, so the asserted inverse lift and preservation of affine constraints require a precise method and hypotheses. The decrease guarantee also lacks support.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Feasibility Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-residual Phase-I model for primal conic feasibility, with attainment stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=b-Ae\). Consider the Phase-I model \[\min_{x,\tau}\ \tau\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+\tau r=b,\quad x\in K,\quad \tau\geq0.\] The point \((e,1)\) is strictly feasible relative to the cone constraints. If this problem attains its minimum, then its minimum value is zero if and only if the original system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a nonnegative scalar multiplying the initial residual. The reference point provides a strict cone initialization, and, when the minimum is attained, a zero minimum is equivalent to feasibility of the original conic system.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a regular cone, \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(e\in\operatorname{int}K\), and \(r=b-Ae\).
The displayed Phase-I problem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \((e,1)\) initializes the auxiliary model, and its attained minimum equals \(0\) exactly when \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), is feasible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual scalar-residual Phase-I model for recovering a feasible dual slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\bar y\) and \(\bar s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and set \(r_d=c-A^*\bar y-\bar s\). Consider \[\min_{y,s,\sigma}\ \sigma\quad\text{subject to}\quad A^*y+s+\sigma r_d=c,\quad s\in K^*,\quad\sigma\geq0.\] The point \((\bar y,\bar s,1)\) is feasible and interior in the cone variables. If the minimum is attained, its value is zero exactly when \(A^*y+s=c\), \(s\in K^*\), is feasible. Strict dual initialization additionally requires the recovered \(s\) to lie in \(\operatorname{int}K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual Phase-I model scales an initial dual residual and has attained value zero exactly when the original dual equations are feasible.
assumptions_latex: The displayed dual Phase-I problem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\sigma=0\Longleftrightarrow\exists(y,s):A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the lifted cone \(\widehat K=K\times\mathbb R_+\), lifted variable \(z=(x,\tau)\), and operator \(Bz=Ax+\tau r\). Then the auxiliary conic system is \(Bz=b\), \(z\in\widehat K\). It contains the known interior point \((e,1)\), because \(Ae+r=b\). Its zero-slice is \[\{(x,0)\in\widehat K:B(x,0)=b\}=\{(x,0):x\in K,\ Ax=b\}.\] Thus the original feasibility problem is represented exactly by the face \(\tau=0\) of the auxiliary product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift the original variable with a nonnegative residual scalar. The zero-scalar face of the augmented product cone reproduces exactly the original feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Status Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact status interpretation for an attained solution of the scalar-residual Phase-I model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Phase-I model \(\min\{\tau:Ax+\tau r=b,\ x\in K,\ \tau\geq0\}\), suppose an optimal solution \((x^*,\tau^*)\) is attained. If \(\tau^*=0\), then \(x^*\) is feasible for the original system. If \(\tau^*>0\), then the original system is infeasible. A barrier-compatible recovered point additionally requires \(x^*\in\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an attained Phase-I optimum, zero yields an original feasible point and a positive value establishes infeasibility. Strict interiority must be checked separately before barrier initialization.
assumptions_latex: The scalar-residual Phase-I problem is solved to an attained optimum \((x^*,\tau^*)\).

children.top_down_role: Degenerate auxiliary outcomes that do not yield usable interior starts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthant family attaining zero Phase-I value without an interior original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), \(A=I\), \(b=(0,1,\ldots,1)\), and \(e=(1,\ldots,1)\). With \(r=b-e=(-1,0,\ldots,0)\), the scalar-residual model \[x+\tau r=b,\qquad x\in K,\quad\tau\geq0\] has the interior reference point \((e,1)\) and attains minimum \(\tau^*=0\) at the unique original feasible point \(x=b\). Nevertheless, \(b\in\partial K\), so no zero-scale recovery lies in \(\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthant Phase-I model attains zero exactly, yet its unique recovered point lies on the cone boundary and cannot initialize an interior barrier method.
assumptions_latex: The Phase-I objective is to minimize \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau^*=0\text{ is attained, but }\{x:Ax=b\}\cap\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing.
review_flags: Distinct generalized family supplied because the immutable orthant seed remains deferred and is not regenerated.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Only Phase-I Recovery Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of one-sided Phase-I success to initialize a feasible-start primal-dual method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal strict feasibility and dual strict feasibility are independent requirements. A verified \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(Ax=b\) does not imply existence of \((y,s)\) with \(A^*y+s=c\) and \(s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and the converse implication also fails. One-sided recovery therefore does not initialize a method requiring both sides to be strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interior point recovered on only one side of a conic pair is insufficient for a feasible-start primal-dual barrier method.
assumptions_latex: The target method requires primal and dual strict feasibility.
Only one Phase-I procedure has returned a verified interior feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{One-sided strict feasibility}\not\Rightarrow\text{primal-dual strict feasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Recovery Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment boundary for exact Phase-I recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Phase-I infimum of zero yields an original feasible point only when a feasible auxiliary point with zero scale is attained. If feasible auxiliary points satisfy \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) but no point with \(\tau=0\) exists, the model provides arbitrarily small residuals but neither original feasibility nor an initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero Phase-I infimum does not recover feasibility unless a zero-scale optimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(\inf\tau=0\), but no feasible auxiliary point has \(\tau=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf\tau=0\not\Rightarrow\exists(x,0)\text{ feasible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonattainment at Zero Phase-I Value

assumptions_latex: Consider \(K=\mathbb R_+^2\) and the equality system \(x_1=0\), \(x_2=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system is feasible but has no point in \(\operatorname{int}K\); hence zero Phase-I value cannot guarantee a barrier-compatible initialization.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit orthant system directly verifies the boundary obstruction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between feasibility and strict feasibility in Phase-I recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+^2\) and impose \(x_1=0\), \(x_2=1\). The original conic system has the unique feasible point \(x=(0,1)\), but \(x\in\partial K\) and \(\operatorname{int}K\cap\{x:x_1=0,\ x_2=1\}=\varnothing\). Any exact Phase-I model representing original feasibility can attain auxiliary value zero at this point, yet no recovered point can satisfy \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\). Thus feasibility recovery alone cannot initialize a barrier method whose domain is \(\operatorname{int}K\); facial reduction or a relative-interior reformulation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible system may lie entirely on a cone face. Then Phase I reaches zero but cannot produce the strictly interior point required by a barrier method.
knowledge_statements.title: Initialization Failure Boundaries

children.title: Artificial-Interior-Point Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initialization through artificial variables and shifted residual systems.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual residuals are \(r_p=b-Ax^0\) and \(r_d=c-A^*y^0-s^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\tau=1\), the augmented system has the known interior point \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\); at \(\tau=0\), it reduces to the original primal-dual equations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-shift artificial initialization for a primal-dual conic system.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(s^0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and \(y^0\), and set \(r_p=b-Ax^0\) and \(r_d=c-A^*y^0-s^0\). Introduce \(\tau\geq0\) and solve the shifted system \[Ax+\tau r_p=b,\qquad A^*y+s+\tau r_d=c,\qquad x\in K,\quad s\in K^*.\] Initialize at \((x,y,s,\tau)=(x^0,y^0,s^0,1)\). Apply an interior-point continuation that drives \(\tau\) toward zero while preserving interiority. Stop when \(\tau\) and the original residuals meet tolerance; output \((x,y,s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Artificial residual shifts make arbitrary interior cone points satisfy an augmented system at scalar one. Driving the scalar to zero recovers the original primal-dual equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Interior-Point Initialization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status limitation of residual-shift initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\tau=0\), the shifted equations become the original primal and dual feasibility equations. A zero-scale endpoint is barrier-compatible only when the recovered cone variables lie in the required cone interiors or relative interiors. Failure to reach \(\tau=0\), or termination at \(\tau>0\), does not by itself certify infeasibility, weak infeasibility, or any other exact status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual shifting supplies an artificial interior start, but only a validated zero-scale endpoint recovers the original system; positive scale is not a status certificate.
assumptions_latex: The shifted equations are \(Ax+\tau r_p=b\) and \(A^*y+s+\tau r_d=c\).
The artificial point at \(\tau=1\) is interior in the cone variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau=0\Rightarrow Ax=b\text{ and }A^*y+s=c;\qquad \tau>0\text{ alone has no exact status implication.}
knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Shift Status Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal and Dual Condition Numbers of a Self-Dual Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines spectral condition measures over the primal and dual embedding solution sets and records their basic boundedness property and the known-bound boundary between LP and SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\widetilde Z\), define
\[
f(\widetilde Z):=\begin{cases}
\infty,&\widetilde Z=0,\\
\displaystyle\min_{i:\lambda_i(\widetilde Z)>0}\lambda_i(\widetilde Z),&\widetilde Z\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
The primal and dual condition numbers of the embedding are
\[
\sigma_P:=\sup_{\widetilde X\in\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{*}}f(\widetilde X),\qquad
\sigma_D:=\sup_{\widetilde S\in\widetilde{\mathcal D}^{*}}f(\widetilde S),
\]
and its condition number is \(\sigma:=\min\{\sigma_P,\sigma_D\}\). The boundedness of the self-dual embedding solution set implies \(0<\sigma<\infty\). In linear programming, \(\sigma\) has a positive lower bound in terms of the problem data; obtaining an analogous bound for semidefinite programming is open.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero embedding variable, f is its smallest positive eigenvalue, while f(0) is infinity. The primal and dual condition numbers are the suprema of f over their respective embedding solution sets, and the overall condition number is their minimum. It is positive and finite when the self-dual embedding solution set is bounded. A data-dependent positive lower bound is known for linear programming, while an analogous semidefinite bound is open.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde{\mathcal P}^{*}\text{ and }\widetilde{\mathcal D}^{*}\text{ are the primal and dual solution sets of the self-dual embedding}
\text{The self-dual embedding solution set is bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_P=\sup_{\widetilde X\in\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{*}}f(\widetilde X),\quad \sigma_D=\sup_{\widetilde S\in\widetilde{\mathcal D}^{*}}f(\widetilde S),\quad \sigma=\min\{\sigma_P,\sigma_D\},\quad 0<\sigma<\infty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invertibility and Positivity of Embedding Newton Factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the locally defined matrices \(E,F\), scaling matrix \(\widetilde P\), and symmetrization operator \(H_{\bar P}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde P\) be invertible and let \(\widetilde X,\widetilde S\) be symmetric positive definite. Then \(E\) and \(F\) are invertible. Moreover, if \(H_{\bar P}(\widetilde X\widetilde S)\succ0\), then \(\operatorname{sym}(E^{-1}F)\succ0\), where \(\operatorname{sym}(M)=(M+M^T)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the scaling matrix is invertible and the augmented primal and dual matrices are symmetric positive definite, then the associated matrices E and F are invertible. If the scaled symmetrization of their product is also positive definite, the symmetric part of E inverse F is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E,F\text{ are invertible, and }H_{\bar P}(\widetilde X\widetilde S)\succ0\implies\operatorname{sym}(E^{-1}F)\succ0.

children.title: Augmented Embedding Cone
children.top_down_role: Cone geometry of the embedding's enlarged variable space.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a regular cone and \(K^*\) is its dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The embedding variables lie in the augmented cone \(\mathcal C=K\times K^*\times\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R^m\), whose dual is \(\mathcal C^*=K^*\times K\times\mathbb R_+^2\times\{0\}\) under the product pairing.

notation.meaning: primal variable, dual slack, and free multiplier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-cone geometry for primal, dual-slack, homogeneous, status, and free embedding variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a conic primal-dual pair over \(K\) and \(K^*\), define the augmented embedding cone by \[\mathcal C=K\times K^*\times\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R^m.\] An embedding vector is \(z=(x,s,\tau,\kappa,y)\in\mathcal C\), where \(x\) and \(s\) are the primal and dual-slack variables, \(\tau\) is the homogenizing scalar, \(\kappa\) is the status scalar, and \(y\) is free. Under the standard product pairing, \(\mathcal C^*=K^*\times K\times\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_+\times\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The embedding uses the product of the primal cone, dual cone, two nonnegative scalar cones, and a free multiplier space; its dual swaps the cone factors.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Embedding Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior and Lineality of the Augmented Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior and pointedness properties of the product cone containing the embedding variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a finite-dimensional regular cone and let \(\mathcal C=K\times K^*\times\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R^m\). Then \[\operatorname{int}\mathcal C=\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*\times\mathbb R_{++}^2\times\mathbb R^m.\] Thus \(\mathcal C\) is closed, convex, and full-dimensional. Its lineality space is \[\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal C)=\{0\}\times\{0\}\times\{0\}^2\times\mathbb R^m.\] Consequently, when \(m>0\), the free multiplier factor makes \(\mathcal C\) nonpointed, so \(\mathcal C\) is not itself a regular cone under the convention that regular cones are pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented cone has the expected product interior, but its free multiplier factor creates lineality; it is therefore generally not pointed or regular despite the regularity of K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{int}\mathcal C=\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*\times\mathbb R_{++}^2\times\mathbb R^m\) and \(\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal C)=\{0\}\times\{0\}\times\{0\}^2\times\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: lineality space of the augmented cone

children.title: Homogeneous Embedding Geometry
children.top_down_role: Scaling structure induced by homogeneous augmentation.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Embedding Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive homogeneity of the standard primal-dual homogeneous self-dual status embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the homogeneous equations \[Ax-b\tau=0,\qquad A^*y+s-c\tau=0,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle-\langle c,x\rangle-\kappa=0,\] with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\tau,\kappa\geq0\). Their feasible set is a cone: for every feasible \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) and every \(\lambda\geq0\), the scaled tuple \(\lambda(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) is feasible. A solution with \(\tau>0\) normalizes to an optimal primal-dual solution, while a solution with \(\kappa>0\) has \(\tau=0\) and may encode a primal or dual status certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous self-dual equations and cone constraints are invariant under nonnegative scaling. Positive homogenizing scalar permits normalization to an optimal primal-dual solution, while positive status scalar belongs to the zero-homogenizing certificate case.
assumptions_latex: The original pair is \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The embedding feasible set is a cone: if \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) is feasible, then \(\lambda(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) is feasible for every \(\lambda\geq0\).

children.title: Self-Dual System Structure
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual symmetry within the embedded conic system.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Dual System Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual coupling and the complementarity identity in the standard homogeneous self-dual embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogeneous self-dual system is \[Ax=b\tau,\qquad A^*y+s=c\tau,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle-angle c,x\rangle=\kappa,\] together with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\tau,\kappa\geq0\). Every feasible tuple satisfies \[\langle x,s\rangle+\tau\kappa=0.\] Hence \(\langle x,s\rangle=0\) and \(\tau\kappa=0\). The cases \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa>0\) therefore correspond respectively to primal-dual solution normalization and the zero-homogenizing status regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous self-dual equations couple the primal and dual systems through a zero-sum complementarity identity. Nonnegativity forces both primal-dual complementarity and the product of the homogenizing and status scalars to vanish.
assumptions_latex: \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfies the displayed homogeneous self-dual equations with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\tau,\kappa\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system satisfies \(\langle x,s\rangle+\tau\kappa=0\), and consequently \(\langle x,s\rangle=0\) and \(\tau\kappa=0\).

notation.meaning: primal cone variable and dual slack

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-operator form exhibiting the algebraic primal-dual symmetry of the homogeneous system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u=(x,y,\tau)\in E\times Y\times\mathbb R\) and define \[Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&A^*&-c\\-A&0&b\\c^*&-b^*&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Under the product inner product, \(Q^*=-Q\). The equations \(Ax=b\tau\), \(A^*y+s=c\tau\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle-\langle c,x\rangle=\kappa\) are equivalently \[Qu+(s,0,\kappa)=0,\qquad u\in K\times Y\times\mathbb R_+,\quad (s,0,\kappa)\in K^*\times\{0\}\times\mathbb R_+.\] This skew-adjoint conic inclusion is the algebraic self-dual representation for the displayed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous primal-dual equations combine into one conic inclusion with a skew-adjoint block operator.
assumptions_latex: The homogeneous equations use the displayed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q^*=-Q\) and the homogeneous system is equivalent to \(Qu+(s,0,\kappa)=0\) with the stated cone memberships.

notation.meaning: grouped primal, multiplier, and homogenizing variables

children.top_down_role: Variants or degeneracies lacking exact self-dual organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding Symmetry Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes algebraic self-duality of an embedding from symmetric-cone scaling geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and \(K^*\) its dual. A homogeneous embedding over factors derived from \(K\) and \(K^*\) may be algebraically self-dual because its augmented linear operator is skew-adjoint. This property does not imply that \(K\) is a symmetric cone or that the embedding admits Nesterov--Todd scaling, self-scaled-barrier identities, or symmetric-cone neighborhood formulas. Those constructions require additional cone and barrier structure that must be established separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Algebraic self-duality of a homogeneous embedding does not by itself supply symmetric-cone scaling. Nesterov--Todd scaling and symmetric-cone neighborhood formulas require additional cone and barrier structure.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
The augmented embedding operator is skew-adjoint under the selected product-space inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Algebraic self-duality of the embedding does not imply symmetric-cone scaling geometry on \(K\).
review_flags: boundary between algebraic and cone symmetry should be checked against the source convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete witness that algebraic homogeneous self-dual embedding does not require a symmetric underlying cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K_{\exp}\) be the exponential cone. It is a regular closed convex cone but is not symmetric. A homogeneous primal-dual embedding can nevertheless be formed using the paired factors \(K_{\exp}\) and \(K_{\exp}^*\) and a skew-adjoint augmented operator. Hence existence of an algebraically self-dual homogeneous embedding does not imply that the underlying cone is symmetric or admits classical Nesterov--Todd scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential cone supports the usual paired-cone homogeneous embedding although it is not symmetric, refuting any implication from embedding self-duality to symmetric-cone geometry.
assumptions_latex: The embedding uses separate primal and dual cone factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{algebraically self-dual embedding}\not\Rightarrow\text{symmetric underlying cone}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric-Cone Embedding Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates skew-adjoint primal-dual coupling from literal equality of the augmented cone with its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal C=K\times K^*\times\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R^m\), the product-pairing dual is \(\mathcal C^*=K^*\times K\times\mathbb R_+^2\times\{0\}\). Thus paired factors \(K\) and \(K^*\), factor swapping, or a skew-adjoint embedding operator do not imply \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C^*\) under the identity map. The free factor dualizes to its annihilator, and identifying the first two factors additionally requires a specified self-dual identification of \(K\). The term homogeneous self-dual describes the coupled primal-dual construction, not automatic self-duality of every displayed cone factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-duality of the coupled embedding system is distinct from literal self-duality of its augmented product cone.
assumptions_latex: Duals are taken under the stated product-space pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Algebraic self-duality of the embedding does not imply \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C^*\) or \(K=K^*\).

notation.meaning: dual of the augmented product cone

knowledge_statements.title: System Self-Duality Versus Cone Self-Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-explicit infeasible-start trajectory for a skew homogeneous embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q^*=-Q\), choose \(z^0\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal C\), \(w^0\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal C^*\), and \(\mu_0>0\) with \(w^0=-\mu_0\nabla F(z^0)\), and set \(r^0=Qz^0-w^0\). The initial pair satisfies the system at \(\mu_0\), and the affine residual tends to zero if such path points exist as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

Embedded Central Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central trajectory for a homogeneous embedding over an augmented cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the augmented embedding cone, let \(F\) be a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}\mathcal C\), and let \(Q\) be the embedding's skew-adjoint linear operator. For \(\mu>0\), an embedded central point is a pair \((z,w)\) satisfying \(z\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal C\), \(w\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal C^*\), \(w=Qz\), and \(w=-\mu\nabla F(z)\). The embedded central path is the set of these points indexed by \(\mu\), whenever they exist; its limit as \(\mu\downarrow0\) approaches complementary embedded solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The embedded central path consists of strictly interior embedding points satisfying the linear embedding equations and barrier complementarity at parameter μ.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P=\{(z,w,\mu):\mu>0,\ z\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal C,\ w=Qz=-\mu\nabla F(z)\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic reduction of NT centrality distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local contraction bound for the centrality distance after a full feasible NT step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After a full feasible NT step, if the pre-step distance is \(0\le\delta<1\), then
\[
\delta^+\le \frac{\delta^2}{\sqrt{2(1-\delta^2)}}.
\]
In particular, if \(\delta\le 1/\sqrt2\), then \(\delta^+\le\delta^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a full feasible NT step, the new centrality distance is bounded by δ squared divided by the square root of 2(1−δ²). Consequently, within radius 1/√2 the distance decreases at least quadratically.
assumptions_latex: \text{A full feasible NT step is taken}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta^+\le\frac{\delta^2}{\sqrt{2(1-\delta^2)}},\qquad \delta\le\frac1{\sqrt2}\Longrightarrow\delta^+\le\delta^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility condition for a full embedded NT step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A central-neighborhood condition guaranteeing strict feasibility and the target complementarity gap after a full NT step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\widetilde X,\widetilde S)\) be a feasible embedded primal-dual pair and set \(\delta=\delta(\widetilde X,\widetilde S,\mu)\). If \(\delta<1\), then the full NT update \((\widetilde X+\Delta\widetilde X,\widetilde S+\Delta\widetilde S)\) is strictly feasible and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((\widetilde X+\Delta\widetilde X)(\widetilde S+\Delta\widetilde S)\right)=\widetilde n\mu.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the embedded primal-dual pair has NT centrality distance less than one, its full NT update remains strictly feasible and attains the target duality gap n-tilde times μ.
assumptions_latex: (\widetilde X,\widetilde S)\text{ is a feasible embedded primal-dual pair}
(\Delta\widetilde X,\Delta\widetilde S)\text{ is the full NT step at parameter }\mu
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widetilde X+\Delta\widetilde X,\widetilde S+\Delta\widetilde S)\text{ is strictly feasible},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((\widetilde X+\Delta\widetilde X)(\widetilde S+\Delta\widetilde S)\right)=\widetilde n\mu.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Central Path of the Self-Dual Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the embedded central path using block-augmented primal and dual variables and the embedding constraints denoted by (5.3.5).

Equivalently, its relaxed complementarity equations are \(XS=\mu I\), \(\tau\rho=\mu\), and \(\nu\vartheta=\mu\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widetilde X(\mu),\widetilde S(\mu))\text{ is the unique solution of (5.3.5) and }\widetilde X\widetilde S=\mu I.

children.title: Primal Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Extraction of primal solution candidates from embedded variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dehomogenization of a positive-scale embedding point into a primal conic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), take an embedded point containing \((x,\tau)\) with \(x\in K\), \(\tau>0\), and primal residual \(r_p=Ax-b\tau\). Output \(\widehat x=x/\tau\). Then \(\widehat x\in K\) and \(A\widehat x-b=r_p/\tau\). Stop with a recovered primal solution when the chosen scaled feasibility test, for example \(\|r_p\|/\tau\leq\varepsilon_p\), is satisfied; otherwise report that primal recovery has not yet been certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide the embedded primal variable by a positive homogeneous scale. Its feasibility residual is the embedded residual divided by that scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x=x/\tau\in K\) and \(A\widehat x-b=(Ax-b\tau)/\tau\).

children.title: Dual Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Extraction of dual solution candidates from embedded variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dehomogenization of positive-scale dual embedding variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual problem \(\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), take embedded variables \((y,s,\tau)\) with \(s\in K^*\), \(\tau>0\), and dual residual \(r_d=A^*y+s-c\tau\). Output \(\widehat y=y/\tau\) and \(\widehat s=s/\tau\). Then \(\widehat s\in K^*\) and \(A^*\widehat y+\widehat s-c=r_d/\tau\). Accept dual recovery when the selected scaled residual test is met; otherwise return no certified dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide embedded dual variables by the positive homogeneous scale; the resulting dual residual is scaled by the same factor.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(s\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat s=s/\tau\in K^*\) and \(A^*\widehat y+\widehat s-c=(A^*y+s-c\tau)/\tau\).

children.title: Optimality Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of embedded evidence supporting approximate optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate obtained by dehomogenizing a positive-scale embedded primal-dual point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given embedded variables \((x,y,s,\tau)\) with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\tau>0\), define \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)=(x,y,s)/\tau\). The tuple is an exact optimality certificate when \(A\widehat x=b\), \(A^*\widehat y+\widehat s=c\), and \(\langle\widehat x,\widehat s\rangle=0\). It is an \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g)\)-certificate when the chosen normalized primal residual, dual residual, and nonnegative complementarity gap do not exceed those tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-scale dehomogenization yields an optimality certificate when primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity are exact or within stated tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Weak duality holds for the displayed primal-dual conic pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact feasibility and \(\langle\widehat x,\widehat s\rangle=0\) certify primal-dual optimality and equality of objective values.
review_flags: normalization convention for approximate residuals must be fixed by an implementation profile

children.title: Infeasibility Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of alternative-system evidence for infeasible statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of alternative-system certificates from a vanishing-scale embedding solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\), let \(b\in Y\), let \(c\in X\), and let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone. Suppose a terminal embedding point has homogeneous scale \(\tau=0\). If its alternative component \(y\in Y\) satisfies \(-A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\), output \(\bar y=y/\langle b,y\rangle\); then \(-A^*\bar y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,\bar y\rangle=1\), which certifies primal infeasibility. If its alternative component \(x\in K\) satisfies \(Ax=0\) and \(\langle c,x\rangle<0\), output \(\bar x=x/(-\langle c,x\rangle)\); then \(A\bar x=0\), \(\bar x\in K\), and \(\langle c,\bar x\rangle=-1\), which certifies dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero homogeneous scale, normalize a valid alternative-system component to obtain a directly checkable certificate of primal or dual infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
The terminal embedding point has \(\tau=0\) and contains a component satisfying one of the displayed alternative systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized \(\bar y\) or \(\bar x\) is a directly checkable conic infeasibility certificate.

children.title: Ambiguous Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Embedded outcomes lacking stable solution or certificate classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cases where embedding variables cannot be stably classified as solutions or certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an approximate embedding point contain nonnegative scales \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\). Stable solution recovery requires \(\tau\) to be safely positive relative to data and residual tolerances, while stable alternative-certificate recovery requires \(\kappa\) and the relevant normalizing functional to be safely positive. If both scales are below their classification thresholds, or if dehomogenization amplifies residuals beyond acceptance tolerances, neither status follows. In particular, \(\tau\approx0\) and \(\kappa\approx0\) is an ambiguous regime associated with numerical degeneracy or proximity to an ill-posed status boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When neither solution scale nor certificate scale is reliably positive, dehomogenization cannot certify optimality or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The embedding point is approximate and tested using fixed positive numerical tolerances.
Recovered objects must pass independent residual and cone-membership checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If neither \(\tau\) nor \(\kappa\) supports a validated normalization, the correct recovery status is indeterminate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative instability of solution recovery when the homogeneous normalization scale is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\tau>0\), \(x=\bar x/\tau\), and \(A\bar x-b\tau=r_p\). Then \[Ax-b=\frac{r_p}{\tau},\qquad \|Ax-b\|=\frac{\|r_p\|}{\tau}.\] Analogous identities hold for dual affine residuals. Thus \(\|r_p\|\le\varepsilon\) yields only \(\|Ax-b\|\le\varepsilon/\tau\). This is sharp: for \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), choosing \(\tau_k=\varepsilon_k^2\) and \(\|r_{p,k}\|=\varepsilon_k\) gives vanishing embedded residual but recovered residual norm \(1/\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dehomogenization divides embedded residuals by the recovery scale, so a small scale can amplify vanishing embedded error into an unbounded recovered residual.
assumptions_latex: The embedded affine residual is \(r_p=A\bar x-b\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stable recovered affine accuracy requires embedded error to be small relative to \(\tau\); no uniform bound exists as \(\tau\downarrow0\).
review_flags: This is a residual-transfer identity and sharp instability family, not a solver convergence theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Homogeneous Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding construction that admits a strictly interior initialization without original feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given conic data \((A,b,c,K)\), choose arbitrary interior trial points \(x^0\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(s^0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), a vector \(y^0\), and positive homogeneous coordinates \(\tau^0,\kappa^0\). Form an augmented homogeneous system by adding residual offsets chosen so that \((x^0,y^0,s^0,\tau^0,\kappa^0)\) satisfies the embedding equations exactly. Apply a primal-dual path-following method to drive the offsets' associated homogenizing contribution to zero. A limit with \(\tau>0\) is dehomogenized into solutions; a limit with \(\tau=0\) and a valid alternative component is normalized into a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual offsets embed arbitrary interior trial points, allowing path following without primal or dual feasibility of the original problem.
assumptions_latex: The augmented system preserves homogeneity and the required primal-dual barrier structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialization of the embedding does not require \(Ax^0=b\) or \(A^*y^0+s^0=c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Lagrange–Slater Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmented embeddings intended to expose feasibility and duality irregularities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended Lagrange--Slater embedding represents a conic primal-dual system in a larger homogeneous conic space by adjoining variables and equations for feasibility residuals, objective-gap balance, and strict-feasibility diagnostics. Its intended terminal alternatives are: a positive homogenizing scale yielding a primal-dual solution after normalization; a nonzero alternative-system component yielding an infeasibility certificate; or an auxiliary degeneracy component indicating failure of the usual Slater-based dichotomy. The exact augmented cone and equations must be specified before these alternatives constitute a formal exhaustive theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extension adds homogeneous diagnostic variables so solutions, infeasibility certificates, and Slater-related degeneracy can be represented in one system.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a finite-dimensional conic primal-dual pair.
The extension explicitly identifies its augmented cone, linear equations, and normalization map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mathematically complete status representation requires the variant-specific augmented system and an exhaustive alternative theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric-Cone Homogeneous Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous embedding architecture using primal and dual barrier oracles without symmetric scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a proper cone, not necessarily symmetric, equipped with a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier \(F\), and let \(K^*\) admit a compatible dual-barrier oracle. A homogeneous embedding may retain its linear skew-adjoint status system and positive scaling coordinates while replacing symmetric-cone scaling equations by relations based on \(\nabla F\), \(\nabla^2F\), or conjugate-barrier evaluations. The embedding's solution and alternative-certificate normalizations remain algebraic, but neighborhood definitions and Newton systems must use the selected nonsymmetric barrier geometry rather than a cone automorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogeneous embeddings extend to nonsymmetric cones by using primal and dual barrier oracles instead of symmetric-cone scaling automorphisms.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a proper cone with a computable logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier.
Required primal and dual barrier derivatives can be evaluated on interior points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Self-dual linear embedding structure can be separated from, and implemented without, symmetric-cone scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Optimality Certificate Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based interface for validating an approximately optimal conic primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(\max\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), a reported tuple \((x,y,s)\) is an \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g)\)-optimality certificate if cone membership is verified to the declared tolerance and \(\|Ax-b\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\|A^*y+s-c\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), and \(0\leq\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle\leq\varepsilon_g\). The interface must state the norm, data scaling, and cone-membership tolerance used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate optimality certificate reports primal and dual residuals, cone membership, and a nonnegative duality gap under explicit tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(K^*\) is its dual.
The norm and all absolute or relative scaling conventions are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing all stated tests certifies approximate primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and weak-duality-consistent objective agreement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Predicate versus Exact Optimality Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limit of a residual-based optimality interface without an a posteriori error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Passing positive-tolerance tests for affine residuals, cone-distance residuals, and objective gap establishes only the declared approximate predicates. Unless an error-bound or conditioning theorem converts those residuals into exact or nearby exact primal-dual feasible points, the tuple need not yield rigorous bounds on the exact optimal value or its distance to the exact solution set. If primal and dual feasibility are exact, weak duality gives \(\langle b,y\rangle\le p^*\le\langle c,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual acceptance is an approximate certificate; exact-value or solution-distance guarantees require exact feasibility or an additional error-bound theorem.
assumptions_latex: The conic primal-dual pair and residual conventions are declared.
At least one feasibility predicate may use a positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive-tolerance acceptance alone does not imply an exact optimal-value bracket, whereas exact compatible feasibility does.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic Farkas certificate for infeasibility of primal equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\), let \(b\in Y\), and let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone. For the feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), a vector \(y\in Y\) is a primal infeasibility certificate if \(-A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\). Such a certificate may be normalized so that \(\langle b,y\rangle=1\). These conditions imply infeasibility; a converse existence claim additionally requires the applicable conic-alternative or closedness hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector whose adjoint image has the required dual-cone sign and whose pairing with the right-hand side is positive certifies that the primal conic equality system is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(-A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\), then \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong alternative-system certificate for the standard finite-dimensional conic primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(d\in K\) satisfying \(Ad=0\) and \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\) is an exactly checkable certificate that the dual constraint system \(A^*y+s=c\), \(s\in K^*\), is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-cone direction in the nullspace of the constraints with negative objective pairing certifies infeasibility of the dual constraints.
assumptions_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear, and let \(b\in F\) and \(c\in E\).
Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*\).
The primal-dual pair is \(\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\).
A proposed vector \(d\in E\) satisfies \(d\in K\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual conic problem is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ray certificate for unboundedness of a minimization-form conic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x_0,d)\) satisfying \(x_0,d\in K\), \(Ax_0=b\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\) is an exactly checkable certificate of primal unboundedness. Its certified feasible ray is \(x(t)=x_0+td\) for \(t\ge 0\), with \(\langle c,x(t)\rangle\to-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point together with a cone direction in the constraint nullspace having negative cost certifies a feasible ray whose objective tends to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear, and let \(b\in F\) and \(c\in E\).
Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and consider \(\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\).
There exist \(x_0,d\in E\) such that \(x_0,d\in K\), \(Ax_0=b\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible ray \(x(t)=x_0+td\) satisfies \(\langle c,x(t)\rangle\to-\infty\), so the primal optimal value is \(-\infty\).

Its certified feasible ray is \((y_0+th,s_0+tq)\) for \(t\ge0\), with objective tending to \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual feasible point together with a homogeneous dual-cone direction having positive objective pairing certifies a dual feasible ray of unbounded value.
assumptions_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear, and let \(b\in F\) and \(c\in E\).

children.title: Certificate Validation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical or geometric regimes weakening certificate reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Validation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact mathematical certificates and tolerance-based numerical evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a specified tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), conditions such as \(\|Ad\|\le\varepsilon\) or \(\operatorname{dist}(d,K)\le\varepsilon\) do not, when \(\varepsilon>0\), imply the exact predicates \(Ad=0\) or \(d\in K\). Likewise, a non-strict or uncertified sign test does not imply the strict improving inequality required by an exact alternative-system certificate. Such tests certify only the declared tolerance-based status unless verified error bounds restore all exact predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive residual tolerances and uncertified sign tests do not by themselves prove exact infeasibility or unboundedness; they validate only the declared numerical status unless error bounds recover the exact predicates.
assumptions_latex: The exact conic model is \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), \(A^*y+s=c\), and \(s\in K^*\).
A norm \(\|\cdot\|\), its induced distance, and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are fixed.
Exact status certificates require exact equalities, exact cone membership, and the applicable strict sign condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only satisfaction of the exact alternative-system predicates validates an exact status certificate; positive-tolerance tests establish at most a tolerance-dependent numerical status unless certified error bounds imply the exact predicates.

notation.meaning: Norm used to measure numerical residuals.
