knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Validation of a Reconstructed Polyhedral Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational reconstruction followed by exact validation for a rational polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given floating candidates, reconstruct bounded-denominator rational values \((\bar x,\bar y,\lambda)\), set \(\bar s=G^{\mathsf T}\lambda\), clear denominators, and verify exactly \[A\bar x=b,\quad G\bar x\geq0,\quad \lambda\geq0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}\bar y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c.\] Compute \(g=c^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b^{\mathsf T}\bar y\) exactly and accept only if \(0\leq g\leq\varepsilon\). If reconstruction or any predicate fails, return \(\text{not certified}\), which makes no assertion about the optimization status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct rational candidates and accept only after exact verification of every affine, cone, dual, and gap predicate.
assumptions_latex: A denominator bound and deterministic reconstruction policy are declared.
The cone is rational polyhedral in the displayed representation.
Exact integer arithmetic is available for validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns a valid exact certificate or the noncommittal result not certified.}
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Validation of a Reconstructed Polyhedral Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Rational Certificate for Polyhedral Conic Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly checkable epsilon-optimality predicate for a rational inequality-represented polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Gx\geq0\}\) with rational \(A,b,c,G\), and consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). A rational tuple \((\bar x,\bar y,\lambda)\) is an exact \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate if \[A\bar x=b,\quad G\bar x\geq0,\quad \lambda\geq0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}\bar y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c,\] and \[0\leq c^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=\bar x^{\mathsf T}G^{\mathsf T}\lambda\leq\varepsilon.\] Every predicate is decidable by integer arithmetic after denominators are cleared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rational polyhedral cones, exact primal feasibility, an explicit nonnegative representation of the dual slack, and a small exact gap certify epsilon optimality.
assumptions_latex: All data and certificate entries are rational and binary encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^{\mathsf T}\bar y\leq p^*\leq c^{\mathsf T}\bar x,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b^{\mathsf T}\bar y\leq\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative rational representation of the dual slack

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Certificate for Polyhedral Conic Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Small Residual without Exact Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational one-dimensional family separating residual acceptance from certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every integer \(N\geq1\), consider \[x\geq0,\qquad x=-2^{-N}.\] This system is infeasible, but \(\hat x=0\) satisfies cone membership exactly and has equality residual \(2^{-N}\). Hence every positive residual tolerance accepts such an infeasible instance for sufficiently large \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible rational system can have an exactly cone-feasible candidate with arbitrarily small equality residual.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility is accepted solely from cone membership and a positive unvalidated equality-residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Small Residual without Exact Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Rational Certificate for Second-Order Cone Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly checkable epsilon-optimality predicate for rational products of Lorentz cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Lorentz cone \(\mathcal L_m=\{(t,u)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{m-1}:t\ge\|u\|_2\}\), rational membership is exactly equivalent to \[t\ge0,\qquad t^2-u^{\mathsf T}u\ge0.\] Consequently, for a rational primal-dual conic pair over a product of Lorentz cones, a rational primal-dual-slack tuple is an exact \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate when all affine equations hold exactly, every primal and slack block satisfies these two rational inequalities, and the exact primal-dual gap lies in \([0,\varepsilon]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lorentz-cone membership and a second-order-cone epsilon-optimality certificate can be checked exactly using rational inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Problem data, certificate entries, and \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are rational.
The cone is represented as a finite product of Lorentz cones.
Exact integer arithmetic is used after denominators are cleared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact primal and dual feasibility together with gap at most }\varepsilon\text{ certifies }\varepsilon\text{-optimality.}
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Certificate for Second-Order Cone Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Rational Certificate for Semidefinite Conic Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly checkable epsilon-optimality predicate for rational standard-form semidefinite data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:\mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ S\succeq0\},\] with rational data. A rational tuple \((\bar X,\bar y,\bar S)\) is an exact \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate when all affine equalities hold exactly, \(\bar X\succeq0\), \(\bar S\succeq0\), and \[0\le \langle C,\bar X\rangle-b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=\langle\bar X,\bar S\rangle\le\varepsilon.\] For rational symmetric matrices, positive semidefiniteness is exactly decidable, for example by verifying that every principal minor is nonnegative after denominators are cleared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational affine identities, PSD membership, and a rational primal-dual gap at most epsilon certify semidefinite epsilon optimality.
assumptions_latex: All problem and certificate entries are rational.
Exact integer arithmetic is used after denominators are cleared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^{\mathsf T}\bar y\le p^*\le\langle C,\bar X\rangle,\qquad \langle C,\bar X\rangle-b^{\mathsf T}\bar y\le\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the rational equality map

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Certificate for Semidefinite Conic Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative enclosure-based validation of a candidate conic primal-dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given outward-rounded enclosures \([x],[y],[s]\), compute rigorous enclosures of \(A[x]-b\), \(A^*[y]+[s]-c\), the cone-membership predicates, and the primal-dual gap. Return \(\varepsilon\)-certified only if both affine-residual enclosures equal \(\{0\}\), every point of \([x]\) lies in \(K\), every point of \([s]\) lies in \(K^*\), and the gap enclosure is contained in \([0,\varepsilon]\). Return \(\mathrm{not\ certified}\) whenever any required inclusion is unproved. Cone-membership inclusion tests must be supplied for the particular cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward interval validation certifies only when every affine, cone-membership, and gap inclusion is rigorously established; otherwise it returns no certificate.
assumptions_latex: All interval operations are outward rounded.
Rigorous inclusion tests are available for the selected primal and dual cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{certified}\Longrightarrow A x=b,\ A^*y+s=c,\ x\in K,\ s\in K^*,\ 0\leq\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle\leq\varepsilon\ \text{for every enclosed tuple}.
knowledge_statements.title: Outward-Interval Primal-Dual Validation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Bit Complexity of Standard Rational Certificate Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation cost for an explicitly supplied rational certificate over polyhedral, Lorentz, or positive-semidefinite cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the total number of binary-encoded scalar entries in a rational conic instance and a supplied rational primal-dual certificate, and let \(L\) bound their encoding lengths. For products of rational polyhedral cones, Lorentz cones, and rational positive-semidefinite cones, exact affine identities, cone membership, and the rational primal-dual gap can be validated using \(\operatorname{poly}(S,L)\) bit operations. Polyhedral predicates reduce to rational linear arithmetic, Lorentz membership to rational quadratic inequalities, and rational PSD membership to exact polynomial-time inertia or sign computation. The bound concerns validation of the supplied tuple, not finding it or bounding the size of a certificate that must exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supplied rational certificates for standard polyhedral, second-order, and semidefinite cone blocks can be validated in polynomial bit complexity in their combined encoding length.
assumptions_latex: All instance and certificate entries are binary-encoded rationals.
Cone blocks are rational polyhedral, Lorentz, or positive-semidefinite blocks.
Exact integer or rational arithmetic is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{bitcost}(\operatorname{validate})\leq\operatorname{poly}(S,L).

notation.meaning: Maximum binary encoding length of an entry

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Bit Complexity of Standard Rational Certificate Validation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness Radius for Bounded-Denominator Rational Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient precision threshold for unique reconstruction of a rational certificate component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\geq1\). If \(a/b\) is reduced, \(1\leq b\leq B\), and \[\left|\widehat q-\frac ab\right|<\frac{1}{2B^2},\] then \(a/b\) is the unique rational with denominator at most \(B\) lying within \(1/(2B^2)\) of \(\widehat q\). Reconstruction inside this radius is unambiguous, but the reconstructed certificate must still pass exact validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A denominator-bounded rational component is uniquely reconstructible when its approximation error is strictly below one over twice the squared denominator bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left|\widehat q-a/b\right|<1/(2B^2)\Longrightarrow a/b\text{ is the unique denominator-}\leq B\text{ candidate in that radius}.

A finite-precision output is a certified \(\varepsilon\)-solution when it yields exactly checkable data \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) satisfying
\[
A\bar x=b,
cua d
A^*\bar y+bar s=c,
cua d
\bar x\in K,
cua d
\bar s\in K^*,

and
\[
0\le\langle c,\bar x\rangle-langle b,\bar y\rangle
=langle\bar x,ar s\rangle\le\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^*\succ0\), let \(A\) have full row rank, and let \(r_d\) and \(r_p\) be the residual right-hand sides. The augmented KKT representation
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
H&A^*\\
A&0
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
\Delta x\\
\Delta y
\end{pmatrix}
=-\begin{pmatrix}
r_d\\
r_p
\end{pmatrix}
\]
is equivalent to the Schur-complement representation
\[
(AH^{-1}A^*)\Delta y=r_p-AH^{-1}r_d,
\qquad
\Delta x=-H^{-1}(r_d+A^*\Delta y).
\]
The matrix \(AH^{-1}A^*\) is positive definite, so both representations determine a unique pair \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric augmented KKT system is equivalently represented by a positive-definite multiplier Schur-complement equation followed by primal-step recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented KKT Representations

Let
\[
K_{\mathrm{KKT}}=
\begin{pmatrix}
H&A^*\\
A&0
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(H=H^*\succ0\) acts on an \(n\)-dimensional space and \(A\) has \(m\) linearly independent rows. Then
\[
\operatorname{inertia}(K_{\mathrm{KKT}})=(n,m,0).
\]
Consequently, \(K_{\mathrm{KKT}}\) is nonsingular and, when \(m>0\), indefinite.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\). For unknowns \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\), the variable-retaining saddle-point Newton system is \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{pmatrix}.\] It represents the coupled equations \(H\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=r_d\) and \(A\Delta x=r_p\) without eliminating either variable. If \(A\) has full row rank, the coefficient matrix is nonsingular, so the retained formulation uniquely determines \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented KKT system retains primal and multiplier directions together; positive-definite primal scaling and full row rank make the coupled system uniquely solvable.
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Variable-Retention Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\). For unknowns \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\), consider the KKT equations \(H\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=r_d\) and \(A\Delta x=r_p\). Elimination gives \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y)\) and hence \[AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=AH^{-1}r_d-r_p.\] If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(N=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\). Solving this positive-definite normal equation and back-substituting for \(\Delta x\) yields exactly the solution of the original KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal direction produces a positive-definite multiplier-space normal equation; back-substitution recovers the same KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Reductions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning intrinsic to the positive-definite normal-equation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and set \(B=AH^{-1/2}\). Then \(N=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=BB^{\mathsf T}\), so \(\lambda_i(N)=\sigma_i(B)^2\) and \(\kappa_2(N)=\kappa_2(B)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-equation matrix is a Gram matrix, so its eigenvalues and condition number are the squares of the scaled constraint operator's singular values and condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})=\sigma_i(AH^{-1/2})^2\) and \(\kappa_2(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})=\kappa_2(AH^{-1/2})^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Gram Spectrum and Squared Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(D\in\mathbb S_{+}^{m}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\). For unknowns \(u\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^m\), consider \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-D\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}b\\c\end{pmatrix}.\] Eliminating \(u=H^{-1}(b-A^{\mathsf T}v)\) gives the Schur system \[(D+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})v=AH^{-1}b-c.\] If \(D+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite, this reduced system has a unique solution, and back-substitution gives the unique solution of the augmented system. Full row rank of \(A\) is sufficient for positive definiteness even when \(D=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block elimination converts a regularized KKT system into a multiplier-space Schur system, with exact recovery of the eliminated variable by back-substitution.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Reductions

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-definiteness boundary for the regularized multiplier-space Schur matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), \(D\in\mathbb S_{+}^{m}\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). For \(S=D+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), \[\ker S=\ker D\cap\ker A^{\mathsf T}.\] Therefore \(S\succ0\) if and only if \(\ker D\cap\ker A^{\mathsf T}=\{0\}\). Full row rank of \(A\) is sufficient but is unnecessary when \(D\) is positive on every nonzero direction in \(\ker A^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized Schur matrix is positive definite exactly when no nonzero multiplier direction is annihilated by both the regularization and the constraint transpose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\iff\ker D\cap\ker A^{\mathsf T}=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Schur Nonsingularity Criterion

children.title: Elimination-Order Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Effects of variable-elimination order on reduced-system size, density, and conditioning.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is the nonsingular block selected for elimination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|H^{-1}e\|_2\leq\lambda_{\min}(H)^{-1}\|e\|_2\quad(H\succ0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity introduced by applying the selected pivot inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An error \(e\) passed through an eliminated nonsingular block satisfies \(\|H^{-1}e\|\leq\|H^{-1}\|\|e\|\). For \(H\succ0\), \(\|H^{-1}\|_2=1/\lambda_{\min}(H)\), so inverse-application sensitivity becomes unbounded as \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating through a nearly singular pivot amplifies solve errors according to the pivot inverse norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Eliminated-Pivot Error Amplification

assumptions_latex: The coefficients and factor structures remain unchanged for all \(q\) solves.
All material formation, factorization, and solve costs are included in \(C_i,T_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1+qT_1<C_2+qT_2\iff\text{choice 1 has lower modeled total work}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized elimination-order selection for repeated right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For elimination choices \(i=1,2\), let \(C_i\) be setup work and \(T_i\) the work per subsequent solve. For \(q\) right-hand sides with unchanged coefficients, choice 1 has lower modeled work exactly when \(C_1+qT_1<C_2+qT_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expensive elimination setup can be preferable when reused factors make subsequent solves sufficiently cheaper.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Solve Elimination Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Equivalence and Cost Tradeoff of Elimination Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution equivalence and implementation criteria for admissible two-block elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a selected pivot and its Schur complement are nonsingular, solving the reduced system and back-substituting yields the unique solution of the full block system. Either admissible order therefore gives the same exact solution. Computational preference depends jointly on reduced order, complement-formation and inverse-application costs, symbolic fill, factor storage, numeric factorization, conditioning, and factor reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admissible elimination orders are exactly solution-equivalent, but their formation, fill, factorization, conditioning, and reuse costs can differ.
assumptions_latex: The full block system is nonsingular.
For each compared order, its pivot and Schur complement are nonsingular.
Solution equivalence is asserted in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\rm order\,1}=x_{\rm order\,2}=M^{-1}b.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Equivalence and Cost Tradeoff of Elimination Orders

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic admissibility test for a block-elimination order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=\begin{bmatrix}H&B^{\mathsf T}\\B&D\end{bmatrix}\) with nonsingular \(H\), let \(S_H=D-BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(\det M=\det H\det S_H\), so \(M\) is nonsingular exactly when \(S_H\) is nonsingular. The analogous result holds with \(D\) as pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elimination order is admissible exactly when its pivot and resulting Schur complement are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ nonsingular}\iff S_H\text{ nonsingular}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pivot–Complement Nonsingularity Criterion
Elimination-Order Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and computational consequences of choosing which KKT block to eliminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular block system with \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), eliminating the \(n\)-dimensional primal block forms \(S_y=D+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) of order \(m\); when invertible, eliminating the \(m\)-dimensional multiplier block instead forms a primal-space complement of order \(n\). Both exact reductions recover the same full-system solution by back-substitution. Their computational costs need not agree: the preferred order is determined by reduced dimension, sparsity and fill of the complement, the cost of applying the eliminated inverse, and numerical conditioning, rather than dimension alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either elimination order is algebraically exact, but reduced dimension, fill, inverse-application cost, and conditioning determine which order is computationally preferable.
assumptions_latex: The selected pivot block and resulting Schur complement are nonsingular.
All reductions and back-substitutions are performed in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible elimination orders yield the same solution but can have different storage, factorization cost, and conditioning.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT equations reduce to the positive-definite system \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZw=Z^{\mathsf T}(r_d-Hp)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-direction reduction onto the null space of the constraint matrix.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\) with \(m\leq n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), and let \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\). Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\), and choose \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ap=r_p\). Every \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(A\Delta x=r_p\) has the form \(\Delta x=p+Zw\) for a unique \(w\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\). Substitution into \(H\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=r_d\), with \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\), followed by multiplication by \(Z^{\mathsf T}\), gives \[Z^{\mathsf T}HZw=Z^{\mathsf T}(r_d-Hp).\] The matrix \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is positive definite on \(\mathbb R^{n-m}\); solving for \(w\) determines \(\Delta x\), after which \(\Delta y\) is uniquely recovered from the stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterizing feasible directions with a null-space basis produces a positive-definite reduced system of order equal to the primal nullity.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Reductions

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal positive-definiteness condition for a null-space reduced KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), and let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\). Then \[Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h^{\mathsf T}Hh>0\ \text{for every }0\neq h\in\ker A.\] Thus global positive definiteness of \(H\) is sufficient but not necessary for a positive-definite null-space reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space reduction is positive definite exactly when the primal Hessian is positive definite on feasible directions; it need not be positive definite on the whole space.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}Z=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\) if and only if \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Reduced-Hessian Regularity Condition

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The range-space reduction has coefficient \(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\) and is equivalent to the KKT system.

notation.meaning: scaled constraint range containing the primal correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-space reduction expressed through the range of the scaled constraint transpose.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\). For unknowns \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\), the equation \(H\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=r_d\) gives \(\Delta x=H^{-1}r_d-H^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\). Enforcing \(A\Delta x=r_p\) gives \[AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=AH^{-1}r_d-r_p.\] Thus the correction to the unconstrained direction \(H^{-1}r_d\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}(H^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})\). If \(A\) has full row rank, the reduced matrix is positive definite, and solving its \(m\)-dimensional system followed by back-substitution is equivalent to solving the full KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The range-space method solves for multipliers in constraint space and corrects the unconstrained primal direction through the scaled constraint-transpose range.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Reductions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Rank Boundary of the Range-Space System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp rank condition for positive definiteness of the multiplier-space reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[S\succ0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ has full row rank}.\] If \(A\) is row-rank deficient, then \(S\succeq0\) is singular and the uncompressed multiplier direction is not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite primal scaling, the range-space matrix is positive definite exactly when the constraint rows are independent; redundant rows make it singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}A=m\); otherwise it is singular positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Rank Boundary of the Range-Space System

assumptions_latex: Numerical rank is defined using a fixed threshold \(\tau\geq0\).
Perturbations and singular values use the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\sigma_i(A)-\tau|\leq\|E\|_2\quad\text{permits}\quad r_\tau(A+E)\neq r_\tau(A).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of rank-based reduction selection near a singular-value threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_\tau(A)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(A)>\tau\}\). If \(|\sigma_i(A)-\tau|\leq\|E\|_2\), a perturbation of size \(\|E\|_2\) can move that singular value across the threshold and change the selected reduced dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical-rank-based choice can switch under a small perturbation when a singular value is near the threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Rank Selection Instability

assumptions_latex: The same \(q\) right-hand sides are solved.
Assembly and basis costs are included separately or are identical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_N+qT_N<F_R+qT_R\Longrightarrow\text{lower modeled direct-solve work for the null-space form}.

notation.meaning: factorization work for null-space and range-space systems

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work comparison after candidate factor patterns are known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With factorization costs \(F_N,F_R\), solve costs \(T_N,T_R\), and \(q\) right-hand sides, the modeled direct-solve work favors the null-space form exactly when \(F_N+qT_N<F_R+qT_R\). Reduced order alone is insufficient because these costs depend on sparsity and fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare factorization plus repeated-solve work, not reduced dimension alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Pattern Selection Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension and dense-work comparison after removal of redundant equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\). A null-space reduction has order \(n-r\), while a range-space reduction has order \(r\). Under dense direct factorization their factorization costs are \(\Theta((n-r)^3)\) and \(\Theta(r^3)\), excluding basis construction, reduced-matrix formation, and back-substitution. Dimension therefore favors the smaller order, but sparsity, fill, conditioning, and formation costs may reverse the choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-space and range-space systems have orders n−r and r; dense cubic costs favor the smaller one unless other costs dominate.
assumptions_latex: Redundant equality rows have been removed or compressed.
The stated arithmetic comparison uses dense direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_N=n-r,\quad k_R=r,\quad W_N=\Theta((n-r)^3),\quad W_R=\Theta(r^3).
knowledge_statements.title: Rank–Dimension Reduction Selection
Dimension-Rank Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-based comparison of null-space and range-space reduced systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), and restrict redundant constraint equations so that the effective constraint dimension is \(r\). A null-space reduction uses a reduced system of order \(n-r\), whereas a range-space reduction uses one of order \(r\). Under a dense direct-factorization model, their leading arithmetic costs scale respectively as \(O((n-r)^3)\) and \(O(r^3)\), excluding basis construction and complement formation. Consequently, dimension alone favors null-space reduction when \(n-r<r\) and range-space reduction when \(r<n-r\); sparsity, fill, conditioning, and basis costs may reverse that preference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank determines reduced dimensions: null-space systems have order primal nullity, while range-space systems have order constraint rank; sparsity and conditioning can override this comparison.
assumptions_latex: Reduced systems are factored by dense direct methods for the stated cost comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced orders are \(n-r\) and \(r\), with dense factorization costs \(O((n-r)^3)\) and \(O(r^3)\), respectively.

children.title: Sparse Cholesky Methods for Schur Systems
children.top_down_role: Positive-definite reduced-system factorization and fill management.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and arithmetic after fixing an elimination ordering and symbolic factor pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_j\) be the number of subdiagonal structural entries in column \(j\) of the Cholesky factor. Factor storage and each triangular solve require \(\Theta(m+\sum_j d_j)\) space or work. A conventional column-oriented numeric factorization has work bounded by \(O(\sum_j(d_j+1)^2)\); exact constants and lower-order work depend on the sparse-factorization implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse Cholesky storage and solve work follow factor nonzeros, while numeric work is governed by the filled column sizes.
assumptions_latex: The symbolic factor pattern and elimination ordering are fixed.
Structural entries are counted independently of accidental numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{storage}(L),\operatorname{work}_{\rm solve}=\Theta(m+\sum_jd_j),\qquad \operatorname{work}_{\rm fact}=O(\sum_j(d_j+1)^2).

notation.meaning: number of subdiagonal structural entries in factor column j

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Dependent Sparse Cholesky Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact definiteness boundary for ordinary unpivoted Cholesky factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real symmetric matrix admits \(S=LL^{\mathsf T}\) with \(L\) nonsingular lower triangular and having positive diagonal if and only if \(S\succ0\). Thus an exact nonpositive pivot precludes this SPD Cholesky method; a computed nonpositive pivot may instead reflect roundoff or loss of numerical definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary Cholesky applies exactly to positive-definite matrices; a nonpositive pivot requires diagnosis or another factorization regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\succ0\iff \exists L\text{ nonsingular lower triangular with positive diagonal such that }S=LL^{\mathsf T}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cholesky Applicability Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic Cholesky structure under a fixed symmetric permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric permutation \(P\), symbolic elimination joins the higher-numbered current neighbors of every eliminated vertex. The resulting filled graph gives the structural pattern permitted for \(L+L^{\mathsf T}\) in \(PSP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\); it is generically exact but numerical cancellation can remove entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic fill is obtained by completing each eliminated vertex's remaining neighbors into a clique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{pattern}(L+L^{\mathsf T})\subseteq G_{\rm filled}(P,S),\text{ with generic equality}.

notation.meaning: filled elimination graph for the permuted sparsity pattern

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Graph and Structural Fill

assumptions_latex: All \(S_k\) share one structural sparsity pattern under the selected ordering.
Structural and accidental numerical zeros are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Symbolic analysis is reused; numerical factorization and solves are repeated for each }k.

notation.meaning: Schur matrix at interior-point iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse Cholesky variant for a sequence with a fixed structural pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For SPD matrices \(S_k\) with a fixed structural sparsity pattern, choose one symmetric ordering and compute the elimination tree and symbolic factor pattern once. For each \(k\), recompute the numerical Cholesky values and perform the triangular solves. Repeat symbolic analysis if the structural pattern changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed Schur sparsity pattern permits reuse of ordering and symbolic analysis while numerical factors are updated.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic-Analysis Reuse Across Schur Solves

assumptions_latex: A valid positive lower bound on \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat y-y_*\|_2\leq\|g-S\widehat y\|_2/\lambda_{\min}(S).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error certificate for an accepted sparse Cholesky solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Sy_*=g\), \(S\succ0\), and \(r=g-S\widehat y\), then \[\|\widehat y-y_*\|_2\leq\|S^{-1}\|_2\|r\|_2=\frac{\|r\|_2}{\lambda_{\min}(S)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual and a positive lower eigenvalue bound certify forward accuracy of the Schur solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Solve Residual Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete direct workflow for a sparse positive-definite Schur system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sparse \(S\succ0\) and \(g\), choose a symmetric fill-reducing permutation \(P\); compute the symbolic elimination structure and numerical factorization \(PSP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\); solve \(Lz=Pg\) and \(L^{\mathsf T}w=z\); return \(y=P^{\mathsf T}w\) if the declared residual test passes. Report definiteness, factorization, or accuracy failure otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order, symbolically analyze, factor, triangularly solve, unpermute, and validate a sparse SPD Schur system.
assumptions_latex: The residual tolerance and norm are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|g-Sy\|\leq\tau\quad\text{on successful termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Schur Cholesky Solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary for fill-free symbolic Cholesky.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An undirected sparsity graph admits an ordering with no symbolic fill if and only if it is chordal. Every perfect elimination ordering of a chordal graph is fill free; every ordering of a nonchordal graph creates fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill-free symbolic Cholesky is possible exactly for chordal graphs using a perfect elimination ordering.
assumptions_latex: The graph is the structural off-diagonal pattern of an SPD matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ chordal}\iff G\text{ admits a fill-free perfect elimination ordering}.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Zero-Fill Characterization
Sparse Cholesky Methods for Schur Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct solution of sparse positive-definite Schur systems with fill-reducing ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a sparse symmetric positive-definite Schur matrix \(S\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\), right-hand side \(g\in\mathbb R^m\), and a symmetric permutation \(P\). Choose \(P\) from the sparsity graph to reduce predicted fill; compute the symbolic elimination structure, then a sparse Cholesky factorization \(PSP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\). Solve \(Lz=Pg\), solve \(L^{\mathsf T}w=z\), and output \(y=P^{\mathsf T}w\). Stop successfully when both triangular solves complete and the residual satisfies the prescribed test \(\lVert g-Sy\rVert\leq\tau\); otherwise report factorization or accuracy failure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense direct factorization for symmetric-indefinite Newton and KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb S^{q}\) be nonsingular. A dense symmetric-indefinite direct method uses a symmetric permutation and block factorization \[P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T},\] where \(L\) is unit lower triangular and \(D\) has nonsingular \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) diagonal blocks. The solve consists of permutation, triangular solves, a block-diagonal solve, and inverse permutation. Two-by-two pivots can be necessary: \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) is nonsingular but has no admissible first \(1\times1\) diagonal pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense symmetric-indefinite systems use symmetrically pivoted block-LDL factorization, and two-by-two pivots may be necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb S^{q}\) is nonsingular and treated as dense.
The pivoting process selects nonsingular \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) pivot blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A permuted block-\(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization enables an exact dense direct solve.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Symmetric-Indefinite Factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage bounds for dense direct solution of a positive-definite reduced Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^{q}\) be stored and factored densely. Standard Cholesky factorization \(M=LL^{\mathsf T}\) requires \(q^3/3+O(q^2)\) floating-point operations and stores \(q(q+1)/2\) triangular entries. Solving one additional right-hand side by forward and backward substitution requires \(2q^2+O(q)\) operations. Thus the dense SPD regime has \(O(q^3)\) factorization work and \(O(q^2)\) factor storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense Cholesky has cubic factorization work, quadratic storage, and quadratic work per additional right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: Costs count scalar floating-point operations and stored triangular entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Factorization costs \(q^3/3+O(q^2)\), storage is \(q(q+1)/2\), and each subsequent solve costs \(2q^2+O(q)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Cholesky Resource Bounds

Thus dense factorization is appropriate when \(q\\) is moderate or sparsity would not survive elimination, while its asymptotic resource bounds are \(O(q^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(q^2)\) storage.

children.title: Block-Structured Factorization Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block Gaussian elimination for a symmetrically partitioned Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=(K_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{p}\) be symmetric with a conformal block partition and a prescribed elimination order. Whenever the active pivot block \(K_{kk}\) is nonsingular, form block multipliers and update the remaining active blocks by \[K_{ij}\leftarrow K_{ij}-K_{ik}K_{kk}^{-1}K_{kj}.\] Repeating these block-Schur updates and then applying block back-substitution gives the exact solution of \(Kx=b\), provided every selected pivot is admissible. An update may create a nonzero block where \(K_{ij}=0\), so ordering controls intermediate block fill, work, and storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled block factorization repeatedly forms block Schur complements; admissible pivots ensure exactness, while ordering controls fill and cost.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is symmetric with a conformal block partition.
Every selected active pivot block is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Block elimination followed by block back-substitution solves the original system exactly; intermediate fill depends on the elimination order.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Block Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separability and additive resource accounting for an uncoupled block-diagonal Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\operatorname{diag}(K_1,\ldots,K_p)\), with every \(K_i\) nonsingular, and partition \(x\) and \(b\) conformally. Then \(Kx=b\) is equivalent to the independent systems \(K_i x_i=b_i\). If local factorization work and storage are \(F_i\) and \(M_i\), total work and storage are \(\sum_iF_i\) and \(\sum_iM_i\), and the blocks may be processed concurrently. Nonzero off-diagonal blocks remove this unconditional independent-solve decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-diagonal Newton matrix decomposes into independent local factorizations with additive work and storage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solve separates blockwise, with total work \(\sum_iF_i\) and storage \(\sum_iM_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Block Factorization Regime
Block-Structured Factorization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block elimination that preserves exploitable separability in a Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetric block matrix \(K=(K_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{p}\), a conformal right-hand side, and an elimination ordering. Initialize the active blocks with \(K_{ij}\). At each step, factor the selected nonsingular diagonal pivot block \(K_{kk}\), compute block multipliers \(L_{ik}=K_{ik}K_{kk}^{-1}\), and update every active pair by \(K_{ij}\leftarrow K_{ij}-K_{ik}K_{kk}^{-1}K_{kj}\). Continue until all pivot blocks are eliminated, solve the resulting block-triangular systems, and output the Newton direction when its residual meets tolerance. The method is advantageous when the ordering limits block fill and permits structured pivot solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor diagonal blocks, update block Schur complements, and solve block-triangular systems while choosing an ordering that limits coupling and fill.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is symmetric with a specified conformal block partition.
Every selected pivot block is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact block elimination and back-substitution return the solution of the original block system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient structural condition for independent row-group assembly and factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the additive mixed-cone Schur representation, suppose \(\mathbb R^m=Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Y_s\) is an orthogonal row partition and, for each \(i\), \(\operatorname{range}(A_i)\subseteq Y_{g(i)}\) for some group \(g(i)\). Then \(S=\sum_iA_iH_i^{-1}A_i^{\mathsf T}\) is block diagonal with respect to this partition, so its row-group blocks can be assembled and factored independently. If some \(A_i\) has components in multiple row groups, block-diagonal cone scaling alone does not guarantee this decomposition and that block may couple the groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint constraint-row support guarantees separable mixed-cone Schur blocks; shared row support can couple them despite block-diagonal cone scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb R^m=Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Y_s\) is an orthogonal decomposition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-space assembly for a product cone with cone-specific positive-definite scaling blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{p}E_i\), let \(H=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\ldots,H_p)\) with \(H_i\in\mathbb S_{++}(E_i)\), and let \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_p]:E\to\mathbb R^m\). Eliminating the cone-variable direction gives \[S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^{p}A_iH_i^{-1}A_i^{\mathsf T}.\] Thus cone-local scaling remains block diagonal, but all blocks contribute in the common constraint space. If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(S\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-specific scaling is block diagonal, while shared constraints add all cone-block contributions into one coupled Schur matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_p]:E\to\mathbb R^m\) has full row rank.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the conic variable space be the product \(E=E_1\oplus\cdots\oplus E_p\), with barrier scaling \(H=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\ldots,H_p)\), where each \(H_i\in\mathbb S_{++}(E_i)\), and write the constraint operator as \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_p]\). Eliminating the cone-variable direction yields the coupled constraint-space matrix \[S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^{p}A_iH_i^{-1}A_i^{\mathsf T}.\] Although \(H\) is block diagonal across cone factors, the common constraint space couples their contributions through this sum. If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(S\) is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schur Positive Definiteness and Exact Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-system structure for a positive-definite primal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\succ0\) and full-row-rank \(A\), \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). If \(q=AH^{-1}r_x-r_y\), any \(\widehat y\) together with \(\widehat x=H^{-1}(r_x-A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y)\) has block residuals \[r_x-H\widehat x-A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=0,\qquad r_y-A\widehat x=S\widehat y-q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Schur operator is SPD, and exact back-substitution makes the remaining full-system residual equal the reduced residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic convergence for an SPD reduced Newton operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S,P\succ0\), preconditioned CG applied through \(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2}\) satisfies \[\lVert e_k\rVert_S\leq2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\lVert e_0\rVert_S,\qquad \kappa=\kappa_2(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2}),\] in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned CG converges geometrically in the Schur energy norm at a rate controlled by the transformed condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert e_k\rVert_S\leq2((\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1))^k\lVert e_0\rVert_S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free PCG for the SPD reduced Newton equation with original-system validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(q=AH^{-1}r_x-r_y\), \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), choose \(y_0\), and form \(g_0=q-Sy_0\). Apply preconditioned conjugate gradients with an SPD preconditioner \(P\), using \(v\mapsto A(H^{-1}(A^{\mathsf T}v))\) and \(z=P^{-1}g\). After the reduced stopping test holds, set \(\widehat y=y_k\), recover \(\widehat x=H^{-1}(r_x-A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y)\), and accept only if both original block residuals meet their prescribed tests. With exact actions, \(r_x-H\widehat x-A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=0\) and \(r_y-A\widehat x=S\widehat y-q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run PCG on the matrix-free SPD Schur operator, recover the primal direction, and validate it using the original block equations.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(P\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and applications of \(H^{-1}\) and \(P^{-1}\) are exact.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration work and storage for matrix-free reduced PCG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: One reduced PCG iteration uses one action each of \(A^{\mathsf T}\), \(H^{-1}\), \(A\), and \(P^{-1}\), plus \(O(n+m)\) vector work. Thus \(k\) iterations cost \[O\!\left(k(C_{A^{\mathsf T}}+C_{H^{-1}}+C_A+C_{P^{-1}}+n+m)\right)\] and use \(O(n+m)\) working-vector storage, excluding storage and setup internal to the operators and preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each reduced-PCG iteration performs one adjoint, inverse-Hessian, constraint, and preconditioner action and needs primal- and reduced-space work vectors.
assumptions_latex: The displayed action costs bound one application of each operator.
Setup and implementation-internal storage are excluded.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement reduction of a symmetric conic Newton system with a positive-definite primal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the Newton equations \(H\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=r_x\) and \(A\Delta x=r_y\), form operator actions with \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) without explicitly assembling \(S\). Starting from \(\Delta y_0\), apply preconditioned conjugate gradients to \(S\Delta y=AH^{-1}r_x-r_y\) until the chosen relative residual tolerance holds. Then recover \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(r_x-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y)\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(S\succ0\), so conjugate gradients is applicable in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal step, solve the positive-definite Schur complement by conjugate gradients, and recover the primal direction by back-substitution.
