children.title: Augmented-System Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Krylov solver families for augmented saddle-point systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability boundary for a positive-definite primal block and retained constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) with \(H\succ0\), \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(A\) has full row rank. If \(A\) is rank deficient, \(Kz=r\) is solvable exactly when \(r\perp\ker K\), and every consistent solution is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-deficient constraints make the augmented operator singular; consistency may permit solutions but cannot restore uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsingular}\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Singularity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic characterization for an unpreconditioned symmetric augmented system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(K\), MINRES chooses \(z_k\in z_0+\mathcal K_k(K,r_0)\) minimizing \(\lVert r-Kz\rVert_2\) over that affine Krylov space. If \(K\) is nonsingular, exact arithmetic terminates at the exact solution in at most the degree of the minimal polynomial relative to \(r_0\), and therefore in at most \(N\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES minimizes the Euclidean residual over successive Krylov affine spaces and terminates finitely in exact arithmetic for a nonsingular symmetric system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert r_k\rVert_2=\min_{z\in z_0+\mathcal K_k(K,r_0)}\lVert r-Kz\rVert_2.

notation.meaning: order-k Krylov subspace generated by K and the initial residual

knowledge_statements.title: MINRES Residual Minimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional forward-error certificate for a nonsingular augmented system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(z_*=K^{-1}r\), then every iterate \(z\) satisfies \[\|z-z_*\|_2\leq\|K^{-1}\|_2\,\|r-Kz\|_2.\] Hence a small residual certifies small forward error only when \(K\) is not too close to singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented-system residual certifies forward accuracy only when the inverse operator norm is controlled.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Residual Error Certificate

assumptions_latex: MINRES is applied in exact arithmetic to the transformed system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widetilde r_k\|_2\leq\min_{p(0)=1,\deg p\leq k}\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(\widetilde K)}|p(\lambda)|\,\|\widetilde r_0\|_2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectrum-dependent exact-arithmetic convergence characterization for MINRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed symmetric \(\widetilde K\), the MINRES residual has the form \(\widetilde r_k=p_k(\widetilde K)\widetilde r_0\), with \(p_k(0)=1\) and \(\deg p_k\leq k\), and satisfies \[\|\widetilde r_k\|_2\leq\min_{p(0)=1,\,\deg p\leq k}\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(\widetilde K)}|p(\lambda)|\,\|\widetilde r_0\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES convergence is governed by polynomial approximation on the effective symmetric spectrum, so clustering away from zero can accelerate convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: MINRES Polynomial Residual Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete Krylov workflow for a symmetric-indefinite augmented Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(P=CC^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), form operator actions for \(\widetilde K=C^{-1}KC^{-\mathsf T}\), initialize \(u_0=C^{\mathsf T}z_0\), and apply MINRES to \(\widetilde Ku=\widetilde r=C^{-1}r\). Stop when \(\|\widetilde r-\widetilde Ku_k\|_2\leq\eta\|\widetilde r\|_2\), recover \(z_k=C^{-\mathsf T}u_k\), and report Lanczos breakdown, nonfinite arithmetic, or iteration-limit failure when applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply MINRES to the symmetrically preconditioned augmented operator, test the transformed residual, and recover the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r-Kz_k\|_{P^{-1}}\leq\eta\|r\|_{P^{-1}}\quad\text{on successful termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Preconditioned MINRES Augmented Solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SPD split transformation for MINRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=CC^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). With \(\widetilde K=C^{-1}KC^{-\mathsf T}\), \(\widetilde r=C^{-1}r\), and \(z=C^{-\mathsf T}u\), the system \(Kz=r\) becomes the Euclidean-symmetric system \(\widetilde Ku=\widetilde r\), and \(\|r-Kz\|_{P^{-1}}=\|\widetilde r-\widetilde Ku\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting an SPD preconditioner on both sides preserves symmetry and converts the preconditioned residual norm to a Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde K\in\mathbb S^N,\qquad \|r-Kz\|_{P^{-1}}=\|\widetilde r-\widetilde Ku\|_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Preserving Split Preconditioning
Augmented-System Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Krylov solution of the symmetric-indefinite augmented Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(r=(r_x,r_y)\). Choose a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(P\), initialize \(z_0=(\Delta x_0,\Delta y_0)\), and apply preconditioned MINRES to \(Kz=r\) using only products by \(H\), \(A\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\), and solves with \(P\). Stop when \(\lVert r-Kz_k\rVert_{P^{-1}}\leq\eta\lVert r\rVert_{P^{-1}}\), and output \(z_k\). Symmetry permits MINRES despite the indefiniteness of \(K\); conjugate gradients is generally inapplicable to this augmented matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply MINRES with a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner directly to the symmetric-indefinite augmented Newton matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(z_k\) has preconditioned relative residual at most \(\eta\).
review_flags: Exact source for augmented-system MINRES and its preconditioning requirements is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the augmented-system leaf, but the precise preconditioned MINRES formulation and residual norm require a source. The tolerance domain and symmetry-preserving transformation are not stated explicitly enough to validate the exact claim.

children.title: Definiteness-Sensitive Krylov Selection
children.top_down_role: Solver selection according to definite, semidefinite, or indefinite system structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification of CG and MINRES when the effective symmetric operator is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(M\succeq0\) is singular, \(Mz=b\) is solvable exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{range}(M)=(\ker M)^\perp\). Consistent solutions are not unique without an additional selection rule. For an inconsistent singular symmetric system, a residual-minimizing method may find a least-residual iterate but cannot solve \(Mz=b\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular semidefinite systems require consistency and lack the unique-solution guarantee of SPD systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mz=b\text{ is solvable}\iff b\perp\ker M.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Semidefinite Selection Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Left Preconditioning Can Hide Euclidean Symmetry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection must account for the working inner product or split transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M,P\in\mathbb S_{++}^N\), the left-preconditioned matrix \(P^{-1}M\) need not be symmetric in the Euclidean inner product. It is self-adjoint in the \(P\)-inner product and is similar to the SPD split transform \(P^{-1/2}MP^{-1/2}\). Applying a Euclidean-symmetry recurrence without this qualification is unjustified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naive left preconditioning can conceal symmetry, so solver selection must specify the inner product or split transform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^{-1/2}MP^{-1/2}\in\mathbb S_{++}^N,\qquad P^{-1}M\text{ need not be Euclidean-symmetric}.
knowledge_statements.title: Left Preconditioning Can Hide Euclidean Symmetry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov Selection by Effective Operator Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural eligibility of standard Krylov families after any preconditioning transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply CG when the effective operator is self-adjoint and positive definite in the working inner product; apply MINRES when it is self-adjoint but may be indefinite; and use a nonsymmetric Krylov method such as GMRES when no usable self-adjoint formulation is available. The classification must be applied to the effective preconditioned operator, not merely the original matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose CG, MINRES, or a nonsymmetric method from the symmetry and definiteness of the effective operator.
assumptions_latex: A fixed linear effective operator and working inner product have been specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{SPD self-adjoint}\Rightarrow\mathrm{CG},\quad\text{self-adjoint indefinite}\Rightarrow\mathrm{MINRES},\quad\text{nonsymmetric}\Rightarrow\text{nonsymmetric Krylov family}.
knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Selection by Effective Operator Structure

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mz=b\text{ is solvable}\iff b\perp\ker M.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency and uniqueness boundary for general singular self-adjoint operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any real symmetric singular matrix \(M\), including an indefinite one, \(Mz=b\) is solvable exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{range}(M)=(\ker M)^\perp\). Every consistent solution is nonunique unless an additional selection rule is imposed. If the system is inconsistent, residual minimization solves a different least-residual problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular symmetric-indefinite system requires consistency and cannot have a unique solution without an added selection rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Symmetric-Indefinite Selection Boundary
Definiteness-Sensitive Krylov Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver selection according to symmetry and definiteness of the Newton operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear Newton equation \(Mz=b\), select conjugate gradients when \(M\) is symmetric positive definite; select MINRES when \(M\) is symmetric but possibly indefinite; and select GMRES when symmetry is absent. With left or split preconditioning, preserve the structural hypothesis required by the selected method: conjugate gradients must see a positive-definite self-adjoint operator, while MINRES requires a self-adjoint preconditioned formulation. A method whose structural hypothesis fails has no corresponding standard recurrence or convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use CG for symmetric positive-definite systems, MINRES for symmetric-indefinite systems, and GMRES when symmetry is unavailable, preserving the relevant structure under preconditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) is the effective preconditioned Newton operator
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Krylov method is chosen from \(\{\mathrm{CG},\mathrm{MINRES},\mathrm{GMRES}\}\) according to the symmetry and definiteness of \(M\).
review_flags: A numerical-linear-algebra source explicitly supporting the three-way selection rule is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The broad CG/MINRES/GMRES guidance is recognizable, but the claims about left or split preconditioning and the absence of a standard recurrence or guarantee require a numerical-linear-algebra source and more precise qualification.

children.title: Conic IPM Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Constraint, cone, block, and low-rank preconditioner families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure through singularity, indefiniteness, or loss of uniform spectral equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SPD reduced problem, a singular or indefinite \(P\) invalidates the standard preconditioned-CG formulation. Even with \(P_k\succ0\), if \(\kappa(P_k^{-1/2}S_kP_k^{-1/2})\) is unbounded along the interior-point iterates, condition-number theory supplies no iteration bound uniform in \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SPD applicability and uniformly controlled spectrum are separate requirements for robust preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_k\kappa(P_k^{-1/2}S_kP_k^{-1/2})=\infty\Longrightarrow\text{no uniform condition-number iteration bound}.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Quality Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quality criterion for an SPD preconditioner of an SPD reduced conic Newton operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S,P\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\) and \(\alpha P\preceq S\preceq\beta P\) for \(0<\alpha\leq\beta\), then every eigenvalue of \(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2}\) lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\) and \(\kappa_2(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2})\leq\beta/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform spectral equivalence bounds the condition number seen by preconditioned CG.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2})\subseteq[\alpha,\beta],\qquad \kappa_2(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2})\leq\beta/\alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Equivalence for Reduced-System Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse application when an easy base approximation receives a low-rank correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P=B+UCU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(B\succ0\), \(C\) is nonsingular, and \(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}U\) is nonsingular, then \[P^{-1}=B^{-1}-B^{-1}U(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}U)^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank correction can be applied using base-preconditioner solves and a small dense solve.
assumptions_latex: If CG is intended, \(P\) must additionally be positive definite.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Correction Preconditioner

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^{-1/2}KP^{-1/2}\in\mathbb S^N.

notation.meaning: inner product induced by the SPD preconditioner

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-adjoint preconditioning formulation for a symmetric-indefinite Newton operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\) and \(P\succ0\), then \(\widetilde K=P^{-1/2}KP^{-1/2}\) is Euclidean-symmetric. Equivalently, \(P^{-1}K\) is self-adjoint in \(\langle u,v\rangle_P=u^{\mathsf T}Pv\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SPD split transform, or the equivalent weighted inner product, preserves self-adjointness for augmented-system MINRES.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Preserving Augmented Preconditioning

assumptions_latex: A block partition conforming to cone or constraint groups is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\rm BJ}=\operatorname{blkdiag}(S_{11},\ldots,S_{pp})\succ0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-diagonal approximation obtained by dropping cross-block Schur couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(S=[S_{ij}]_{i,j=1}^p\succ0\). Its principal diagonal blocks are positive definite, so \[P_{\rm BJ}=\operatorname{blkdiag}(S_{11},\ldots,S_{pp})\succ0.\] Its inverse applies through independent block solves; quality depends on the discarded off-diagonal couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block Jacobi retains diagonal cone or constraint blocks and permits independent preconditioner solves.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Jacobi Preconditioner

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\succ0,\qquad\Gamma^{-1}P\preceq S\preceq\gamma^{-1}P.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-space construction induced by an approximation to the cone-scaling block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) and \(P=A\widehat H^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\gamma\widehat H\preceq H\preceq\Gamma\widehat H\), then \[\Gamma^{-1}P\preceq S\preceq\gamma^{-1}P,\] and full row rank of \(A\) gives \(P\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximating the cone-scaling block induces an SPD constraint-space preconditioner with inherited spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Schur Preconditioner
Conic IPM Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral requirements for preconditioners used with conic interior-point Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reduced positive-definite Newton operator \(S\), choose \(P\succ0\) so that \(\alpha P\preceq S\preceq\beta P\) with constants \(0<\alpha\leq\beta\). Then every eigenvalue of \(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2}\) lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and its spectral condition number is at most \(\beta/\alpha\). Constraint, cone-block, block-diagonal, and low-rank-update preconditioners are admissible when they are inexpensive to apply and maintain this spectral equivalence. For symmetric-indefinite augmented systems, the preconditioning transformation must additionally preserve self-adjointness for MINRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A useful conic Newton preconditioner is cheap to apply, spectrally equivalent to the reduced operator, and compatible with the symmetry requirements of the Krylov solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(P^{-1/2}SP^{-1/2})\leq\beta/\alpha\).
review_flags: A source connecting spectral-equivalence preconditioning to conic IPM Newton systems is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-equivalence bound is mathematically standard, but no source supports its asserted application to the listed conic-IPM preconditioner families or the augmented-system MINRES requirement.

children.title: Matrix-Free Barrier-Hessian Operations
children.top_down_role: Implicit derivative and operator interfaces for large cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and storage excluding setup for matrix-free Newton solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one iteration uses an operator action of cost \(C_{\rm op}\), a preconditioner action of cost \(C_P\), and \(O(N)\) vector work, then \(k\) iterations cost \(O(k(C_{\rm op}+C_P+N))\). Short-recurrence CG or MINRES uses \(O(N)\) iteration storage, whereas unrestarted GMRES may use \(O(kN)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free work is iterations times operator and preconditioner cost; memory depends on the Krylov recurrence.
assumptions_latex: Operator and preconditioner application costs are bounded by \(C_{\rm op}\) and \(C_P\) per iteration.
Setup and cone-oracle preprocessing are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{work}=O(k(C_{\rm op}+C_P+N)).
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Only Krylov Cost Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for independently implemented forward and adjoint routines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The routines labeled \(A\) and \(A^*\) represent an adjoint pair only if \(\langle Au,y\rangle_{\mathcal Y}=\langle u,A^*y\rangle_{\mathcal X}\) for every admissible \(u,y\). Violation of this identity can destroy the self-adjointness of the nominal reduced action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and adjoint routines must satisfy the defining inner-product identity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) are finite-dimensional inner-product spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \langle Au,y\rangle_{\mathcal Y}=\langle u,A^*y\rangle_{\mathcal X}.
knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Consistency Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a fixed self-adjoint outer operator under uncontrolled nested solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If successive calls intended to apply \(H^{-1}\) return uncontrolled, varying approximations, the outer iteration generally sees a changing operator. Standard fixed-operator CG or MINRES recurrences then need not retain their usual guarantees; the perturbations must be controlled or a compatible flexible method and full residual test must be used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncontrolled variable inner solves invalidate ordinary fixed-operator Krylov assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Inverse-Hessian actions are computed approximately and may vary between calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde H_j^{-1}\neq\widetilde H_\ell^{-1}\text{ without error control}\Longrightarrow\text{fixed-operator Krylov theory need not apply}.

notation.meaning: approximate inverse action used on outer iteration j

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Inverse-Action Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward, adjoint, Hessian, and inverse-Hessian actions on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\), let \(A^*:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X\) be its adjoint, and let \(H:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\) be self-adjoint positive definite. Matrix-free access consists of routines for \(u\mapsto Au\), \(y\mapsto A^*y\), \(u\mapsto Hu\), and, when a reduced product is required, an exact or controlled approximation to \(u\mapsto H^{-1}u\). The reduced action is \(y\mapsto AH^{-1}A^*y\) without materializing \(H\) or the Schur matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Typed forward, adjoint, Hessian, and controlled inverse-Hessian routines implement Newton products without dense assembly.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) are finite-dimensional inner-product spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\mapsto AH^{-1}A^*y\text{ is evaluable using only operator routines}.
knowledge_statements.title: Typed Matrix-Free Newton Operator Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled nested solution used to implement an inverse-Hessian action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To implement a requested action \(H^{-1}v\) on outer call \(j\), approximately solve \(Hw=v\) until an explicitly recomputed residual satisfies \(\|v-Hw_j\|\leq\eta_j\|v\|\). Return \(w_j\), the achieved residual, and the inner status; if the bound is not attained, report failure. The outer method records \(\eta_j\), uses variable actions only when supported by its iteration, and accepts a Newton direction only after testing the full original-system residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate inverse-Hessian call returns a verified residual and status, while the enclosing solver validates the resulting direction in the original Newton system.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\) is self-adjoint positive definite.
The inner method can evaluate \(Hw\) and recompute its residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|v-Hw_j\|\leq\eta_j\|v\|\quad\text{or an explicit failure is returned}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Inverse-Hessian Action Protocol
Matrix-Free Barrier-Hessian Operations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-only Newton products for large cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a twice differentiable barrier \(F\), an interior point \(x\), and linear maps \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\), expose routines \(v\mapsto\nabla^2F(x)v\), \(v\mapsto Av\), and \(y\mapsto A^{\mathsf T}y\). A reduced product is evaluated as \(y\mapsto A(\nabla^2F(x))^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}y\), where the inverse action is computed by a cone-specific solve or inner iteration. A Krylov method then constructs the Newton direction using these routines and terminates at a prescribed residual tolerance, without storing the barrier Hessian or Schur complement as dense matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supply Hessian-vector, constraint, adjoint, and inverse-Hessian actions so a Krylov solver can compute Newton directions without assembling dense matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Newton-system products are evaluable without explicit formation of \(\nabla^2F(x)\) or \(A(\nabla^2F(x))^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\).
review_flags: A source for matrix-free barrier-Hessian and inverse-action interfaces is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the matrix-free operations leaf, but the spaces of the operators and the conditions under which an inverse-Hessian action is available are underspecified. No source supports the stated cone-specific interface.

children.title: Structure-Exploiting Conic Linear Algebra
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebra reductions exploiting separability, sparsity, low rank, or repeated structure.

children.title: Decomposition-Structured Linear Algebra
children.top_down_role: Block eliminations and decomposition-aware Newton systems.

children.title: Block-Angular Structure
children.top_down_role: Newton-system organization induced by block-angular coupling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arrow normal matrix induced by block-angular constraints and conformally block-diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[A=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{diag}(A_1,\ldots,A_p)\\ L_1\ \cdots\ L_p\end{bmatrix},\qquad H^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(H_1^{-1},\ldots,H_p^{-1}).\] Then \[AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{diag}(A_iH_i^{-1}A_i^{\mathsf T})&(A_iH_i^{-1}L_i^{\mathsf T})_{i=1}^p\\(L_iH_i^{-1}A_i^{\mathsf T})_{i=1}^p&\sum_iL_iH_i^{-1}L_i^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix},\] an arrow matrix under the local-row/linking-row ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-angular constraints and aligned block-diagonal scaling generate an arrow weighted normal matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\text{ has block-arrow structure}.

notation.meaning: Contribution of variable block i to the linking rows

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Angular Normal Matrix

assumptions_latex: Variable columns are partitioned into blocks \(x_1,\ldots,x_p\).
The weighted normal matrix uses a symmetric metric \(H^{-1}\) conformal with that partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Off-diagonal \(H^{-1}_{ij}\) can create nonzero local-row blocks \(A_iH^{-1}_{ij}A_j^{\mathsf T}\), so block-angular constraints alone do not ensure an arrow normal matrix.

notation.meaning: Metric block coupling variable blocks i and j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of induced arrow structure when the Newton metric is not aligned with block-angular variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Block-angular sparsity of \(A\) does not by itself make \(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) an arrow matrix. If \(H^{-1}\) has an off-diagonal block \(H^{-1}_{ij}\), the corresponding local-row cross block contains \(A_iH^{-1}_{ij}A_j^{\mathsf T}\), which may be nonzero. For example, with two scalar local blocks, \(A=I_2\) and \(H^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{bmatrix}\), \(0<|\rho|<1\), the nominally local rows are coupled. Conformal block-diagonal scaling is therefore an essential sufficient assumption for the accepted arrow normal-matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Off-diagonal Newton scaling can couple nominally independent local rows, so block-angular constraints induce an arrow normal matrix only under aligned scaling or equivalent cancellation.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Alignment Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-linked block-angular constraints with private variable blocks and common linking rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(A\) has row-linked block-angular structure if row and column permutations give \[A=\begin{bmatrix}A_1&0&\cdots&0\\0&A_2&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&A_p\\L_1&L_2&\cdots&L_p\end{bmatrix}.\] For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\), the equations \(A_ix_i=b_i\) are local and \(\sum_iL_ix_i=b_0\) are linking constraints. Removing the linking rows leaves independent block systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row-linked block-angular matrix consists of independent local row blocks plus shared linking rows across the variable blocks.
assumptions_latex: The row and column permutations preserve the represented linear system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Removing the linking rows leaves }\operatorname{diag}(A_1,\ldots,A_p).

notation.meaning: Contribution of variable block \(i\) to the linking rows

knowledge_statements.title: Permuted Block-Angular Constraint Matrix
Block-Angular Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-angular constraint form with local variables coupled through shared linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint matrix has block-angular structure if, after row and column permutations, it can be written as \[A=\begin{bmatrix}A_1&0&\cdots&0\\0&A_2&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&A_p\\L_1&L_2&\cdots&L_p\end{bmatrix}.\] The diagonal blocks \(A_i\) impose independent local constraints on variable blocks \(x_i\), while the final block row imposes the linking constraint \(\sum_{i=1}^pL_ix_i=b_0\). If the cone and barrier are products over the same blocks, local Newton eliminations are independent conditional on the linking variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-angular systems contain independent local constraint blocks joined by a comparatively small set of linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed permuted form defines block-angular structure and separates local from linking constraints.

children.title: Arrow Structure
children.top_down_role: Newton-system organization induced by arrow-shaped coupling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical dense algebra for local blocks and a dense shared block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D_i\in\mathbb S^{n_i}\), \(B_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times s}\), classical dense factorization of the local blocks, formation of the shared Schur complement, and its dense factorization require \[O\!\left(\sum_i n_i^3+\sum_i n_i^2s+\sum_i n_is^2+s^3\right)\] arithmetic operations. The local factorizations and contributions can be formed independently.

Arrow Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arrow-structured symmetric matrices arising from independent blocks coupled to a shared block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric matrix has block-arrow structure if, after a simultaneous row and column permutation, it has the form \[M=\begin{bmatrix}D_1&0&\cdots&0&B_1\\0&D_2&\cdots&0&B_2\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&D_p&B_p\\B_1^{\mathsf T}&B_2^{\mathsf T}&\cdots&B_p^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix},\] where the \(D_i\) are mutually uncoupled diagonal blocks and \(C\) is a shared coupling block. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-arrow matrix consists of independent diagonal blocks connected only through one shared block, allowing parallel local elimination.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local elimination produces the coupling-block Schur complement \(C-\sum_{i=1}^pB_i^{\mathsf T}D_i^{-1}B_i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchy of separability notions used in barrier Newton linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cone-barrier separability means \(K=\prod_iK_i\) and \(F(x)=\sum_iF_i(x_i)\). Affine separability means that, after row permutation, every nonlinking affine equation uses variables from only one block. Full Newton separability means that, after conformal equation and variable permutations, the Newton matrix is block diagonal and its right-hand side is partitioned accordingly. Cone-barrier separability gives block-separable barrier derivatives but does not imply full Newton separability. If objective derivatives, cone-barrier derivatives, and all affine equations are block local under the same partition, the Newton equations split into independent block systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-barrier, affine, and full Newton-system separability are distinct; full separation requires every Newton coupling to respect the same block partition.

children.title: Decomposition-Aware Elimination
children.top_down_role: Elimination regimes that preserve or exploit decomposition structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric decomposition-structured system with a nonsingular block-diagonal local pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(D_1,\ldots,D_p)\) be symmetric and nonsingular and \(M=\begin{bmatrix}D&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\). For \(S=C-B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B\), \[\operatorname{inertia}(M)=\sum_{i=1}^p\operatorname{inertia}(D_i)+\operatorname{inertia}(S).\] Consequently, under the stated nonsingularity of the \(D_i\), \(M\) is nonsingular exactly when \(S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structure-preserving local elimination splits the full-system inertia into local-pivot inertias and the coupling Schur-complement inertia.
assumptions_latex: D_i=D_i^{\mathsf T}\text{ and }D_i\text{ is nonsingular for every }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{inertia}(M)=\sum_i\operatorname{inertia}(D_i)+\operatorname{inertia}(S).

notation.meaning: Positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts of Q

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia Decomposition Under Local Elimination

assumptions_latex: \(\widehat S=C-\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}Q_iB_i\), where certified bounds on \(\|Q_i-D_i^{-1}\|\) are available.
The matrix norm is subordinate and submultiplicative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat S-S\|\leq\sum_i\|B_i\|^2\|Q_i-D_i^{-1}\|\).

notation.meaning: Schur complement assembled with approximate inverse actions
Approximate inverse action for local block i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise certificate for error introduced by inexact local solves during decomposition-aware Schur assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S=C-\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}D_i^{-1}B_i\) and approximate local inverse actions \(Q_i\) produce \(\widehat S=C-\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}Q_iB_i\), then \[\|\widehat S-S\|\leq\sum_i\|B_i\|^2\,\|Q_i-D_i^{-1}\|.\] Therefore certified local inverse-action error bounds give a normwise certificate for the assembled coupling operator. Large inverse-action errors, including those caused by nearly singular pivots, can make the reduced system unreliable even when its subsequent solve is accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified errors in local inverse actions bound the assembled Schur-operator error by a coupling-weighted sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Local-Elimination Assembly Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Elimination, Coupling Solve, and Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact structure-preserving elimination for independent local blocks coupled through shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[D_iu_i+B_iv=r_i,\qquad \sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}u_i+Cv=r_0,\] factor each nonsingular \(D_i\) independently, form \[S=C-\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}D_i^{-1}B_i,\qquad g=r_0-\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}D_i^{-1}r_i,\] solve \(Sv=g\), and recover \(u_i=D_i^{-1}(r_i-B_iv)\). Under nonsingularity of every \(D_i\), the full system has a unique solution exactly when \(S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor and eliminate local blocks independently, solve the coupling Schur complement, and recover local directions by back-substitution.
assumptions_latex: All blocks and right-hand sides have conformal dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sv=g,\qquad u_i=D_i^{-1}(r_i-B_iv),\qquad\text{and the recovered tuple solves the original system}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Elimination, Coupling Solve, and Recovery

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decomposition Elimination Work, Storage, and Communication Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical dense local algebra with distributed Schur contributions and a dense coupling solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_i\) have order \(n_i\), let the coupling block have order \(s\), and assign one local block to each of \(p\) workers. Dense local factorization and Schur assembly require \[O\!\left(\sum_i(n_i^3+n_i^2s+n_is^2)\right)\] arithmetic and \(O(\sum_i(n_i^2+n_is))\) local storage. If each worker communicates one dense symmetric Schur contribution and reduced right-hand side, aggregate communication is \(O(ps^2)\) words before reduction. Dense coupling factorization adds \(O(s^3)\) work and \(O(s^2)\) storage; sparse or iterative coupling solvers replace these terms with their own fill or iteration models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition-aware elimination separates parallel local factorization and Schur assembly from communication and the final coupling solve.
assumptions_latex: Classical dense algebra is used within local blocks.
Each of \(p\) workers sends one dense order-\(s\) Schur contribution.
The coupling solve is dense unless another solver is explicitly selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T=O\!\left(\sum_i(n_i^3+n_i^2s+n_is^2)+s^3\right),\quad M=O\!\left(\sum_i(n_i^2+n_is)+s^2\right),\quad W_{\mathrm{comm}}=O(ps^2).

notation.meaning: Number of local blocks or workers

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Elimination Work, Storage, and Communication Model
Decomposition-Aware Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local elimination that preserves the coupling structure of decomposed Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block equations \(D_i u_i+B_i v=r_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^pB_i^{\mathsf T}u_i+Cv=r_0\), independently compute \(D_i^{-1}r_i\) and operator actions by \(D_i^{-1}B_i\). Solve the coupling equation \[\left(C-\sum_{i=1}^pB_i^{\mathsf T}D_i^{-1}B_i\right)v=r_0-\sum_{i=1}^pB_i^{\mathsf T}D_i^{-1}r_i.\] Recover each local direction as \(u_i=D_i^{-1}(r_i-B_iv)\). The algorithm forms no fill between distinct local blocks; communication occurs only through the coupling equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate independent local blocks in parallel, solve the resulting coupling Schur complement, and recover each local direction by back-substitution.
assumptions_latex: All displayed blocks have conformal dimensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered \((u_1,\ldots,u_p,v)\) solves the original block system whenever the coupling Schur complement is nonsingular.

children.title: Low-Rank SDP Operators

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^n\) has trace inner product \(\langle X,Z\rangle_{\mathrm{tr}}=\operatorname{tr}(XZ)\), and \(\mathbb R^m\) has its Euclidean inner product.
\(\mathcal T:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb S^n\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N=\mathcal A\mathcal T\mathcal A^*\), \(y^{\mathsf T}\mathcal Ny=\|\mathcal T^{1/2}\mathcal A^*y\|_F^2\), and \(\mathcal N\succ0\iff\ker\mathcal A^*=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint under the trace and Euclidean inner products
Self-adjoint positive-definite inverse-Hessian or scaling action

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-specific composition of low-rank SDP measurement data with a self-adjoint positive-definite metric operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\mathcal A(X)_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle_{\mathrm{tr}}\), the adjoint under the trace and Euclidean inner products is \[\mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_i y_iA_i=\sum_i y_iU_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}.\] For a self-adjoint positive-definite Newton metric action \(\mathcal T\), the reduced normal operator \(\mathcal N=\mathcal A\mathcal T\mathcal A^*\) satisfies \[y^{\mathsf T}\mathcal Ny=\langle\mathcal A^*y,\mathcal T(\mathcal A^*y)\rangle_{\mathrm{tr}}=\|\mathcal T^{1/2}\mathcal A^*y\|_F^2.\] Hence \(\mathcal N\succeq0\), and \(\mathcal N\succ0\) exactly when \(\mathcal A^*\) is injective. The action may form \(\mathcal A^*y\) from thin factors, apply \(\mathcal T\), and remeasure with \(\mathcal A\); retaining thin-factor intermediates through the metric action additionally requires compatible structure in \(\mathcal T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank SDP data enter the Newton normal operator through an explicitly defined adjoint and positive metric action; the result is a Gram operator, while factor retention through the metric requires compatible structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-Rank Data in the Newton Normal Operator
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Data in the Newton Normal Operator
Low-Rank SDP Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factored evaluation of semidefinite measurement operators with low-rank data matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the semidefinite measurement operator be \(\mathcal A(X)_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\), where \(A_i=U_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\), \(U_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_i}\), and \(C_i\in\mathbb S^{r_i}\). Then \[\mathcal A(X)_i=\operatorname{tr}(C_iU_i^{\mathsf T}XU_i),\qquad \mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m y_iU_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}.\] Thus operator and adjoint actions can retain the factors \((U_i,C_i)\) and need not store each \(A_i\) as a dense \(n\)-by-\(n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each low-rank SDP data matrix by factors, enabling measurement and adjoint actions without storing dense matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(X)_i=\operatorname{tr}(C_iU_i^{\mathsf T}XU_i)\) and \(\mathcal A^*(y)=\sum_i y_iU_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\).

children.title: Spectral SDP Compression
children.top_down_role: Spectral representations used to compress semidefinite linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral SDP Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best rank-limited spectral compression of a positive-semidefinite matrix in Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have eigendecomposition \(X=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\), with \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\). For \(0\leq r<n\), define \(X_r=Q_r\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)Q_r^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(X_r\) minimizes \(\lVert X-Y\rVert_F\) over \(Y\in\mathbb S_+^n\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\leq r\), and \(\lVert X-X_r\rVert_F^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^n\lambda_j^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncating a positive-semidefinite matrix to its leading eigenpairs gives a best rank-limited positive-semidefinite approximation in Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_r\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Y\succeq0,\,\operatorname{rank}(Y)\leq r}\lVert X-Y\rVert_F\), with squared error \(\sum_{j>r}\lambda_j^2\).

notation.meaning: matrix of the leading r eigenvectors

review_flags: Confirm that the cited section includes the best rank-r Frobenius approximation statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniqueness condition for the best PSD rank-at-most-r Frobenius approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le r<n\), the Frobenius-norm minimizer over \(Y\succeq0\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le r\) is unique if and only if either \(\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}\) or \(\lambda_r=0\). If \(\lambda_r=\lambda_{r+1}>0\), distinct \(r\)-dimensional choices within the tied positive eigenspace give distinct minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral truncation is uniquely optimal unless a positive eigenvalue tie crosses the rank cutoff; a zero tie is harmless because the matrix already has rank below r.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Y\succeq0,\,\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le r}\|X-Y\|_F\) is a singleton exactly when \(\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}\) or \(\lambda_r=0\).

notation.meaning: Eigenvalues immediately above and below the truncation cutoff.

review_flags: Corrects the Builder's false strict-gap-only criterion when the cutoff eigenvalues are both zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Truncation Uniqueness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-norm best rank-limited approximation of a PSD matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge0\), and let \(X_r\) retain its leading \(r\) eigenpairs. Then \(X_r\) minimizes \(\|X-Y\|_2\) over all matrices \(Y\) of rank at most \(r\), hence also over PSD such matrices, and \(\|X-X_r\|_2=\lambda_{r+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Leading-eigenpair truncation is a best rank-r operator-norm approximation, with error equal to the first discarded eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le r}\|X-Y\|_2=\|X-X_r\|_2=\lambda_{r+1}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Norm Spectral Compression

children.title: Rank-Sensitive Schur Assembly
children.top_down_role: Schur-system assembly organized around effective spectral rank.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-arithmetic cost for cached thin-factor Schur contractions, excluding Schur factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_i=U_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\), with \(U_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_i}\), \(C_i\in\mathbb S^{r_i}\), and \(R=\sum_i r_i\). For dense symmetric \(W\), caching \(V_i=WU_i\) costs \(O(n^2R)\); forming all \(G_{ij}=U_i^{\mathsf T}V_j\) costs \(O(nR^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(R^2)\) storage. Given these factors, all contractions \(\operatorname{tr}(C_iG_{ij}C_jG_{ij}^{\mathsf T})\) cost \(O\!\left(\sum_{i,j}(r_i^2r_j+r_ir_j^2)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Caching scaled thin factors forms all rank-sized cross factors in O(n²R+nR²) work; subsequent Schur contractions use only rank-sized dense products.
assumptions_latex: Classical dense multiplication is used, every ordered cross factor is cached, and lower-order and symmetry savings are omitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_i\) and \(G_{ij}\) require \(O(n^2R+nR^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(R^2)\) cross-factor storage; all stated contractions require \(O(\sum_{i,j}(r_i^2r_j+r_ir_j^2))\) further arithmetic.
review_flags: Conditional cost model; it does not establish which SDP scaling convention defines the solver's Schur operator.
Excludes assembly-output storage and subsequent Schur factorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Cached Rank-Sensitive Assembly Cost

assumptions_latex: The assembled Schur matrix \(S\in\mathbb S^m\) is dense.
A classical dense direct factorization is used after assembly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rank-sensitive entry assembly does not reduce the \(\Theta(m^2)\) storage or \(\Theta(m^3)\) dense-factorization regime of \(S\).

notation.meaning: Number of affine SDP constraints and order of the Schur matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on the end-to-end benefit of rank-sensitive Schur-entry assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Low-rank factors can reduce the arithmetic and intermediate storage used to assemble entries of an SDP Schur matrix, but they do not by themselves reduce the dimension or density of the resulting \(m\)-by-\(m\) matrix. If \(S\) is dense and is factored by a classical dense direct method, storing it still requires \(\Theta(m^2)\) memory and factorizing it still requires \(\Theta(m^3)\) arithmetic, independently of the coefficient ranks. End-to-end solve savings therefore require additional sparsity or structure, or an iterative Schur solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cheaper rank-sensitive entry assembly does not make a dense Schur matrix smaller or cheaper to factor; solve savings require additional structure or a different solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Assembly Savings Do Not Imply Solve Savings
knowledge_statements.title: Assembly Savings Do Not Imply Solve Savings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cached or streamed assembly of one triangle for the declared two-sided scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(i\), compute \(V_i=WU_i\). For each \(1\leq j\leq i\leq m\), form \(G_{ij}=U_i^{\mathsf T}V_j\) and set \[S_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(C_iG_{ij}C_jG_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\right),\qquad S_{ji}=S_{ij}.\] Store one triangle unless the downstream solver requires both. Recompute or stream \(G_{ij}\) rather than caching all cross factors when \(O(R^2)\) auxiliary storage is unacceptable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache scaled thin factors, assemble one triangle from rank-sized contractions, and mirror it; cross factors may instead be streamed.
assumptions_latex: The declared two-sided scaling and thin factorizations satisfy the preceding identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=S^{\mathsf T}\quad\text{is assembled exactly in exact arithmetic for the declared operator}.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Cached Thin-Factor Schur Assembly

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Thin-Factor Schur Entry Identity for a Declared Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank-sensitive identity for the explicitly defined two-sided Schur operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_{ij}=\langle A_i,WA_jW\rangle\) for symmetric \(W\) and factorizations \(A_i=U_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\). With \(G_{ij}=U_i^{\mathsf T}WU_j\), \[S_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(C_iG_{ij}C_jG_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\right).\] The identity is exact for this declared operator and does not assert that every SDP scaling uses \(Z\mapsto WZW\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the explicitly declared two-sided scaling, each Schur entry is an exact contraction of rank-sized cross factors.
assumptions_latex: The Schur matrix is explicitly defined by \(S_{ij}=\langle A_i,WA_jW\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(C_iG_{ij}C_jG_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\right),\qquad G_{ij}=U_i^{\mathsf T}WU_j.

notation.meaning: Schur matrix for the declared two-sided scaling

Rank-Sensitive Schur Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factored Schur-complement entries for low-rank SDP constraint matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric scaling matrix \(W\) and SDP data matrices \(A_i=U_iC_iU_i^{\mathsf T}\), define the Schur matrix by \(S_{ij}=\langle A_i,WA_jW\rangle\). Cyclic invariance of trace gives \[S_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(C_iU_i^{\mathsf T}WU_jC_jU_j^{\mathsf T}WU_i\right).\] Hence each entry can be assembled from the cross factors \(U_i^{\mathsf T}WU_j\), whose dimensions are \(r_i\)-by-\(r_j\), rather than by first forming the dense matrices \(WA_jW\). The storage and arithmetic can therefore depend on the ranks \(r_i,r_j\) as well as the ambient order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute SDP Schur entries from small cross factors between low-rank constraint matrices, avoiding explicit dense scaled matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}(C_iU_i^{\mathsf T}WU_jC_jU_j^{\mathsf T}WU_i)\).

children.title: Chordally Decomposed Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Clique-based cone representations and consistency-system linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on computational savings from clique decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Chordal decomposition alone gives no strict reduction in Newton-solve complexity. A chordal extension containing a clique of order \(\Theta(n)\), or a separator or affine-coupling reduction that becomes dense at a dimension comparable to the undecomposed reduced system, can eliminate the anticipated saving.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large fill cliques or dense global coupling can erase the computational advantage of chordal decomposition.
assumptions_latex: n\text{ is the order of the undecomposed semidefinite matrix}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Chordal representability does not by itself imply a cheaper Newton solve.}
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Decomposition Cost Boundary

assumptions_latex: Dense symmetric storage and classical dense eigendecomposition are used within each clique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{clique}}=\sum_kd_k\), local storage is \(O(\!\sum_kc_k^2)\), and local spectral work is \(O(\!\sum_kc_k^3)\); these do not bound the global consistency-system factorization.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the symmetric clique-variable space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionally explicit accounting for clique-cone variables and local spectral operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric clique variable of order \(c_k\) has vector-space dimension \(d_k=c_k(c_k+1)/2\). Storing all clique matrices densely requires \(O(\sum_kc_k^2)\) memory, and one dense spectral factorization or eigendecomposition per clique requires \(O(\sum_kc_k^3)\) arithmetic. These are clique-cone operation costs, not a bound for factorizing the vectorized Newton or consistency system, whose dimension, sparsity, and fill depend on the chosen primal or dual formulation and affine coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique matrices require quadratic local storage and cubic local spectral work in their orders; the global Newton factorization must be costed from its own dimension and fill.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Local Dimension and Work Accounting

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S_G^n\) is the space of symmetric matrices supported on the diagonal and edges of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb S_G^n=\sum_{k=1}^q E_k^{\mathsf T}\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}E_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual sparse-cone representation used by chordally decomposed SDP Newton formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For chordal \(G\), every \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb S_G^n\) admits clique-supported matrices \(Z_k\succeq0\) such that \(Z=\sum_{k=1}^qE_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k\). Conversely, every such sum is positive semidefinite and supported on \(G\). Thus the dual sparse-cone formulation uses clique variables coupled through their aggregate sparse matrix; it is distinct from separator-equality copies of a partial primal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordally sparse PSD matrix is exactly a sum of PSD matrices supported on maximal cliques, giving the dual clique-decomposition variant.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Cone Clique Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton assembly and recovery for a fixed primal clique-copy formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Vectorize the clique directions, assemble each clique-local Newton or scaling block, and append the separator equalities associated with a fixed clique tree. Eliminate a chosen clique-local block only when its pivot is nonsingular, solve the resulting separator-and-affine coupling system, and recover eliminated directions by back-substitution. Accept the recovered family as one aggregate sparse direction only when every separator residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assemble clique-local Newton blocks, solve the separator and affine coupling system, and recover a globally consistent sparse direction.
assumptions_latex: A primal clique-copy formulation and fixed clique tree are used.
Every eliminated local pivot is nonsingular.
Redundant affine or overlap equations are removed or handled consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Zero separator residuals certify that the recovered clique directions represent one aggregate sparse direction.}
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Consistency Newton Assembly and Recovery

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse Cholesky accounting for a specified positive-definite global consistency system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be the symmetric positive-definite global consistency or affine-coupling matrix after formulation-specific elimination, and let \(L\) be its Cholesky factor under a fixed ordering. If \(\ell_j\) is the stored length of column \(j\) of \(L\), then \[\operatorname{storage}=\Theta(\operatorname{nnz}(L)),\qquad \operatorname{work}=\Theta\!\left(\sum_j\ell_j^2\right)\] for classical sparse numeric factorization. Clique orders alone therefore do not determine global work or storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global consistency solve is governed by fill in its own factor, not solely by the SDP clique sizes.
assumptions_latex: A fixed sparse Cholesky ordering and classical numeric factorization are used.
\(\ell_j\) counts stored entries in column \(j\) of \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{storage}=\Theta(\operatorname{nnz}(L)),\qquad \operatorname{work}=\Theta\!\left(\sum_j\ell_j^2\right).

notation.meaning: Sparse Cholesky factor of the global coupling matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Aware Global Consistency Factorization Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally owned consistency representation for Newton directions in a primal clique-copy formulation; the underlying PSD-completion theorem is cross-indexed rather than duplicated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) and clique tree \(T\). Clique directions \(\Delta X_k\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) represent one partial symmetric direction on \(G\) exactly when, for every tree edge \((k,\ell)\) with separator \(S_{k\ell}=C_k\cap C_\ell\), \[E_{S_{k\ell},C_k}\Delta X_kE_{S_{k\ell},C_k}^{\mathsf T}=E_{S_{k\ell},C_\ell}\Delta X_\ell E_{S_{k\ell},C_\ell}^{\mathsf T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique-local Newton directions represent one chordally sparse direction exactly when their entries agree on every clique-tree separator.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree of the maximal cliques of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{\Delta X_k\}_k\text{ represents one partial direction on }G\iff\text{all clique-tree separator equalities hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Copy Newton-Direction Consistency

assumptions_latex: The semidefinite variable has aggregate sparsity pattern \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sparse Newton system is equivalently expressible in clique variables coupled by separator-consistency equations.

notation.meaning: Separator between adjacent cliques in a clique tree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sparse SDP representation using a fixed clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S^{|V|}\) have specified entries only on \(E\) and the diagonal. Associate \(X_k=E_kXE_k^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) with every maximal clique. A chordally decomposed Newton formulation replaces the sparse matrix direction by clique directions \(\Delta X_k\) and imposes, for every clique-tree edge \((k,\ell)\), \[E_{S_{k\ell},C_k}\Delta X_kE_{S_{k\ell},C_k}^{\mathsf T}=E_{S_{k\ell},C_\ell}\Delta X_\ell E_{S_{k\ell},C_\ell}^{\mathsf T}.\] Local cone-scaling and Hessian blocks act separately on the \(\Delta X_k\); the displayed consistency equations are the only coupling required to represent a single aggregate sparse direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal sparse semidefinite Newton direction can be represented by clique directions whose overlapping separator entries agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordally Decomposed Newton Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but no citation supports the chordal completion/decomposition claim. Whether separator consistency is the only coupling depends on the chosen primal or dual decomposition and Newton-system construction, so the asserted equivalence cannot be reviewed reliably without a specific source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder proposal reviewed because the dimension of a clique Newton block was not specified.
