children.title: Multi-Level KKT Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization families for rank deficiency and unstable pivots.

children.title: Primal Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization applied to primal-side system structure.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(H\) by \(H+\rho_p I_n\) defines primal regularization, shifts every eigenvalue by \(\rho_p\), and makes the regularized primal block positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric saddle-point systems with a positive diagonal regularization of a positive-semidefinite primal block.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the symmetric Newton equations \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{pmatrix},\] where \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\). Primal regularization with parameter \(\rho_p>0\) replaces \(H\) by \[H_{\rho_p}:=H+\rho_p I_n\] and therefore uses the coefficient matrix \[\begin{pmatrix}H_{\rho_p}&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}.\] Its eigenvalues satisfy \(\lambda_i(H_{\rho_p})=\lambda_i(H)+\rho_p\). Hence, when \(H\succeq0\), the shifted block is positive definite, although the regularized system is a perturbation of the original Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal regularization adds a positive diagonal shift to a positive-semidefinite primal Newton block, making that block positive definite while perturbing the Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Regularization

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Boundary for Primal-Only KKT Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp nonsingularity condition when the primal block is shifted and the multiplier block remains zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=H+\rho_pI_n\succ0\). Then \[K_p=\begin{pmatrix}P&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\] is nonsingular if and only if \(A\) has full row rank. Its multiplier Schur complement is \(-AP^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), which is negative definite exactly under full row rank. In that case \(\operatorname{inertia}(K_p)=(n,m,0)\). If \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) for some \(y\ne0\), then \(K_p(0,y)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive primal shift makes the primal block definite, but the full primal-only KKT matrix is nonsingular only when the constraint rows are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_p\) is nonsingular iff \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\); otherwise every nonzero \(y\in\ker A^{\mathsf T}\) gives a null vector \((0,y)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Boundary for Primal-Only KKT Regularization

children.title: Dual Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization applied to dual-side system structure.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing the zero multiplier block by \(-\rho_d I_m\) defines dual regularization and makes that block nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric saddle-point systems using the convention of a negative multiplier-block shift.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the symmetric Newton equations \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{pmatrix},\] where \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\). Under the stated sign convention, dual regularization with parameter \(\rho_d>0\) replaces the zero multiplier block by \(-\rho_d I_m\), giving \[K_{\rho_d}:=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\rho_d I_m\end{pmatrix}.\] Equivalently, the second block equation becomes \(A\Delta x-\rho_d\Delta y=r_p\). The multiplier block is then nonsingular, and the primal-feasibility equation is perturbed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual regularization replaces the zero multiplier block by a negative diagonal shift, making that block nonsingular while perturbing the primal-feasibility equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularization

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Regularization Schur Representation and Nonsingularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of the multiplier direction when only the negative multiplier block is regularized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho_d>0\), \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\rho_dI\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{pmatrix}\] is equivalent to \[\left(H+\rho_d^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}A\right)\Delta x=r_d+\rho_d^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}r_p,\qquad \Delta y=\rho_d^{-1}(A\Delta x-r_p).\] The dual-regularized KKT matrix is nonsingular exactly when \(H+\rho_d^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}A\) is nonsingular. If \(H\succeq0\), this is equivalent to \(\ker H\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual regularization yields a primal Schur equation; with a positive-semidefinite primal block, nonsingularity holds exactly when the primal block and constraint matrix have no common null direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system is nonsingular iff \(H+\rho_d^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}A\) is nonsingular; for \(H\succeq0\), iff \(\ker H\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Regularization Schur Representation and Nonsingularity Boundary

children.title: KKT Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization applied to the coupled KKT representation.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two-sided regularized KKT matrix \(K_{\rho_p,\rho_d}\) is nonsingular without a rank assumption on \(A\).

notation.meaning: Identity matrices of orders n and m

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional two-sided diagonal KKT regularization with a positive-semidefinite primal block.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the two-sided regularized KKT matrix by \[K_{\rho_p,\rho_d}:=\begin{pmatrix}H+\rho_p I_n&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\rho_d I_m\end{pmatrix}.\] If \(H\succeq0\), \(\rho_p>0\), and \(\rho_d>0\), then \(K_{\rho_p,\rho_d}\) is nonsingular for every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), including rank-deficient \(A\). Consequently, the regularized Newton equations \[K_{\rho_p,\rho_d}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{pmatrix}\] have a unique solution \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal block is positive semidefinite, positive primal and dual diagonal shifts make the regularized KKT matrix nonsingular even if the constraint Jacobian is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Regularization

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidefinite Inertia of Two-Sided KKT Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur structure and inertia of a two-sided regularized symmetric KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=H+\rho_pI_n\succ0\) and \(\rho_d>0\). The Schur complement of \(P\) in \[K=\begin{pmatrix}P&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\rho_dI_m\end{pmatrix}\] is \[S=-\rho_dI_m-AP^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\prec0.\] Consequently, \(K\) has inertia \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\) for every \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided regularization makes the KKT matrix symmetric quasidefinite, with a positive primal pivot, negative multiplier Schur complement, and exactly n positive and m negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\prec0\) and \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\).

notation.meaning: Numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues

knowledge_statements.title: Quasidefinite Inertia of Two-Sided KKT Regularization

children.title: Regularization-Induced Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy tradeoffs introduced by stabilizing perturbations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample showing that a fixed stabilizing shift need not recover the original Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar system \(Kz=b\) with \(K=[1]\) and \(b=[1]\), the exact direction is \(z_0=1\). With a fixed regularization \(E=[\rho]\), \(\rho>0\), the regularized direction is \(z_\rho=(1+\rho)^{-1}\). Its error and residual in the original equation are \[|z_\rho-z_0|=\frac{\rho}{1+\rho},\qquad |b-Kz_\rho|=\frac{\rho}{1+\rho}.\] Both remain positive while \(\rho\) is fixed and vanish only as \(\rho\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a nonsingular one-dimensional problem retains nonzero direction error and original-equation residual under a fixed positive regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed \(\rho>0\) produces persistent error \(\rho/(1+\rho)\); vanishing \(\rho\) is necessary in this family for exact recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Error Under Fixed Regularization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive shift reduction controlled by the residual in the original KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose trial regularization shifts, compute a regularized direction \(z_k\), and evaluate the original KKT residual \(e_k=r_k-K_kz_k\). Accept the shifts only if \(\|e_k\|\leq\eta_k\mathcal R_k\), where \(\eta_k\downarrow0\); otherwise reduce the shifts and resolve, or report failure at the safeguard limit. For an exact solve of \((K_k+E_k)z_k=r_k\), \(e_k=E_kz_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduce the regularization until its measured error in the original KKT equations satisfies a vanishing forcing tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A positive normalization \(\mathcal R_k\) and forcing sequence \(\eta_k\downarrow0\) are prescribed.
The original KKT residual can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r_k-K_kz_k\|\leq\eta_k\mathcal R_k\quad\text{for every accepted regularized direction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Forced Vanishing Regularization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise perturbation result for a nonsingular KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz_0=r\) and \((K+E)z_E=r\). Then \(z_E=(I+K^{-1}E)^{-1}z_0\) and \(r-Kz_E=Ez_E\). If \(\|K^{-1}E\|<1\) in a subordinate norm, then \(K+E\) is nonsingular and \[\|z_E-z_0\|\leq\frac{\|K^{-1}E\|}{1-\|K^{-1}E\|}\|z_0\|.\] Hence \(\|K^{-1}E_j\|\to0\) implies \(z_{E_j}\to z_0\), while a fixed nonzero shift has no such implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small regularization gives a controlled direction perturbation, and the original KKT residual equals the regularization action.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Regularization Perturbation Bound

assumptions_latex: The unregularized KKT matrix \(K\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing shifts recover the unregularized step, while fixed nonzero shifts generally leave a nonvanishing equation perturbation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local perturbation regimes for a nonsingular finite-dimensional KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Kz_0=r\), define \(z_\rho\) by \((K+E(\rho_p,\rho_d))z_\rho=r\). The vanishing-regularization regime is \(\|K^{-1}E(\rho_p,\rho_d)\|<1\) with \(\max\{\rho_p,\rho_d\}\to0\); then \[\|z_\rho-z_0\|\leq\frac{\|K^{-1}\|\,\|E(\rho_p,\rho_d)\|}{1-\|K^{-1}E(\rho_p,\rho_d)\|}\,\|z_0\|,\] and hence \(z_\rho\to z_0\). In a fixed-regularization regime, \(\|E(\rho_p,\rho_d)\|\not\to0\); the computed direction instead satisfies the original equation with residual \(r-Kz_\rho=E(\rho_p,\rho_d)z_\rho\), which need not vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing regularization recovers the exact KKT step under a small-perturbation condition; fixed regularization can leave a persistent residual in the original equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Induced Perturbation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regime distinction and perturbation estimate are plausible and locally appropriate, but the record has no source. A specific perturbation-analysis reference is required to support the norm condition, bound, and limiting conclusion.

children.title: Residual-Based Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Accuracy recovery after approximate direct or iterative solves.

children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Post-solve accuracy recovery through repeated refinement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual propagation for repeated refinement using a fixed approximate inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be nonsingular and let \(B\) be fixed. For \[r_j=b-Kz_j,\qquad d_j=Br_j,\qquad z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j,\] one has \[r_{j+1}=(I-KB)r_j,\qquad r_j=(I-KB)^jr_0.\] In any subordinate norm, if \(q:=\|I-KB\|<1\), then \[\|r_j\|\leq q^j\|r_0\|,\qquad \|z_j-K^{-1}b\|\leq\|K^{-1}\|q^j\|r_0\|.\] Thus exact-arithmetic stationary refinement converges at least linearly under the contraction condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed approximate inverse, iterative refinement propagates residuals through the correction-error matrix and converges linearly whenever that matrix is a contraction.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is fixed and \(\|I-KB\|<1\) in a subordinate norm.
The displayed residuals and updates are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_j=(I-KB)^jr_0\), and residuals and forward errors converge at least linearly with factor \(q<1\).

notation.meaning: Fixed approximate inverse used for corrections

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Iterative-Refinement Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated residual-based refinement with declared arithmetic and explicit failure handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(z_0\), recompute \(r_j=b-Kz_j\) in the declared residual arithmetic. Return \(z_j\) if \[\|r_j\|\leq\tau(\|K\|\|z_j\|+\|b\|).\] Otherwise approximately solve \(Kd_j=r_j\), update \(z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j\) in the declared update arithmetic, and recompute the residual. Report failure if a residual or correction is nonfinite, the correction solve fails, the update leaves the stored iterate unchanged, residual reduction stagnates for the configured window, or the iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute a reliable residual, solve and accumulate a correction, stop at a backward-error test, and report arithmetic failure or stagnation.
assumptions_latex: Residual, correction, and update arithmetic are declared.
\(\tau>0\), a stagnation rule, and an iteration limit are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|b-Kz_j\|\leq\tau(\|K\|\|z_j\|+\|b\|)\quad\text{or explicit failure is returned}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Iterative-Refinement Workflow

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar divergence caused by a noncontractive correction operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=[1]\), \(b=[1]\), and a correction routine returning \(d_j=-r_j\), the update is \(z_{j+1}=z_j-r_j\) and \(r_{j+1}=1-z_{j+1}=2r_j\). Hence \(r_j=2^jr_0\) whenever \(r_0\ne0\), even with exact residual evaluation and updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correction operator with the wrong sign doubles the residual at every refinement step.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Refinement Divergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perturbed Iterative-Refinement Recurrence and Accuracy Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-precision convergence under an explicit true-residual perturbation recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_j=b-Kz_j\) be the true residual. Suppose the implemented refinement satisfies \[e_{j+1}=Ge_j+\xi_j,\qquad \|G\|\leq q<1.\] If \(\|\xi_j\|\leq\delta\), then \[\|e_j\|\leq q^j\|e_0\|+\frac{1-q^j}{1-q}\delta.\] More generally, if \(\|\xi_j\|\leq au\|e_j\|+\delta\) and \(q+au<1\), then \[\|e_j\|\leq(q+au)^j\|e_0\|+\delta\frac{1-(q+au)^j}{1-q-au}.\] Thus the recurrence contracts geometrically only to its perturbation floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive implemented refinement recurrence converges geometrically to a floor determined by residual, correction, and update perturbations.
assumptions_latex: The implemented iteration admits the displayed true-residual recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|e_j\|\leq(q+au)^j\|e_0\|+\delta\frac{1-(q+au)^j}{1-q-au}.

notation.meaning: Linear part of implemented residual propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed Iterative-Refinement Recurrence and Accuracy Floor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterations to a Prescribed Residual above the Perturbation Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction-count bound implied by the accepted perturbed-contraction model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\|e_j\|\le q^j\|e_0\|+\delta/(1-q)\), where \(0<q<1\). For any \(\varepsilon>\delta/(1-q)\), it suffices that \[j\ge \left\lceil\frac{\log\!\left(\|e_0\|/(\varepsilon-\delta/(1-q))\right)}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil_+,\qquad \lceil t\rceil_+:=\max\{0,\lceil t\rceil\},\] to obtain \(\|e_j\|\le\varepsilon\). This estimate gives no guarantee for \(\varepsilon\le\delta/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contractive refinement reaches any tolerance strictly above its certified perturbation floor in logarithmically many corrections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j\) satisfying the displayed bound implies \(\|e_j\|\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: True residual after refinement step j

knowledge_statements.title: Iterations to a Prescribed Residual above the Perturbation Floor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact outer refinement with correction solves satisfying a uniform normwise backward-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be nonsingular. At step \(j\), suppose \((K+\Delta K_j)d_j=r_j\), where \(r_j=b-Kz_j\), and update \(z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j\) exactly. If \(\theta:=\sup_j\|K^{-1}\Delta K_j\|<1\), then \[r_{j+1}=\Delta K_j(K+\Delta K_j)^{-1}r_j,\qquad \|r_{j+1}\|\leq\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}\|r_j\|.\] Hence \(\theta<1/2\) implies linear residual convergence with factor at most \(\theta/(1-\theta)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded condition-amplified backward errors in the correction solves make exact outer refinement contract when their bound is below one half.
assumptions_latex: Residual formation and iterate updates are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta<1/2\Longrightarrow\|r_j\|\leq\left(\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}\right)^j\|r_0\|.

notation.meaning: Backward perturbation of correction solve j

knowledge_statements.title: Backward-Stable Correction Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient exact-arithmetic convergence criterion for refinement using a fixed approximate inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=I-KB\) for nonsingular \(K\), and let \(r_{j+1}=Gr_j\). Then \(r_j\to0\) for every \(r_0\) if and only if \(\rho(G)<1\). Equivalently, stationary refinement converges to \(K^{-1}b\) from every initial iterate exactly when \(\rho(I-KB)<1\). For every \(q\) satisfying \(\rho(G)<q<1\), there is a constant \(C_q<\infty\) such that \(\|G^j\|\le C_qq^j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationary iterative refinement converges from every initial iterate exactly when its residual-propagation matrix has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: Residual formation and updates are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_j\to0\ \forall r_0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\rho(I-KB)<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Radius Criterion for Stationary Refinement

assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and \(b\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration outputs the first \(z_j\) satisfying the prescribed residual test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based refinement of one nonsingular Newton or KKT linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K\), \(b\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), and an initial approximate solve \(z_0\), repeat for \(j=0,1,\ldots\): compute \[r_j=b-Kz_j,\qquad Kd_j\approx r_j,\qquad z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j.\] Residual formation uses the most accurate available arithmetic, while the correction equation may reuse the existing factorization or preconditioner. Stop and return \(z_j\) when \[\|r_j\|\leq\tau\bigl(\|K\|\,\|z_j\|+\|b\|\bigr),\] or report nonconvergence when a prescribed iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement repeatedly forms the linear-system residual, approximately solves for a correction, updates the Newton direction, and stops at a backward-error tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf and the steps describe standard iterative refinement, but no source is cited. The backward-error stopping test and the precision requirements for residual formation need a numerical linear algebra source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-aware interpretation of a generic approximate linear solve, not specifically iterative refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=K^{-1}b\), \(r=b-Kz\), and \(b\ne0\). In any subordinate norm, \[\frac{\|z-x\|}{\|x\|}\leq\kappa(K)\frac{\|r\|}{\|b\|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual certifies forward accuracy only when combined with a condition-number bound.
assumptions_latex: One subordinate norm is used throughout.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\|r\|}{\|b\|}\leq\frac{\eta}{\kappa(K)}\Longrightarrow\frac{\|z-K^{-1}b\|}{\|K^{-1}b\|}\leq\eta.

notation.meaning: Condition number in the declared norm

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Forward-Error Certificate

children.title: Residual Correction
children.top_down_role: Accuracy recovery organized around correction of linear-system residuals.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Kd=r\) is solvable iff \(r\in\operatorname{range}(K)\); whenever it is solvable, its solution is unique iff \(\ker K=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient matrix of the correction equation
Residual used as the correction right-hand side

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundary for one residual-correction equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The correction equation \(Kd=r\) is solvable exactly when \(r\in\operatorname{range}(K)\). Conditional on solvability, the correction is unique exactly when \(\ker K=\{0\}\); in particular, square nonsingular \(K\) gives a unique correction for every residual. If \(r\notin\operatorname{range}(K)\), exact residual correction is undefined. For example, \(K=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) and \(r=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\) give an inconsistent correction equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correction exists exactly when the residual lies in the coefficient matrix's range, and a square nonsingular matrix gives a unique correction for every residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Correction Equation Solvability Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One correction step for a linear system, excluding repeated refinement and precision-specific casting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=b-Kz\). Choose \(d\) with correction-solve residual \(e=r-Kd\), and set \(z^+=z+d\). Then \[b-Kz^+=e.\] Thus an exact solution of \(Kd=r\) annihilates the residual, whereas an inexact solution replaces the old residual by the correction-solve residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a correction computed from the current residual; the corrected residual equals the correction solve's residual.
assumptions_latex: The equation \(Kd=r\) is solvable when an exact correction is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b-K(z+d)=r-Kd=e.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact and Inexact Residual-Correction Step

assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), and an approximation \(z\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding a computed solution of the residual equation produces a corrected approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One correction step within residual-based iterative refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the residual \(r=b-Kz\), approximately solve the correction equation \[Kd=r\] using the available factorization or iterative linear solver, and set \(z^+=z+d\). If the correction solve has residual \(e=r-Kd\), then the corrected residual satisfies the exact identity \[b-Kz^+=e.\] Thus an exact correction solve annihilates the residual, while an inexact correction replaces the old residual by the correction-solve residual. Accept \(z^+\) when its normwise backward error meets the prescribed tolerance; otherwise use it as the next refinement iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual correction solves for the error indicated by the current residual; the new residual equals the correction solve's own residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Correction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual identity is correct when a correction is computed, but the assumptions do not ensure that the correction equation is solvable, and no source is supplied. A source and an explicit nonsingularity or residual-equation solvability hypothesis are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder proposal reviewed for canonical ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r=b-Kz\), the perturbation \(\Delta b=-r\), \(\Delta K=0\) makes \((K+\Delta K)z=b+\Delta b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual supplies a right-hand-side backward-error witness for any approximate linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Kz=b-r=b+\Delta b\quad\text{with}\quad\Delta b=-r.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Backward-Error Certificate

children.title: Mixed-Precision Accuracy Recovery
children.top_down_role: Refinement regimes combining multiple arithmetic precision levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision failure modes specific to using lower precision for corrections and higher precision for residuals and updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Mixed-precision refinement can fail to recover higher-precision accuracy if the low-precision factors are singular or unusably ill conditioned, if casting the residual to the correction precision loses essential components or overflows or underflows, or if computed corrections are too small to change the higher-precision iterate. Contractivity of an idealized correction map alone does not exclude these finite-precision failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accuracy recovery requires usable low-precision factors, representable correction right-hand sides, and corrections that remain visible when accumulated.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are formed and updates are accumulated in precision \(u_h\).
Correction right-hand sides and solves use a lower precision \(u_\ell>u_h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Failure of factor usability, representability, or update visibility can prevent accuracy recovery.}
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Refinement Breakdown Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-precision refinement with low-precision factors and high-precision residual certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cast \(K\) to precision \(u_\ell\), compute low-precision factors, and obtain an initial solution by low-precision solves. At iteration \(j\), form \(r_j=b-Kz_j\) in precision \(u_h<u_\ell\) and stop only if its high-precision normwise backward error is at most \(\tau\). Scale if needed, cast \(r_j\) to the low format, solve for \(d_j\) with the stored factors, cast the correction back, and accumulate \(z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j\) in precision \(u_h\). Report failure on unusable factors, overflow or destructive underflow during casting, failed solves, invisible updates, residual stagnation, or the iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use low precision for factorization and correction solves while forming residuals, accumulating updates, and certifying backward error in higher precision.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is stored or cast and factorized in precision \(u_\ell\).
Residuals and accumulated iterates use precision \(u_h<u_\ell\).
Casting and arithmetic failures are detectable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A returned iterate satisfies the high-precision backward-error test; otherwise explicit failure is reported.}
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Two-Precision Refinement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract residual contraction with a mixed-precision perturbation floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the true residual be \(e_j=b-Kz_j\). Suppose the computed residual is \(r_j=e_j+f_j\), the computed correction is \(d_j=B_\ell r_j+g_j\), and the stored update is \(z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j+h_j\). If \(\|I-KB_\ell\|\leq q<1\) and \(\|KB_\ell f_j+Kg_j+Kh_j\|\leq\delta\), then \[\|e_j\|\leq q^j\|e_0\|+\frac{1-q^j}{1-q}\delta.\] Thus the residual contracts geometrically to an accuracy floor no larger than \(\delta/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive low-precision correction gives geometric residual reduction, while residual, solve, and update rounding impose an accuracy floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|b-Kz_j\|\leq q^j\|b-Kz_0\|+\delta(1-q^j)/(1-q).

notation.meaning: bound on the combined per-step residual perturbation

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Perturbed-Contraction Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Cast Underflow Can Destroy a Required Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-component stagnation caused by casting a high-precision residual to a narrower correction format.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=I_2\), let the high-precision residual be \(r=(1,\alpha)^{\mathsf T}\), and suppose conversion to the low correction format flushes every positive magnitude below \(\beta\) to zero, where \(0<\alpha<\beta\). The cast residual is \(r_\ell=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\). Even an exact low-format correction solve returns \(d=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), leaving true residual \((0,\alpha)^{\mathsf T}\). Every subsequent cast produces zero in the second component, so refinement cannot reduce it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Casting can erase a necessary residual component and make mixed-precision refinement stagnate despite exact correction solves.
assumptions_latex: Conversion flushes positive magnitudes below \(\beta\) to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The second residual component remains }\alpha\text{ after every subsequent correction.}\)

notation.meaning: Smallest positive magnitude retained under the declared low-format conversion rule

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Cast Underflow Can Destroy a Required Correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage cost for dense two-precision refinement after a reusable low-precision factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dense \(n\times n\) system, let \(F_\ell(n)=\Theta(n^3)\) be the low-precision factorization cost. Each correction requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) high-precision work to form \(b-Kz_j\), \(\Theta(n^2)\) low-precision work for triangular solves, and \(O(n)\) high-precision update work. Thus \(J\) corrections cost \[F_\ell(n)+\Theta(Jn^2)\] scalar operations and use \(\Theta(n^2)\) matrix and factor storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense mixed-precision refinement uses one cubic low-precision factorization and quadratic work per correction.
assumptions_latex: A dense direct factorization and dense residual evaluation are used.
The factors are reused for all \(J\) corrections.
Scalar operations are counted at unit cost by format.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(n,J)=F_\ell(n)+\Theta(Jn^2),\qquad S(n)=\Theta(n^2).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Two-Precision Refinement Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized two-precision refinement with exact outer residuals and updates and backward-stable low-precision correction solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be nonsingular. Suppose each low-precision correction satisfies \((K+\Delta K_j)d_j=r_j\), with \(\|\Delta K_j\|\leq\gamma_\ell u_\ell\|K\|\), while residuals and updates are exact in the outer model. Put \(\theta=\kappa(K)\gamma_\ell u_\ell\). If \(\theta<1/2\), then \[\|r_{j+1}\|\leq\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}\|r_j\|,\qquad \|r_j\|\leq\left(\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}\right)^j\|r_0\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Idealized two-precision refinement contracts when conditioning-amplified low-precision correction error is below one half.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular and one subordinate norm is fixed.
High-precision residual formation and accumulation are exact in the stated model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r_j\|\leq\left(\frac{\kappa(K)\gamma_\ell u_\ell}{1-\kappa(K)\gamma_\ell u_\ell}\right)^j\|r_0\|.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Precision Backward-Stability Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional mixed-precision variant that rescales a residual before conversion to the lower-precision correction format.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a high-precision residual \(r_j\ne0\), if there exists a representable \(\sigma_j>0\) for which every nonzero component of \(\sigma_jr_j\) lies in the usable range of the low-precision format, convert \(\sigma_jr_j\), solve \(K\widetilde d_j\approx\sigma_jr_j\) with the stored low-precision factors, and accumulate \(d_j=\widetilde d_j/\sigma_j\) in high precision. In exact arithmetic this scaling leaves the correction equation unchanged. It can prevent range loss but cannot recover relative-rounding losses or cure unusable factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a common safe scaling exists, scale the residual into the low format's range, solve the scaled correction equation, and unscale before the high-precision update.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular and usable low-precision factors are available.
A representable common scaling places every nonzero residual component in the declared usable low-format range.
Scaling, solving, and unscaling do not overflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\widetilde d_j=\sigma_jr_j\Longrightarrow K(\widetilde d_j/\sigma_j)=r_j\quad\text{in exact arithmetic}.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Scaled Low-Precision Correction Variant

assumptions_latex: Residuals and updates are evaluated in precision \(u_h\).
The factorization and triangular solves use lower precision \(u_\ell\), with \(u_h<u_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure seeks high-precision backward accuracy while reusing a low-precision factorization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-precision refinement for Newton or KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Factor \(K\) once in precision \(u_\ell\) and obtain \(z_0\) from low-precision solves. For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), form \[r_j=b-Kz_j\] in precision \(u_h\), cast \(r_j\) to the low-precision solve format, compute \(d_j\approx K^{-1}r_j\) using the stored low-precision factors, and accumulate \(z_{j+1}=z_j+d_j\) in precision \(u_h\). Return the first iterate satisfying \[\|r_j\|\leq\tau\bigl(\|K\|\,\|z_j\|+\|b\|\bigr);\] otherwise report failure after the iteration limit or upon residual stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-precision refinement uses a low-precision factorization for inexpensive corrections but forms residuals and accumulates updates in higher precision.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Accuracy Recovery

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder proposal reviewed for canonical ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z_{j+1}=z_j+B_\ell(b-Kz_j)\), the condition \(\lVert I-B_\ell K\rVert<1\) implies geometric forward-error contraction in the corresponding induced norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary approximate-inverse iteration converges when its error-propagation operator is contractive.
assumptions_latex: \text{Outer residual and update operations are exact in the stated model}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert z_j-K^{-1}b\rVert\leq\lVert I-B_\ell K\rVert^j\lVert z_0-K^{-1}b\rVert.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Refinement Contraction

children.title: Data Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Pre-solve balancing of numerical magnitudes in conic data.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility Boundary for Uniform Row–Column Norm Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary compatibility of exact uniform Euclidean row and column norms after positive diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=D_rAD_c\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). If every row of \(B\) has Euclidean norm \(\alpha\) and every column has Euclidean norm \(\beta\), then \[m\alpha^2=\|B\|_F^2=n\beta^2.\] Hence prescribed uniform targets require \(m\alpha^2=n\beta^2\). In particular, simultaneous unit row and column norms are impossible when \(m\ne n\). An identically zero row or column cannot be scaled to a positive target by finite positive diagonal factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact uniform row and column targets must have equal total squared norm; rectangular unit targets and positive targets for zero rows or columns are impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are finite positive diagonal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform targets require \(m\alpha^2=n\beta^2\), and zero rows or columns obstruct positive targets.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility Boundary for Uniform Row–Column Norm Targets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Damped alternating row-column equilibration with compatible Euclidean targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D_r=I\), \(D_c=I\). For \(B=D_rAD_c\), update \[D_r\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}\!\left((\alpha/\|e_i^{\mathsf T}B\|_2)^\omega\right)D_r,\] recompute \(B\), and update \[D_c\leftarrow D_c\operatorname{diag}\!\left((\beta/\|Be_j\|_2)^\omega\right).\] Stop when every row and column logarithmic norm error is at most \(\varepsilon\), or report nonconvergence at the iteration limit. One sparse sweep costs \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A))\) arithmetic and stores the two diagonal vectors in addition to \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately damp row and column scalings toward compatible Euclidean norm targets and stop when every multiplicative norm error is small.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has no zero row or column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\log(\|e_i^{\mathsf T}D_rAD_c\|_2/\alpha)|\leq\varepsilon,\quad |\log(\|D_rAD_ce_j\|_2/\beta)|\leq\varepsilon\ \text{at termination}.

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scalings

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Alternating Euclidean Equilibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of diagonal equilibration factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\gamma>0\), \((\gamma D_r)A(\gamma^{-1}D_c)=D_rAD_c\). Thus the factors require a gauge normalization. Each connected component of the bipartite support graph admits an independent reciprocal gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal row and column rescaling leaves the equilibrated matrix unchanged, with one gauge per support component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (D_r,D_c)\sim(\gamma D_r,\gamma^{-1}D_c)\text{ on each support component}.
knowledge_statements.title: Connected-Support Gauge Freedom

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Equilibration as Nonnegative Matrix Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of Euclidean norm targets to prescribed-margin scaling of squared entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=A\circ A\), \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(p)\), \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(q)\), \(u_i=p_i^2\), and \(v_j=q_j^2\). The squared row and column norms of \(D_rAD_c\) are the margins of \(X=\operatorname{diag}(u)B\operatorname{diag}(v)\). Hence Euclidean equilibration to targets \(\alpha_i,\beta_j\) is equivalent to scaling \(A\circ A\) to margins \(\alpha_i^2,\beta_j^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean row-column equilibration is nonnegative matrix scaling of the entrywise-squared data.
assumptions_latex: Requested targets and diagonal factors are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|e_i^{\mathsf T}D_rAD_c\|_2^2=(X\mathbf1)_i,\quad \|D_rAD_ce_j\|_2^2=(X^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1)_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Equilibration as Nonnegative Matrix Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projective Convergence for Full-Support Euclidean Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact alternating scaling rate when the entrywise-squared matrix is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=A\circ A\) be entrywise positive, and let positive margins \(r,c\) satisfy \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}r=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}c\). For the exact alternating row-column scaling map \(T\), Hilbert's projective metric satisfies \[d_H(Tv,Tw)\leq \rho d_H(v,w),\qquad \rho\leq\tanh^2\!\bigl(\Delta(B)/4\bigr)<1,\] where \[\Delta(B)=\log\max_{i,k,j,l}\frac{B_{ij}B_{kl}}{B_{il}B_{kj}}.\] If \(0<\rho<1\), then \(d_H(v_k,v_*)\leq\rho^k d_H(v_0,v_*)\), so \(k\geq\log(d_H(v_0,v_*)/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\) cycles suffice for projective error at most \(\varepsilon\). If \(\rho=0\), the projective factor is attained after one full cycle. Each sparse cycle costs \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A))\) arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With full support, exact alternating Euclidean equilibration contracts geometrically in projective distance; the rank-one zero-diameter case terminates projectively in one cycle.
assumptions_latex: The positive target margins have equal total mass.
Every row and column normalization is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_H(v_k,v_*)\leq\rho^k d_H(v_0,v_*),\qquad \rho\leq\tanh^2(\Delta(B)/4)<1.

notation.meaning: Projective diameter of the positive matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Projective Convergence for Full-Support Euclidean Equilibration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Sensitive Existence and Uniqueness of Euclidean Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence criterion for prescribed Euclidean row and column norms via nonnegative matrix scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=A\circ A\geq0\), let \(r\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), and suppose \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}r=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}c\). Positive diagonal matrices \(U,V\) such that \(X=UBV\), \(X\mathbf1=r\), and \(X^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=c\) exist if and only if there is a nonnegative matrix \(Y\) with \(\operatorname{supp}Y=\operatorname{supp}B\), \(Y\mathbf1=r\), and \(Y^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=c\). Whenever such scaling exists, \(X\) is unique. The factors are unique up to reciprocal multiplication on each connected component of the bipartite support graph. Taking \(D_r=U^{1/2}\) and \(D_c=V^{1/2}\) gives row norms \(\sqrt{r_i}\) and column norms \(\sqrt{c_j}\) for \(D_rAD_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean equilibration exists exactly when the squared-entry support admits the requested margins; the scaled matrix is unique and its factors have componentwise gauge freedom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V\succ0:\ X=UBV,\ X\mathbf1=r,\ X^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=c\iff\exists Y\geq0:\operatorname{supp}Y=\operatorname{supp}B,\ Y\mathbf1=r,\ Y^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=c.

notation.meaning: Entrywise square of the data matrix
Requested squared row- and column-norm margins

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Sensitive Existence and Uniqueness of Euclidean Equilibration

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has no identically zero row or column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Data equilibration selects diagonal scalings that approximately balance row and column norms of \(D_rAD_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal row-column equilibration of conic constraint data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D_r=I\) and \(D_c=I\). Repeatedly compute row norms \(r_i=\|e_i^{\mathsf T}D_rAD_c\|_p\) and column norms \(c_j=\|D_rAD_ce_j\|_p\), then update \[D_r\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(r_i^{-1/2})D_r,\qquad D_c\leftarrow D_c\operatorname{diag}(c_j^{-1/2}).\] Stop when all nonzero row and column norms of \(\widetilde A=D_rAD_c\) lie within a prescribed multiplicative tolerance of their target values. Scale associated right-hand-side and objective data consistently, and retain \(D_r,D_c\) for recovering variables and residuals in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data equilibration iteratively applies positive diagonal row and column scalings so the scaled constraint matrix has approximately balanced row and column norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Data Equilibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a recognizable diagonal equilibration scheme and fits the leaf, but the simultaneous inverse-square-root update for a general p-norm is method dependent and uncited. A specific equilibration source is required.

children.title: Constraint Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling regimes focused on constraint rows or blocks.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is diagonal and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Left scaling preserves the primal feasible set, transforms equality multipliers by \(y=D_r^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y\), and maps scaled residuals back by \(r_p=D_r^{-1}\widetilde r_p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsingular diagonal scaling of conic equality constraints.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace the equality constraint \(Ax=b\) by \[\widetilde A x=\widetilde b,\qquad \widetilde A:=D_rA,\qquad \widetilde b:=D_rb.\] Because \(D_r\) is nonsingular, \(Ax=b\) if and only if \(\widetilde A x=\widetilde b\), so the primal feasible set is unchanged. If \(\widetilde y\in\mathbb R^m\) is the multiplier for the scaled equality and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is the multiplier in the original coordinates, then \[y=D_r^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y.\] For the residuals \(r_p=b-Ax\) and \(\widetilde r_p=\widetilde b-\widetilde A x\), one has \(\widetilde r_p=D_rr_p\), hence \[r_p=D_r^{-1}\widetilde r_p.\] Termination tests stated for the original problem must use the reconstructed original-coordinate residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular row scaling preserves the equality-constrained feasible set, transforms equality multipliers by the transpose scaling, and maps scaled residuals back through the inverse scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Scaling

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning under nonsingular diagonal row scaling of a full-column-rank equality matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full column rank and \(D_r\) is nonsingular, then \[\kappa_2(D_rA)\leq\kappa_2(D_r)\kappa_2(A),\qquad \kappa_2(A)\leq\kappa_2(D_r)\kappa_2(D_rA).\] Thus row scaling preserves rank but need not improve conditioning. For \(A=I_n\) and \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon,1,\ldots,1)\), \(\kappa_2(D_rA)=\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular row scaling preserves rank but can worsen the spectral condition number arbitrarily; the change is controlled by the scaling matrix's condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full column rank.
\(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular and diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(D_rA)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\), while conditioning can deteriorate arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Boundary for Constraint Scaling

children.title: Cone-Data Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling regimes tailored to conic variables and cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which coordinate scaling preserves the declared cone rather than replacing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an invertible linear map \(T\), the scaled variable remains in the same cone \(K\) exactly when \(T\) is a cone automorphism: \(T(K)=K\). Positive diagonal maps are automorphisms of \(\mathbb R_+^n\), and nonsingular congruences \(Z\mapsto RZR^{\mathsf T}\) are automorphisms of the PSD cone. A general invertible map instead replaces \(K\) by \(T^{-1}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only cone automorphisms preserve the named cone; arbitrary invertible coordinate changes require transforming the cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T^{-1}K=K\iff T(K)=K.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Preserving Scaling Specialization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic equivalence does not imply improved numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\succ0\) and invertible \(T\), \[\kappa_2(T^{\mathsf T}HT)\leq\kappa_2(T)^2\kappa_2(H).\] Families attain quadratic amplification in \(\kappa_2(T)\), so a valid cone-coordinate transformation can substantially worsen Euclidean Hessian conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid coordinate scaling can amplify Hessian conditioning quadratically in the transformation's condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(T^{\mathsf T}HT)\leq\kappa_2(T)^2\kappa_2(H).

notation.meaning: unscaled SPD barrier or Newton Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Coordinate Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and Hessian transformation for a barrier expressed in scaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled barrier gradient transforms by the transpose and its Hessian by congruence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2\widetilde F(z)=T^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(Tz)T.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Derivatives Under Coordinate Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual equivalence under an invertible cone-coordinate transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), and dual convention \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), set \(x=Tz\), where \(T\) is invertible. Then \(\widetilde A=AT\), \(\widetilde c=T^{\mathsf T}c\), and \(\widetilde K=T^{-1}K\). With \(\widetilde s=T^{\mathsf T}s\), one has \(\widetilde K^*=T^{\mathsf T}K^*\), \(\widetilde A^{\mathsf T}y+\widetilde s=\widetilde c\), and \(\langle\widetilde s,z\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\). Recovery is \(x=Tz\) and \(s=T^{-\mathsf T}\widetilde s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible cone-coordinate change bijectively transforms the primal variable, affine data, dual cone, and slack while preserving objective values and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde K=T^{-1}K,\quad \widetilde K^*=T^{\mathsf T}K^*,\quad \langle T^{\mathsf T}s,z\rangle=\langle s,Tz\rangle.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Cone-Coordinate Equivalence

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution \(x=Tz\) maps \(x\in K\) to \(z\in T^{-1}K\), while dual slacks transform as \(\widetilde s=T^{\mathsf T}s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible coordinate scaling of a finite-dimensional conic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic program with \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), and objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), set \(x=Tz\). The scaled data are \[\widetilde A=AT,\qquad \widetilde c=T^{\mathsf T}c,\qquad \widetilde K=T^{-1}K,\] so \(x\in K\) if and only if \(z\in\widetilde K\), and the objective value is unchanged. If \(s\in K^*\) is the original dual slack, define \(\widetilde s=T^{\mathsf T}s\); then \(\widetilde s\in\widetilde K^*\) and complementarity is invariant because \[\langle \widetilde s,z\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle.\] When \(T(K)=K\), the cone itself is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible cone-coordinate scaling transforms primal variables, data, and dual slacks consistently while preserving feasibility, objective values, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Data Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate transformation, transformed dual slack, and complementarity identity are mathematically coherent and the representation kind fits. However, the record has no citation, so the cone and dual-cone transformation claims require a specific conic optimization source.

children.title: Dynamic Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical scaling adjusted during the interior-point solve.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noninvariance of Scaled Residual Stopping Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw scaled-residual tolerances under iteration-dependent nonsingular row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an original residual \(r\ne0\) and scaled residual \(\widetilde r_k=D_kr\), no absolute stopping threshold on \(\|\widetilde r_k\|\) is invariant under unrestricted nonsingular diagonal \(D_k\). Taking \(D_k=\varepsilon I\) gives \(\|\widetilde r_k\|=\varepsilon\|r\|\), which can satisfy any positive scaled tolerance while \(r\) is unchanged. Therefore dynamic rescaling must evaluate termination after reconstructing the original residual, or use a rigorously transformation-invariant normalized test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing row scaling can make a fixed nonzero residual appear arbitrarily small, so dynamic regimes cannot terminate from raw scaled residuals alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Raw tests on \(\|D_kr\|\) are not invariant under dynamic scaling; original-coordinate or invariant tests are required.
knowledge_statements.title: Noninvariance of Scaled Residual Stopping Tests

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility, state transport, and invariant validation for an externally triggered scaling update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the enclosing solver invokes a scaling update, construct candidate invertible maps \(T_{k+1},D_{k+1}\). Reject the update if it violates the declared cone-compatibility or conditioning safeguards or produces nonfinite data. Otherwise transport \[z^{\rm new}=T_{k+1}^{-1}T_kz^{\rm old},\quad \widetilde y^{\rm new}=D_{k+1}^{-\mathsf T}D_k^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y^{\rm old},\quad \widetilde s^{\rm new}=T_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}T_k^{-\mathsf T}\widetilde s^{\rm old}.\] Transport directions by the corresponding linear maps. After solving the transformed Newton equations, reconstruct primal feasibility, stationarity, cone membership, complementarity, and objective gap in original coordinates before accepting termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A triggered scaling update must be admissible and finite, transport the complete primal-dual state exactly, and retain original-coordinate termination tests.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted \(T_k,D_k\) is invertible and satisfies the declared cone-compatibility rule.
Original-coordinate primal-dual diagnostics can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Accepted updates are bijective coordinate changes, and termination uses original-coordinate diagnostics.}

notation.meaning: scaled primal variable, multiplier, and slack

knowledge_statements.title: Guarded Dynamic-Scaling Transport Protocol

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarded trigger layered on exact state transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\theta_{\rm on}>\theta_{\rm off}\geq1\), spacing \(h\geq1\), and \(\kappa_{\max}\). Propose rescaling only when a declared original-coordinate imbalance \(q_k\geq\theta_{\rm on}\) and at least \(h\) iterations have elapsed. Accept candidate maps only if they are finite, cone compatible, bounded in condition number by \(\kappa_{\max}\), and satisfy a declared original-coordinate residual safeguard after exact state transport; otherwise restore the previous maps and state. Re-enable proposals only after \(q_k\leq\theta_{\rm off}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use hysteresis and spacing to trigger rescaling, enforce cone, conditioning, and residual safeguards, and roll back rejected updates.
assumptions_latex: The imbalance diagnostic and acceptance residual are evaluated in original coordinates.
Candidate maps use the accepted exact transport protocol.
Thresholds and rollback state are fixed before each proposal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every accepted update satisfies spacing, hysteresis, compatibility, conditioning, and residual safeguards.}
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Triggered Dynamic Rescaling with Rollback

assumptions_latex: Each scaling matrix \(T_k\) is invertible and each row scaling \(D_k\) is nonsingular.
All residuals and termination tests can be mapped to original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dynamic scaling is valid only when every iterate, direction, multiplier, and residual is consistently transported between successive coordinate systems.

notation.meaning: Variable and constraint scalings at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent invertible scaling with original-coordinate stopping tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose \(T_k,D_k\), form \[\widetilde A_k=D_kAT_k,\qquad \widetilde b_k=D_kb,\qquad \widetilde c_k=T_k^{\mathsf T}c,\] map the current state into scaled coordinates, solve the scaled Newton system for \(\Delta z_k\), and recover \(\Delta x_k=T_k\Delta z_k\). If the scaling changes, transport the state by \[z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{new}}=T_{k+1}^{-1}T_kz_{k+1}^{\mathrm{old}}\] and apply the corresponding inverse-transpose map to dual slacks. Accept termination only after residuals are reconstructed in the original coordinates; otherwise scaling changes could alter the apparent stopping accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic scaling periodically changes coordinates, transports the full primal-dual state consistently, solves the scaled Newton system, and evaluates stopping criteria in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Scaling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the dynamic-scaling leaf, but no source supports the iteration-dependent state transport, dual transformation, or stopping protocol. Update frequency and safeguards are solver dependent, so a specific dynamic-scaling reference is required.

children.title: Conic Error Measures
children.top_down_role: Forward, backward, and regularized error organizations for conic systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backward error for a quadratic inequality system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines feasibility and aggregate positive-part violation for convex or quasiconvex quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i:\mathbb R^l\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be convex or quasiconvex quadratic functions. Define \(\mathcal S:=\{y\in\mathbb R^l:g_i(y)\le 0\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,m\}\). The backward error at \(y\) is \(E_b(y):=\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(y)]_+\). Since each \(g_i\) is quadratic, \(g_i(y)=g_i(0)+\nabla g_i(0)^Ty+\tfrac12y^T\nabla^2g_i\,y\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^l\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a system of convex or quasiconvex quadratic inequalities, the backward error of a point is the sum of the positive constraint violations. Each constraint has its exact second-order expansion about zero.
assumptions_latex: g_i:\mathbb R^l\to\mathbb R\text{ is a convex or quasiconvex quadratic for }i=1,\ldots,m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal S=\{y:g_i(y)\le0\ \forall i\},\qquad E_b(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(y)]_+.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward and backward errors for a conic feasibility system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines residual-based backward error and solution-set forward error for feasibility in the intersection of a symmetric cone and an affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasibility system be \(x\in\mathcal K\cap(b+\mathcal A)\), where \(\mathcal K\) has spectral minimum eigenvalue \(\lambda_{\min}\), and fix a norm for distance. The cone violation is \([ -\lambda_{\min}(x)]_+\), the affine violation is \(\operatorname{dist}(x,b+\mathcal A)\), and the backward error is \(\operatorname{dist}(x,b+\mathcal A)+[-\lambda_{\min}(x)]_+\). The forward error is the distance from \(x\) to the solution set \(\mathcal K\cap(b+\mathcal A)\). Small backward error need not by itself determine small forward error; an error bound is needed to relate them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a conic feasibility system, backward error is the sum of the distance to the affine constraint and the positive part of the negated minimum cone eigenvalue. Forward error is the distance to the original solution set. Relating forward error to backward error requires an error bound.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal K\text{ is a cone with }x\in\mathcal K\iff\lambda_{\min}(x)\ge 0
b+\mathcal A\text{ is an affine subspace}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{berr}(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,b+\mathcal A)+[-\lambda_{\min}(x)]_+,\qquad \operatorname{ferr}(x)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\mathcal K\cap(b+\mathcal A)\bigr).

source_evidence.locator: Error Analysis / 7.2. Preliminaries / Definition 7.2-extra-1

children.title: Forward Error
children.top_down_role: Error regimes based on displacement of computed solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance from a reported point to the exact conic feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\). For \(\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat x;A,b,K):=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,\mathcal F)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal F}\|\widehat x-x\|_2,
\]
with \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,\varnothing):=+\infty\). This is feasibility forward error; replacing \(\mathcal F\) by an optimal-solution set defines a different output measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute forward error is the distance from the reported point to the exact feasible set, with value infinity when that set is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat x;A,b,K)=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,\{x\in K:Ax=b\}).
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Forward Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-set, attainment, and stability properties for a nonempty conic feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\), then \(\mathcal F\) is closed and convex. Consequently, the Euclidean infimum defining \(e_{\mathrm f}\) is attained, the projection onto \(\mathcal F\) is unique,
\[
e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat x)=0\iff \widehat x\in\mathcal F,
\]
and
\[
|e_{\mathrm f}(x)-e_{\mathrm f}(y)|\le\|x-y\|_2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty conic feasible set, forward error has a unique nearest feasible point, vanishes exactly on the feasible set, and is one-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_{\mathrm f}^{-1}(0)=\mathcal F,\qquad |e_{\mathrm f}(x)-e_{\mathrm f}(y)|\le\|x-y\|_2.

notation.meaning: zero set of the forward-error function

knowledge_statements.title: Forward-Error Distance Properties
Forward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute forward error for a conic feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone and let \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\). For an approximate point \(\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n\), its absolute forward error is
\[
 e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat x;A,b,K):=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,\mathcal F)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal F}\|\widehat x-x\|_2.
\]
Thus the forward error measures displacement in solution space, rather than violation of the supplied conic equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward error is the Euclidean distance from an approximate point to the exact feasible set of the given conic system.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat x;A,b,K)=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,\mathcal F)\).
review_flags: Exact conic forward-error convention requires an authoritative source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, but the chosen absolute forward-error convention lacks a source, and the domains of A and b are not introduced.

children.title: Backward Error
children.top_down_role: Error regimes based on perturbations to the represented problem data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-cone joint Frobenius–Euclidean perturbation model for conic equality feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n\). Define
\[
e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat x;A,b,K):=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\inf_{\Delta A,\Delta b}\left\{\bigl(\|\Delta A\|_F^2+\|\Delta b\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}:(A+\Delta A)\widehat x=b+\Delta b\right\},&\widehat x\in K,\\
+\infty,&\widehat x\notin K.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(\widehat x\in K\),
\[
e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat x;A,b,K)=\frac{\|A\widehat x-b\|_2}{\sqrt{1+\|\widehat x\|_2^2}}.
\]
Consequently, \(e_{\mathrm b}=0\) exactly when \(\widehat x\in K\) and \(A\widehat x=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the cone fixed, absolute backward error is the smallest joint perturbation of A and b making the reported point exactly feasible; it has an explicit residual formula.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
Only \(A\) and \(b\) are perturbed, using the displayed product norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x\in K\Longrightarrow e_{\mathrm b}=\|A\widehat x-b\|_2/\sqrt{1+\|\widehat x\|_2^2},\qquad e_{\mathrm b}=0\iff \widehat x\in K,\ A\widehat x=b.
review_flags: This is one explicit backward-error convention; componentwise, relative, and cone-perturbation models have different values.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Normwise Backward Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of unnormalized data perturbation on equation scaling and the admissible perturbation blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The value of a backward error is defined only relative to specified perturbable data blocks and a specified norm or scaling. In particular, replacing \((A,b)\) by \((\alpha A,\alpha b)\) with \(\alpha>0\) leaves the exact feasible set unchanged but changes the absolute joint backward error to
\[
\frac{\alpha\|A\widehat x-b\|_2}{\sqrt{1+\|\widehat x\|_2^2}}.
\]
Thus an absolute backward error is not invariant under equivalent rescaling of the represented equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute backward error depends on the chosen data representation, perturbation blocks, and scaling even when the exact feasible set is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The absolute joint perturbation model in the preceding record is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F(A,b,K)=\mathcal F(\alpha A,\alpha b,K)\quad\text{but}\quad e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat x;\alpha A,\alpha b,K)=\alpha e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat x;A,b,K).
knowledge_statements.title: Backward-Error Representation Dependence
Backward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute normwise data perturbation for conic equality feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For \(\widehat x\in K\), define the absolute backward error by
\[
 e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat x;A,b,K):=\inf\left\{\bigl(\|\Delta A\|_F^2+\|\Delta b\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}:(A+\Delta A)\widehat x=b+\Delta b\right\}.
\]
It is the smallest normwise perturbation of the equality data for which the reported point is exactly conically feasible; it equals \(+\infty\) when \(\widehat x\notin K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward error is the smallest perturbation of the equality data that makes the reported cone-feasible point an exact solution.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
Data perturbations are measured by \(\bigl(\|\Delta A\|_F^2+\|\Delta b\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm b}\) is the minimum data perturbation making \(\widehat x\) exactly feasible.
review_flags: The chosen normwise perturbation model needs an exact source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The particular joint Frobenius–Euclidean perturbation model requires a source. The definition assumes the reported point lies in K but then assigns a value outside K without formally extending its domain.

children.title: Error-Measure Disagreement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which forward-error and backward-error assessments differ materially.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioned scalar family separating absolute forward and backward errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(K=\mathbb R_+\), \(A_\varepsilon=[\varepsilon]\), \(b=0\), and \(\widehat x=1\). The feasible set is \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon=\{0\}\). Under the absolute forward-error distance and joint \((\Delta A,\Delta b)\) backward-error conventions,
\[
e_{\mathrm f}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,K)=1,
\qquad
e_{\mathrm b}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,K)=\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt2}.
\]
Hence \(e_{\mathrm b}\to0\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), while \(e_{\mathrm f}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a scalar ill-conditioned family, backward error tends to zero while forward error remains one.
assumptions_latex: The absolute forward-error and joint absolute backward-error conventions of the sibling leaves are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_{\mathrm b}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,\mathbb R_+)\to0\quad\text{while}\quad e_{\mathrm f}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,\mathbb R_+)=1.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar ill-conditioned family separating absolute forward and backward errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
e_{\mathrm f}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,K)=1,
\qquad
e_{\mathrm b}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,K)=\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt2}.
\]
Consequently, \(e_{\mathrm b}\to0\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), while \(e_{\mathrm f}=1\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm b}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,\mathbb R_+)\to0\) while \(e_{\mathrm f}(1;A_\varepsilon,0,\mathbb R_+)=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Backward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A face-aware perturbation measure allowing regularized correction of the reported point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a closed face of a closed convex cone \(K\), let \(\widehat x\in K\), and fix \(\lambda>0\). Define the face-regularized backward error of \(A x=b\), \(x\in F\), by
\[
 e_{\mathrm{rb},\lambda}(\widehat x;A,b,F):=\inf_{y\in F,\,\Delta A,\,\Delta b}\left\{\bigl(\|\Delta A\|_F^2+\|\Delta b\|_2^2+\lambda\|y-\widehat x\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}:(A+\Delta A)y=b+\Delta b\right\}.
\]
The final term regularizes corrections caused by rank deficiency or confinement to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This face-aware error balances data perturbation against movement of the reported point to an exact solution on a selected cone face.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a closed face of the closed convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm{rb},\lambda}\) is the displayed regularized minimum over face-feasible corrections and data perturbations.

notation.meaning: Selected face supporting the reduced conic system

review_flags: No supplied locator fixes a canonical definition of regularized backward error.
The face-aware convention requires specialist review.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal-Face Component Error Bound from Singularity Degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the facial-reduction sequence defining singularity degree and the source-specific U(z),N(z) decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that for every 0<\epsilon\leq1, \operatorname{dist}(x(\epsilon),\overline{\mathcal A})\leq\epsilon and \lambda_{\min}(x(\epsilon))\geq-\epsilon. Let d=d(\overline{\mathcal A},\mathcal K), z=z^{d+1}, and \gamma=2^{-d}. Then \operatorname{face}(\mathcal K,z) is the minimal cone for \mathcal A and \[\|x_{U(z)}(\epsilon)\|+\|x_{N(z)}(\epsilon)\|=O\!\left(\epsilon^{\gamma}\|x(\epsilon)\|^{1-\gamma}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After one step beyond the singularity degree, the facial-reduction sequence identifies the minimal cone. The components transverse to that face satisfy a Hölder-type error estimate with exponent two to the negative singularity degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{face}(\mathcal K,z)\text{ is the minimal cone for }\mathcal A,\qquad \|x_{U(z)}(\epsilon)\|+\|x_{N(z)}(\epsilon)\|=O\!\left(\epsilon^{\gamma}\|x(\epsilon)\|^{1-\gamma}\right).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source-specific orthogonal face decomposition indexed by a cone element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \overline{\mathcal A}\subseteq\mathbb R^N be a linear subspace, z\in\mathcal K, and suppose that for every 0<\epsilon\leq1, \operatorname{dist}(x(\epsilon),\mathcal A)\leq\epsilon, \|x_{U(z)}(\epsilon)\|+\|x_{N(z)}(\epsilon)\|\leq\epsilon, and \lambda_{\min}(x(\epsilon))\geq-\epsilon. If y\in\operatorname{relint}(\overline{\mathcal A}^{\perp}\cap\operatorname{face}(\mathcal K,z)^*) and z'=z+y_{B(z)}, then z'\in\mathcal K and \|x_{N(z')}(\epsilon)\|=O(\epsilon). If (y,z) is regular, then \|x_{U(z')}(\epsilon)\|\leq\|x_{U(z)}(\epsilon)\|=O(\epsilon); otherwise \|x_{U(z')}(\epsilon)\|=O\!\left(\sqrt{\epsilon\|x(\epsilon)\|}\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exposing-direction update remains in the cone and reduces the new null component to order epsilon. Under regularity the unresolved component is also order epsilon; without regularity it is bounded by the square root of epsilon times the norm of the approximate point.
assumptions_latex: \overline{\mathcal A}\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ is a linear subspace},\quad z\in\mathcal K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z'\in\mathcal K,\quad \|x_{N(z')}(\epsilon)\|=O(\epsilon),\quad \|x_{U(z')}(\epsilon)\|\leq\|x_{U(z)}(\epsilon)\|=O(\epsilon)\ \text{if }(y,z)\text{ is regular},\quad \|x_{U(z')}(\epsilon)\|=O\!\left(\sqrt{\epsilon\|x(\epsilon)\|}\right)\ \text{otherwise}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hölder Error Bound Governed by Singularity Degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A regularized conic feasibility error bound for bounded approximate points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \overline{\mathcal A}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:x+tb\in\mathcal A\text{ for some }t\in\mathbb R\}. Suppose \{x(\epsilon):0<\epsilon\leq1\} is bounded and, for every 0<\epsilon\leq1, \operatorname{dist}(x(\epsilon),\mathcal A)\leq\epsilon and \lambda_{\min}(x(\epsilon))\geq-\epsilon. Then \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(x(\epsilon),(b+\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal K\right)=O\!\left(\epsilon^{2^{-d(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)}}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded family that is within epsilon of the affine constraints and violates cone membership by at most epsilon, the distance to the conic feasible set obeys a Hölder error bound whose exponent is determined by the singularity degree.
assumptions_latex: \overline{\mathcal A}=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:x+tb\in\mathcal A\text{ for some }t\in\mathbb R\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}\!\left(x(\epsilon),(b+\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal K\right)=O\!\left(\epsilon^{2^{-d(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)}}\right).
