children.title: Cone-Face-Dependent Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Error behavior specialized to second-order, semidefinite, and general cones.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General-cone criterion for a local linear conic feasibility-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone, \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\), and
\[
\Phi(x):=(Ax-b,x)-(\{0\}\times K).
\]
For \(\bar x\in\mathcal F\), metric subregularity of \(\Phi\) at \((\bar x,(0,0))\), under a compatible product norm, is equivalent to a local estimate
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F)\le\kappa\bigl(\|Ax-b\|+\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general conic system has a local linear feasibility-error bound exactly when its residual mapping is metrically subregular at the reference solution.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.
A compatible product norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,(0,0))\iff\text{ the displayed local linear error bound holds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Subregularity Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOC and PSD boundary systems for which a linear residual bound fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L_3=\{(u,v,w):u\ge\sqrt{v^2+w^2}\}\), impose \(u-v=0\) and take \(x_t=(\sqrt{1+t^2},1,t)\in L_3\). Its equality residual is \(\Theta(t^2)\), while its distance to the feasible set \(\{(a,a,0):a\ge0\}\) is \(\Theta(|t|)\). For \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\), impose \(X_{11}=0\) and take
\[
X_t=\begin{pmatrix}t^2&t\\t&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
The equality residual is \(t^2\), whereas
\[
\operatorname{dist}_F(X_t,\mathcal F)=\sqrt{t^4+2t^2}=\Theta(|t|).
\]
Thus a local linear bound in the displayed equality residual fails in both systems, and square-root order is attained along these sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elementary Lorentz-cone and PSD systems can have residual of order t squared but solution distance of order t.
assumptions_latex: Euclidean distance is used for \(L_3\), and Frobenius distance for \(\mathbb S^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(z_t,\mathcal F)=\Theta(\sqrt{r(z_t)}),\quad\text{so no local bound }\operatorname{dist}(z,\mathcal F)\le Cr(z)\text{ holds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Curved-Cone Square-Root Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facewise comparison between distance to a face and distance to the ambient cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A closed convex cone \(K\) is amenable when, for every face \(F\unlhd K\), there exists \(\kappa_F\ge0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa_F\operatorname{dist}(x,K)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{span}F.
\]
Polyhedral cones, second-order cones, and positive-semidefinite cones are amenable; the modulus may depend on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Amenability supplies a face-dependent linear comparison between distance to a selected face and distance to the whole cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.
\(F\unlhd K\) ranges over the faces of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ amenable}\iff \forall F\unlhd K\ \exists\kappa_F\ge0:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa_F\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\ \forall x\in\operatorname{span}F.

notation.meaning: F is a face of K

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global linear error bound for nonempty polyhedral conic equality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedral cone and \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\). For fixed finite-dimensional norms, there is \(H<\infty\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F)\le H\bigl(\|Ax-b\|+\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\bigr)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedral conic system has a global linear error bound controlled by its equality residual and cone distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists H<\infty\ \forall x:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F)\le H(\|Ax-b\|+\operatorname{dist}(x,K)).
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Hoffman Error Regime
Cone-Face-Dependent Error Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error bounds stratified by the active cone face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\). For a face \(F\unlhd K\), define \(\mathcal F_F=\mathcal F\cap F\). A face-dependent local error regime holds at \(\bar x\in\mathcal F_F\) when constants \(\kappa_F,\rho_F>0\) satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F_F)\leq\kappa_F\bigl(\|Ax-b\|_2+\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\bigr)
\]
whenever \(\|x-\bar x\|_2\leq\rho_F\). Constants valid on one face need not remain bounded along sequences whose minimal faces drop dimension, so a uniform whole-cone bound is a strictly stronger property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic error bounds may hold face by face while their constants deteriorate when solutions approach lower-dimensional faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A facewise bound does not by itself imply a uniform error bound over changing active faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Feasible Conic Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility without strict feasibility relative to the ambient cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone with nonempty interior, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). The system
\[
Ax=b,\qquad x\in K
\]
is weakly feasible when its feasible set \(\mathcal F:=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\) is nonempty but \(\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\). Equivalently, the minimal face
\[
F_{\min}:=\bigcap\{F\unlhd K:\mathcal F\subseteq F\}
\]
is a proper face of \(K\). The reduced system over \(F_{\min}\) is relatively strictly feasible, meaning \(\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly feasible conic system has feasible points but none in the interior of the ambient cone. Its feasible set lies in a proper minimal face, relative to which strict feasibility holds.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\neq\varnothing\), \(\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\), and \(F_{\min}\lneqq K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit zero-distance infeasible semidefinite family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[L=\left\{X(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&t\end{pmatrix}:t\in\mathbb R\right\}.\] Then \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^2=\varnothing\), but \[\operatorname{dist}(X(t),\mathbb S_+^2)=\frac{2}{t+\sqrt{t^2+4}}\longrightarrow0\qquad(t\to+\infty).\] Thus \(L\) and \(\mathbb S_+^2\) form a weakly infeasible conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-by-two affine matrix family never meets the PSD cone although its distance to that cone vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^2\) is equipped with the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\cap\mathbb S_+^2=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^2)=0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-form characterization of weak conic infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex cone \(K\) and linear map \(A\), the system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), is weakly infeasible exactly when \[b\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K).\] Equivalently, no \(x\in K\) satisfies \(Ax=b\), while \(\inf_{x\in K}\|Ax-b\|=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak infeasibility means that the right-hand side is not attained by the conic image but is arbitrarily approximable by it.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric consequences of zero-distance infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a nonempty affine set and \(K\) a nonempty closed convex cone with \(L\cap K=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(L,K)=0\). Every sequence \((u_k,v_k)\in L\times K\) satisfying \(\|u_k-v_k\|\to0\) is unbounded. Moreover, no affine hyperplane separates \(L\) and \(K\) with a strictly positive margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-feasible pairs must escape to infinity, and weak infeasibility admits no positive-margin separating certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a nonempty closed affine set.
\(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|u_k\|+\|v_k\|\to\infty\text{ for every }\|u_k-v_k\|\to0,\text{ and no positive-margin separator exists.}
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Infeasibility Signatures
Weakly Infeasible Conic Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility with zero distance between the affine constraints and the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and let \(L:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\) be nonempty. The conic system \(L\cap K\neq\varnothing\) is weakly infeasible precisely when
\[
 L\cap K=\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{dist}(L,K):=\inf_{u\in L,\,v\in K}\|u-v\|_2=0.
\]
Equivalently, there exist sequences \(u_k\in L\) and \(v_k\in K\) with \(\|u_k-v_k\|_2\to0\), although no point satisfies both constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly infeasible system has no feasible point, yet its affine space and cone have zero distance.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\cap K=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(L,K)=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Escape-rate bound for approximate feasible points of a weakly infeasible SDP system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The corrupted sign in the eigenvalue condition is interpreted as \(\lambda_{\min}(x(\epsilon))\ge-\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((b+\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal K=\varnothing\) and a family \(\{x(\epsilon):\epsilon>0\}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x(\epsilon),b+\mathcal A)\le\epsilon\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(x(\epsilon))\ge-\epsilon\) for every \(\epsilon>0\). Then \(d(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)\ge1\). Moreover, for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), \(x(\epsilon)\ne0\) and \(\|x(\epsilon)\|^{-1}=O\!\left(\epsilon^{1/(2^{d(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)}-1)}\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an infeasible semidefinite system has points simultaneously approaching its affine constraints and the positive-semidefinite cone, its facial-reduction degree is at least one and those approximate points must escape to infinity at the stated rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)\ge1,\qquad x(\epsilon)\ne0\text{ for sufficiently small }\epsilon,\qquad \frac1{\|x(\epsilon)\|}=O\!\left(\epsilon^{1/(2^{d(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)}-1)}\right)

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial-reduction preprocessing for a feasible conic equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(K_0=K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone. Assume \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\). At iteration \(j\), stop and output \(K_j\) if some \(x\in\operatorname{ri}K_j\) satisfies \(Ax=b\). Otherwise, choose \(y_j\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[
z_j:=A^*y_j\in K_j^*,\qquad b^Ty_j=0,
\]
where the restriction of \(z_j\) to \(\operatorname{span}K_j\) is nonzero, and set
\[
K_{j+1}:=K_j\cap z_j^\perp.
\]
Every feasible point remains in each \(K_j\), and the terminal face supports a relatively strictly feasible reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial reduction repeatedly uses exposing certificates to replace the cone by a smaller face containing every feasible point, stopping when the reduced feasible system meets the relative interior.
assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
Each failed relative-interior test supplies the displayed exposing certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output face contains every feasible point and satisfies \(\{x:Ax=b\}\cap\operatorname{ri}K_j\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singularity Degree and Finite Reduction Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Length bound for exact facial reduction of a nonempty finite-dimensional conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The singularity degree \(\operatorname{sd}(A,b,K)\) is the minimum number \(d\) of proper certified reductions in a chain \(K=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq F_d=F_{\min}\). If \(F_{\min}=K\), then \(d=0\); otherwise \[1\leq d\leq \dim(\operatorname{span}K)-\dim(\operatorname{span}F_{\min}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singularity degree is the shortest certified facial-reduction chain reaching the minimal feasible face, bounded by the corresponding dimension loss.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
Each proper reduction exposes a face of the current face while preserving every feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\min}=K\Rightarrow\operatorname{sd}=0\), and \(F_{\min}\lneqq K\Rightarrow1\leq\operatorname{sd}\leq\dim(\operatorname{span}K)-\dim(\operatorname{span}F_{\min})\).

notation.meaning: Minimal face containing the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Singularity Degree and Finite Reduction Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact handoff from facial reduction to a barrier method on the reduced face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\min}\) be the minimal face containing \(\mathcal F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\). Then \[\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\{x\in F_{\min}:Ax=b\},\qquad \mathcal F\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\neq\varnothing.\] Hence a barrier method may be formulated in \(\operatorname{span}F_{\min}\) using a barrier on \(\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\). If \(F_{\min}\lneqq K\), the unreduced feasible set does not meet \(\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction to the minimal feasible face preserves the problem and restores relative strict feasibility for a face-based barrier method.
assumptions_latex: A suitable barrier is available on \(\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\) relative to \(\operatorname{span}F_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F=\{x\in F_{\min}:Ax=b\}\) and \(\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Barrier Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-stratum definition for a primal feasible point in semidefinite programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be a surjective linear map, let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) satisfy \(\mathcal A(X)=b\). Suppose
\[
X=Q\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda,0)Q^T,
\]
where \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is orthogonal, \(\Lambda\in\mathbb S_{++}^r\), and \(r=\operatorname{rank}X\). Define
\[
\mathcal T_X:=\left\{Q\begin{bmatrix}U&V\\V^T&0\end{bmatrix}Q^T:U\in\mathbb S^r,\ V\in\mathbb R^{r\times(n-r)}\right\}.
\]
The point \(X\) is primal nondegenerate when \(\mathcal A(\mathcal T_X)=\mathbb R^m\), and primal degenerate when this surjectivity condition fails. Equivalently, primal degeneracy holds when some \(0\neq y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfies \(\mathcal A^*y\in\mathcal T_X^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal SDP feasible point is degenerate when the equality map is not surjective on the tangent space of the positive-semidefinite matrices having the same rank as that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal degeneracy is equivalent to \(\mathcal A(\mathcal T_X)\neq\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: Tangent space of the fixed-rank PSD stratum at X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness consequence at an optimal SDP primal matrix; the converse is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SDP with attained zero-gap primal and dual optima, if an optimal primal matrix \(X\) is primal nondegenerate, then the optimal dual multiplier, and hence its slack, is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-nondegenerate optimal matrix permits at most one optimal dual multiplier and slack.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual SDP optima are attained with zero duality gap.
\(X\) is optimal and satisfies \(\mathcal A(\mathcal T_X)=\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (y_1,S_1),(y_2,S_2)\in Y^\star\implies y_1=y_2\ \text{and}\ S_1=S_2.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-stratum definition for a dual slack in semidefinite programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) produce the dual slack \(S:=C-\mathcal A^*y\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Suppose
\[
S=Q\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma,0)Q^T,
\]
where \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is orthogonal, \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^s\), and \(s=\operatorname{rank}S\). Define
\[
\mathcal T_S:=\left\{Q\begin{bmatrix}U&V\\V^T&0\end{bmatrix}Q^T:U\in\mathbb S^s,\ V\in\mathbb R^{s\times(n-s)}\right\}.
\]
The slack \(S\) is dual nondegenerate when
\[
\mathcal T_S+\operatorname{range}\mathcal A^*=\mathbb S^n,
\]
and dual degenerate when this spanning condition fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual SDP slack is degenerate when its fixed-rank tangent space together with the span of the equality-constraint matrices fails to cover the ambient symmetric-matrix space.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual degeneracy is equivalent to \(\mathcal T_S+\operatorname{range}\mathcal A^*\neq\mathbb S^n\).

notation.meaning: Tangent space of the fixed-rank PSD stratum at S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional certificate equivalent to failure of the dual tangent-space spanning condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual degeneracy holds if and only if there exists \(0\ne H\in\mathbb S^n\) such that \[H\in\mathcal T_S^\perp\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal A(H)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual degeneracy is exactly witnessed by a nonzero symmetric matrix orthogonal to the slack's fixed-rank tangent space and annihilated by the primal constraint map.
assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is a dual slack with fixed-rank tangent space \(\mathcal T_S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is dual degenerate}\iff\exists\,0\ne H\in\mathcal T_S^\perp\cap\ker\mathcal A.

notation.meaning: fixed-rank tangent space at the dual slack

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness consequence at an optimal SDP dual slack; the converse is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SDP with an attained optimal primal solution, if an optimal dual slack \(S\) is dual nondegenerate, then the primal optimal matrix is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-nondegenerate optimal slack permits at most one primal optimal matrix.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual SDP optima are attained with zero duality gap.
\(S\) is an optimal dual slack satisfying \(\mathcal T_S+\operatorname{range}\mathcal A^*=\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_1,X_2\in X^\star\implies X_1=X_2.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Degeneracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous primal and dual degeneracy at an optimal SDP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\) be SDP data. Consider an optimal primal-dual triple \((X,y,S)\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal A(X)=b,\qquad X\in\mathbb S_+^n,\qquad S=C-\mathcal A^*y\in\mathbb S_+^n,\qquad XS=0.
\]
Let \(\mathcal T_X\) and \(\mathcal T_S\) be the fixed-rank tangent spaces at \(X\) and \(S\). The associated optimal pair \((X,S)\) lies in a coupled degeneracy regime when
\[
\mathcal A(\mathcal T_X)\neq\mathbb R^m
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal T_S+\operatorname{range}\mathcal A^*\neq\mathbb S^n.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal complementary SDP pair is coupled degenerate when both the primal tangent-space surjectivity condition and the dual tangent-space spanning condition fail at that pair.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\) are fixed SDP data.
\((X,y,S)\) is an optimal primal-dual triple satisfying the displayed feasibility and complementarity conditions.
\(\mathcal T_X\) and \(\mathcal T_S\) are the associated fixed-rank tangent spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(\mathcal T_X)\neq\mathbb R^m\) and \(\mathcal T_S+\operatorname{range}\mathcal A^*\neq\mathbb S^n\).

notation.meaning: Complementary primal matrix and dual slack
Fixed-rank tangent spaces at X and S

children.title: Failure of Strict Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Optimal-face geometry without strictly complementary solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-complementarity boundary for semidefinite optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega^*\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\times\mathbb S_+^n\) be the nonempty set of primal-matrix and dual-slack pairs \((X,S)\) arising from optimal solutions of a semidefinite program and satisfying \(XS=0\). A pair \((X,S)\in\Omega^*\) is strictly complementary exactly when
\[
X+S\succ0,
\]
equivalently when \(\operatorname{rank}X+\operatorname{rank}S=n\). Strict complementarity fails for the problem exactly when
\[
\forall (X,S)\in\Omega^*,\qquad X+S\not\succ0,
\]
equivalently when every \((X,S)\in\Omega^*\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}X+\operatorname{rank}S<n\). For each such pair, \(\ker X\cap\ker S\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity fails for an SDP when no optimal complementary primal-matrix and dual-slack pair has a positive-definite sum, equivalently when every such pair has total rank below n.
assumptions_latex: Every \((X,S)\in\Omega^*\) is an optimal complementary pair satisfying \(XS=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure occurs exactly when \(X+S\not\succ0\) for every \((X,S)\in\Omega^*\), equivalently when \(\operatorname{rank}X+\operatorname{rank}S<n\) for every such pair.

notation.meaning: Set of optimal complementary primal-matrix and dual-slack pairs

children.title: Nonunique Optimal Solutions
children.top_down_role: Optimal sets containing multiple distinguishable solution points.

assumptions_latex: The conic program \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) attains its finite optimum \(p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^\star\) is nonunique exactly when it contains distinct points, equivalently when \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}X^\star)\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal conic programs with an attained optimum.

source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the optimal-solution set by \[X^\star:=\{x\in K:Ax=b,\ \langle c,x\rangle=p^\star\}.\] The program has nonunique optimal solutions when there exist \(x_1,x_2\in X^\star\) with \(x_1\ne x_2\). Because \(X^\star\) is convex, this is equivalent to the inclusion of the nondegenerate segment \(\{(1-t)x_1+tx_2:0\le t\le1\}\) in \(X^\star\), and hence to \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}X^\star)\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic program has nonunique optima when its optimal set contains two distinct points; convexity then makes the entire segment between them optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Dimensional Optimal Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic dimension of the exposed optimal face of a finite-dimensional conic feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P:=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\) and let \[F^\star:=\{x\in P:\langle c,x\rangle=p^\star\}.\] Because the objective is linear, \(F^\star\) is an exposed face of \(P\). For a prescribed integer \(r\ge1\), the optimal face is high-dimensional at level \(r\) when \[\dim(\operatorname{aff}F^\star)\ge r.\] Every point of \(F^\star\) is feasible and optimal by definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal face is the exposed face of the feasible region on which the attained objective equals its optimum. It is high-dimensional at level r when its affine dimension is at least r, and all of its points are optimal.
assumptions_latex: The conic program \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in K,\ Ax=b\}\) attains its finite optimum \(p^\star\).
A dimension threshold \(r\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(r\ge1\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exposed optimal face \(F^\star\) is high-dimensional at level \(r\) exactly when \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}F^\star)\ge r\).

notation.meaning: exposed optimal face of the feasible region

children.title: Limiting-Face Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity in the active face approached by an interior-point trajectory.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-variable orthant program exhibiting genuine perturbation-dependent limiting faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^2\), consider \[P_d:\quad \min\ d(x_1-x_2)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_1+x_2=1,\quad x\in K.\] If \(d>0\), the unique optimum and the limit of the logarithmic-barrier central path is \((0,1)\); if \(d<0\), it is \((1,0)\). At \(d=0\), every point of the feasible segment is optimal and its minimal containing cone face is \(K\). Hence \(d_k=1/k\) and \(e_k=-1/k\) select limits in the two different coordinate-ray faces of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite vanishing objective perturbations of a two-variable LP select opposite endpoints of the limiting optimal segment, which lie in different coordinate faces.
assumptions_latex: For each \(d\ne0\), selection is by the limit of the standard logarithmic-barrier central path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{face}_K(0,1)\ne\operatorname{face}_K(1,0),\quad d_k\downarrow0,\quad e_k\uparrow0.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Direction Linear-Programming Example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of the cone face containing a selected perturbed central-path limit on the direction of vanishing data perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_d\) be conic programs whose data converge to those of \(P_0\) as \(d\to0\). For each \(d\ne0\), let \(x(d)\) be a selected limit of an interior-point trajectory for \(P_d\), and suppose every cluster point of \(x(d)\) is optimal for \(P_0\). Limiting-face ambiguity occurs if there are sequences \(d_k\to0\) and \(e_k\to0\) such that \(x(d_k)\to\bar x\), \(x(e_k)\to\hat x\), and \(\operatorname{face}_K(\bar x)\ne\operatorname{face}_K(\hat x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting-face ambiguity occurs when different vanishing perturbation directions make selected interior-point limits approach points in different faces of the cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
The data of \(P_d\) converge to those of \(P_0\) as \(d\to0\).
Each \(x(d)\) is a selected limit of an interior-point trajectory for \(P_d\), and its cluster points are optimal for \(P_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,d_k,e_k\to0:\ x(d_k)\to\bar x,\ x(e_k)\to\hat x,\ \operatorname{face}_K(\bar x)\ne\operatorname{face}_K(\hat x).

notation.meaning: conic program with perturbation parameter d
selected limit of an interior-point trajectory for the perturbed program
minimal face of K containing x

children.title: Near-Ill-Posed Conic Instances
children.top_down_role: Instances close to changes in feasibility or boundedness status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive upper bound on proximity to a declared conic status boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d+\Delta d\in\Sigma\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\leq\|\Delta d\|\). For \(d\neq0\), \(\|\Delta d\|/\|d\|\) is an upper bound on relative distance to ill posedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified perturbation reaching ill-posed data certifies an upper bound on distance to the status boundary.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal D,\|\cdot\|)\) is the declared data space.
\(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) is the declared ill-posed set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\leq\|\Delta d\|.

notation.meaning: verified perturbation reaching the ill-posed set

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Boundary-Perturbation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional lower bound on separation from a declared ill-posed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(B(d,r)=\{d':\|d'-d\|<r\}\) is verified to satisfy \(B(d,r)\cap\Sigma=\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\geq r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified perturbation ball containing no ill-posed data certifies a lower distance bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is closed in the declared finite-dimensional normed data space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\geq r.

notation.meaning: open norm ball centered at the instance data

knowledge_statements.title: Status-Stability Inner-Ball Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional conic family approaching a feasibility-status boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_t:\ x=t,\ x\in\mathbb R_+\), perturbing only \(t\), feasibility holds exactly for \(t\geq0\). Thus \(\Sigma=\{0\}\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(t,\Sigma)=t\downarrow0\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible scalar systems with positive right-hand side approach the feasibility boundary with stability radius tending to zero.
assumptions_latex: Only the scalar right-hand side is perturbed, with norm \(|\cdot|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(t,\Sigma)=t\to0\quad(t\downarrow0).

notation.meaning: status boundary in the selected perturbation slice

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Feasibility-Boundary Family

assumptions_latex: \(d,e\) belong to the same normed data space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)-\operatorname{dist}(e,\Sigma)|\leq\|d-e\|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation sensitivity of distance to a fixed conic status boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any data \(d,e\) and nonempty set \(\Sigma\), \[|\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)-\operatorname{dist}(e,\Sigma)|\leq\|d-e\|.\] Thus perturbing the data by norm at most \(\varepsilon\) can reduce their distance from the declared boundary by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a fixed ill-posed set changes by no more than the data perturbation.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Sensitivity of Boundary Distance

assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is a nonempty subset of a normed data space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)=\sup\{r\geq0:B(d,r)\cap\Sigma=\varnothing\}.

notation.meaning: open ball in the declared data norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric stability-radius identity for a declared ill-posed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty set \(\Sigma\) and \(d\notin\overline\Sigma\), \[\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)=\sup\{r\geq0:B(d,r)\cap\Sigma=\varnothing\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to the declared ill-posed set is exactly the largest open-ball radius avoiding that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Stability-Radius Identity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale Invariance of Relative Boundary Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous data models whose declared ill-posed set is a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Sigma\) is a cone, \(d\ne0\), and \(\alpha>0\), then \[\frac{\operatorname{dist}(\alpha d,\Sigma)}{\|\alpha d\|}=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)}{\|d\|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a conic ill-posed set, common positive data scaling preserves relative distance to ill posedness.
assumptions_latex: The data norm is absolutely homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(\alpha d)=\rho(d),\qquad \rho(d)=\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)/\|d\|.

notation.meaning: relative distance to the declared ill-posed set

knowledge_statements.title: Scale Invariance of Relative Boundary Distance

assumptions_latex: Conic instances are represented by data \(d=(A,b,c)\) in a normed data space.
\(\Sigma\) is the set of ill-posed data lying on a boundary between distinct feasibility, infeasibility, or boundedness statuses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance is near ill-posed when \(\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)/\|d\|\) is small, equivalently when its reciprocal distance condition measure is large.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise distance-to-ill-posedness for finite-dimensional conic data.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero data \(d\), define \[\rho(d):=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)}{\|d\|},\qquad \mathcal C(d):=\rho(d)^{-1}.\] The instance is near ill posed at tolerance \(\tau>0\) when \(0<\rho(d)\le\tau\). Consequently, a relative perturbation of size at most \(\tau\) can approach or cross \(\Sigma\), where primal or dual feasibility, infeasibility, or boundedness status may change; equivalently, \(\mathcal C(d)\ge\tau^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic instance is near ill posed when a small relative perturbation can reach data where feasibility or boundedness status changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Ill-Posed Conic Instances

children.title: Newton-System Singularity
children.top_down_role: Singular linear-system regimes in conic Newton computations.

assumptions_latex: At an interior-point iterate, the Newton correction satisfies \(M\Delta z=r\) for a square matrix \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact Newton-system singularity is the condition \(\ker M\ne\{0\}\), equivalently \(\det M=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic singularity of a square primal-dual Newton matrix.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Newton system is singular precisely when \[\ker M\ne\{0\},\] equivalently when \(\operatorname{rank}M<\dim M\) or \(\det M=0\). If the system is consistent, the correction is then nonunique because \(\Delta z+v\) solves \(M\Delta z=r\) whenever \(v\in\ker M\); if \(r\notin\operatorname{range}M\), no exact Newton correction exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A square Newton system is singular when its coefficient matrix has a nontrivial nullspace, causing either nonunique corrections or inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-System Singularity

children.top_down_role: Progressive or structural loss of effective Newton-system rank.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVD diagnostic reporting effective rank and its backward-error scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the singular values of the scaled Newton matrix and report \(r_\tau=\#\{i:\sigma_i/\sigma_1>\tau\}\), together with \(\tau\|M\|_2\). Singular values not exceeding the threshold identify directions removable by perturbations no larger than the reported scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled SVD reports numerical rank using an explicit threshold and backward-error magnitude.
assumptions_latex: A scaling convention and \(\tau\) are declared.
Singular values are computed by a backward-stable procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_\tau=\#\{i:\sigma_i/\sigma_1>\tau\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled SVD Rank-Revealing Diagnostic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family separating numerical rank loss from exact singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M(t)=\operatorname{diag}(1,t)\), \(0<t\leq1\), exact rank is two. Under threshold \(\tau\), numerical rank is two for \(t>\tau\) and one for \(0<t\leq\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matrices diag(1,t) remain nonsingular but lose thresholded numerical rank as t crosses the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(M(t))=2\text{ for }t>0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}_\tau(M(t))=1\text{ for }0<t\leq\tau.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingular Threshold-Crossing Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-relative numerical rank of a nonzero Newton matrix under an explicitly declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\neq0\) with singular values \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_p\geq0\) and declared \(\tau\in(0,1)\), define \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M)>\tau\sigma_1(M)\}\). Numerical rank loss means \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M)<\operatorname{rank}(M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank is the number of singular values above an explicit relative threshold; numerical rank loss is tolerance-dependent and can precede exact singularity.
assumptions_latex: A dimensionless threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\) and matrix scaling convention are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}_\tau(M)=\#\{i:\sigma_i(M)>\tau\sigma_1(M)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Thresholded Numerical Rank

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error interpretation of the smallest singular value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with full rank \(r=\min\{m,n\}\), \[\min_{\operatorname{rank}(M+E)<r}\|E\|_2=\sigma_r(M).\] Hence \(\sigma_r(M)\leq\tau\|M\|_2\) exactly when a relative spectral perturbation of size at most \(\tau\) can make \(M\) rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest singular value is exactly the spectral-norm distance from a full-rank matrix to rank deficiency.
assumptions_latex: Perturbations are measured in spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\operatorname{rank}(M+E)<r}\|E\|_2=\sigma_r(M).
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Distance to Rank Deficiency

assumptions_latex: The Newton matrix \(M_k\) is evaluated in floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Numerical rank loss occurs when \(\sigma_n(M_k)\le\gamma u\,\sigma_1(M_k)\) for a prescribed threshold factor \(\gamma\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise numerical rank loss under a singular-value threshold.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a chosen \(\gamma\ge1\), the Newton matrix has numerical rank loss when \[\sigma_n(M_k)\le\gamma u\,\sigma_1(M_k).\] Equivalently, when \(M_k\) is nonsingular, \(\kappa_2(M_k)\ge(\gamma u)^{-1}\). In this regime, a perturbation \(E\) with \(\|E\|_2\le\gamma u\|M_k\|_2\) can make \(M_k+E\) singular, so computed Newton corrections need not retain meaningful relative accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton matrix loses numerical rank when its smallest singular value is at roundoff scale relative to its largest singular value.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-System Rank Loss

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank threshold and perturbation interpretation are standard numerical-linear-algebra ideas, but the cited interior-point section does not specifically support the chosen threshold or the relative-accuracy conclusion.

children.title: Reduced-System Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Rank-related failure in normal-equation or Schur-complement systems.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual Newton equations are reduced by eliminating a block with symmetric positive-definite scaling matrix \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduced-system breakdown occurs when \(S\) is singular or numerically rank deficient, preventing a stable unique reduced correction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement reduction of a primal-dual Newton system.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Elimination yields a reduced equation \(S\Delta y=q\) with \[S:=AH^{-1}A^*.\] Exact breakdown occurs when \(\ker S\ne\{0\}\). Numerical breakdown at threshold \(\tau>0\) occurs when \(\sigma_{\min}(S)\le\tau\sigma_{\max}(S)\). Since \(H\succ0\), exact singularity is equivalent to the existence of \(y\ne0\) such that \(A^*y=0\); extreme conditioning of \(H\) can additionally produce numerical breakdown without exact rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Newton solve breaks down when its Schur complement is singular or so ill conditioned that a stable unique correction cannot be computed.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Breakdown

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

children.title: Augmented-System Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Rank-related failure in augmented saddle-point systems.

assumptions_latex: A primal-dual Newton step uses the symmetric augmented matrix \(M=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^*\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) with \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented system is singular exactly when \(A\) lacks full row rank; it is numerically broken when \(\sigma_{\min}(M)\) is at the working-error scale.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric augmented formulation with a positive-definite primal block.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[M:=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^*\\A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H\succ0,\] exact augmented-system breakdown is \(\ker M\ne\{0\}\). Under \(H\succ0\), this occurs exactly when \(A\) is not surjective, equivalently when \(A^*y=0\) for some \(y\ne0\). At numerical threshold \(\tau>0\), breakdown is declared when \(\sigma_{\min}(M)\le\tau\sigma_{\max}(M)\), because the computed primal-dual correction then becomes highly perturbation-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite primal block, the augmented KKT matrix is singular exactly when the constraints lack full row rank; near-singularity causes numerical breakdown.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Breakdown

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

children.title: Interiority-Scaling Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Boundary crossing and extreme primal-dual scaling ratios.

children.title: Loss of Interiority
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes approaching or crossing the cone boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
A primal-dual iterate satisfies \(x_k\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(s_k\in\operatorname{int}K^*\) before a computed update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of interiority occurs when the accepted computed iterate leaves \(\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual iterates for a cone with nonempty interior.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given computed directions \(\widehat{\Delta x}_k\) and \(\widehat{\Delta s}_k\), define \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k\widehat{\Delta x}_k\) and \(s_{k+1}=s_k+\alpha_k\widehat{\Delta s}_k\). Loss of interiority occurs when \[(x_{k+1},s_{k+1})\notin\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*.\] At such a point, a barrier gradient, Hessian, or primal-dual scaling requiring strict interiority is undefined, so the standard barrier Newton iteration cannot continue without restoration or step rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interiority is lost when a computed primal or dual update reaches or crosses the cone boundary, making the barrier-based Newton step undefined.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Interiority

children.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Extremes
children.top_down_role: Extreme magnitude ratios between primal-side and dual-side quantities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large but finite condition number of a declared positive-definite SDP scaling matrix; no universal breakdown threshold is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a positive-definite primal-dual scaling matrix \(W\), the spectral norm, and a diagnostic threshold \(\Gamma>1\). Scaling is called extreme at threshold \(\Gamma\) when \[\kappa_2(W):=\|W\|_2\|W^{-1}\|_2\ge\Gamma.\] This is a convention-specific conditioning diagnostic, not by itself a certificate that a Newton solve is inaccurate or that the iteration has failed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixing the scaling convention, norm, and threshold, scaling is extreme when the scaling matrix has a sufficiently large condition number; threshold exceedance alone does not prove solver failure.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) is the declared primal-dual scaling matrix.
Conditioning is measured in the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(W)\ge\Gamma.
knowledge_statements.title: Convention-Specific Extreme Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditioning of the basic congruence transformations induced by a positive-definite scaling matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), define \(\mathcal C_W(H)=WHW\) on \(\mathbb S^n\). In the Frobenius norm, \[\kappa(\mathcal C_W)=\kappa_2(W)^2.\] The inverse congruence \(\mathcal C_{W^{-1}}\) has the same condition number. Thus a large \(\kappa_2(W)\) produces quadratically separated scales in these congruence coordinate maps, although the conditioning of a complete Newton system also depends on its other operators and formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Congruence by an SDP scaling matrix has condition number equal to the square of the matrix condition number, but this alone does not determine the accuracy of the full Newton system.
assumptions_latex: The domain and range of \(\mathcal C_W\) use the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa(\mathcal C_W)=\kappa(\mathcal C_{W^{-1}})=\kappa_2(W)^2.

notation.meaning: congruence map H mapped to WHW
operator condition number in the Frobenius norm

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning of SDP Congruence Scaling

assumptions_latex: The cone is the positive-semidefinite cone, with \(X\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling is extreme when \(\kappa_2(W)\) exceeds a prescribed threshold, amplifying rounding errors in scaled Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite programming with a symmetric primal-dual scaling.

source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a threshold \(\Gamma>1\), primal-dual scaling is extreme when \[\kappa_2(W):=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(W)}{\lambda_{\min}(W)}\ge\Gamma.\] Because multiplication by \(W\) and \(W^{-1}\) can respectively amplify normwise perturbations by factors proportional to \(\|W\|_2\) and \(\|W^{-1}\|_2\), the round-trip scaling map can amplify relative errors by order \(\kappa_2(W)\). Thus extreme scaling marks a finite-precision reliability boundary for the scaled Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual scaling is extreme when its largest and smallest spectral scales are widely separated, causing scaled Newton equations to amplify rounding errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Extremes

source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-number threshold is a permissible convention, but the claimed error amplification for the scaled Newton equations depends on the exact scaling operators and may involve different powers of the condition number. A numerical SDP source is required.

children.title: Boundary-Proximity Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Numerical degradation caused by operation too close to the cone boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
A computed interior iterate \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) is stored with normwise relative uncertainty at most \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary-proximity breakdown occurs when \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial K)\le\eta\|x\|\), since admissible perturbations can leave the cone interior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise finite-precision boundary test for a primal cone iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Boundary-proximity breakdown at uncertainty level \(\eta>0\) is the condition \[\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial K)\le\eta\|x\|.\] Then there exists a perturbation \(e\) with \(\|e\|\le\eta\|x\|\) such that \(x+e\notin\operatorname{int}K\). Hence the stored iterate cannot be certified as strictly interior at the working accuracy, even if its exact nominal value belongs to \(\operatorname{int}K\); barrier and scaling evaluations may consequently be unreliable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Breakdown occurs when an iterate is no farther from the cone boundary than its numerical uncertainty, so strict interiority cannot be certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Proximity Breakdown

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-norm specialization for a positive-definite semidefinite iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \[\operatorname{dist}_2(X,\partial\mathbb S_+^n)=\lambda_{\min}(X).\] Since \(\|X\|_2=\lambda_{\max}(X)\), boundary-proximity breakdown at relative uncertainty \(\eta\) is equivalent to \[\lambda_{\min}(X)\le\eta\lambda_{\max}(X),\] or \(\kappa_2(X)\ge\eta^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite SDP iterate, spectral-norm boundary distance is its smallest eigenvalue, making relative boundary proximity an exact eigenvalue-ratio test.
assumptions_latex: Distance and perturbation size use the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}_2(X,\partial\mathbb S_+^n)=\lambda_{\min}(X),\qquad \lambda_{\min}(X)\le\eta\|X\|_2\iff\kappa_2(X)\ge\eta^{-1}.
knowledge_statements.title: PSD Spectral Boundary-Distance Test

children.title: Residual-Based Status Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision regimes where progress and certificate tests become inconclusive.

children.title: Residual Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision regimes where residual reduction ceases to provide reliable progress.

assumptions_latex: A finite-precision algorithm produces nonnegative normalized residuals \(R_k\) and seeks \(R_k\le\varepsilon\).
A stagnation window \(m\ge1\) and required contraction factor \(q\in(0,1)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual stagnation is detected when \(R_k>\varepsilon\) and \(R_k>qR_{k-m}\).

notation.meaning: aggregate normalized residual at iteration k
window length and required contraction factor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stagnation test for normalized primal-dual residuals.

source_refs.source_title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\) aggregate the normalized primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity residuals. For fixed \(m\ge1\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), residual stagnation at iteration \(k\ge m\) is detected when \[R_k>\varepsilon\quad\text{and}\quad R_k>qR_{k-m}.\] Thus the termination tolerance remains unmet while the observed reduction over the window is smaller than the required factor; repeated detection indicates that further finite-precision Newton steps are not delivering the prescribed residual progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residuals stagnate when they remain above tolerance and fail to contract by a prescribed factor over a fixed iteration window.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Stagnation

source_witnesses.source_title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed windowed test is internally coherent but is an algorithm-specific convention. The cited general interior-point section does not establish this particular residual aggregation and contraction criterion.

children.title: Status Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Regimes where optimality, infeasibility, or numerical failure cannot be cleanly distinguished.

knowledge_statements.title: Status Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision ambiguity between approximate optimality, infeasibility, and unknown status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(Ax=b,\ x\in K\) and \(A^{*}y+s=c,\ s\in K^{*}\), let \(T_O,T_P,T_D\) be numerical tests for approximate optimality, primal infeasibility, and dual infeasibility. Status is ambiguous at computed data \((x,y,s)\) when backward-error bounds produce intervals \(I_O,I_P,I_D\) for the tested residuals or certificate margins and either two status tests can simultaneously pass for admissible perturbations, or every test can both pass and fail over its interval. In either case the finite-precision observations do not determine a unique status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Status is ambiguous when certified error intervals allow conflicting solver statuses or prevent every status test from having a definite truth value.
assumptions_latex: Residual and certificate evaluations have valid finite-precision error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{the computed observations do not determine a unique conic-program status}\)
review_flags: Exact authoritative locator for interval-based status ambiguity is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the tests, interval semantics, and admissible perturbations are not defined precisely enough to establish the stated ambiguity criterion without an authoritative source.

children.title: Certificate-Test Inconclusiveness
children.top_down_role: Precision-limited regimes where certificate tests do not support a decisive status.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Test Inconclusiveness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite-precision infeasibility certificates to pass or fail decisively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal-infeasibility candidate \(y\) tested by \(A^{*}y\in K^{*}\) and \(b^{T}y<0\). Suppose computation certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(A^{*}y,K^{*})\leq\delta\) and \(b^{T}y\in[\ell,u]\). The certificate test is inconclusive whenever \(\delta\) exceeds the prescribed cone-membership tolerance or \(0\in[\ell,u]\): the available bounds establish neither the exact certificate conditions nor their negation. The analogous condition applies to a dual-infeasibility ray after exchanging the primal and dual systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate test is inconclusive when error bounds cannot establish both cone membership and the required strict separating sign, nor refute them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta>\tau_K\ \text{or}\ 0\in[\ell,u]\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{certificate test inconclusive}\)

notation.meaning: certified interval enclosing the separating scalar

review_flags: A source explicitly supporting finite-precision certificate-test logic is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record conflates failure of a tolerance-based numerical test with inability to establish or refute the exact certificate conditions. In particular, an upper bound exceeding a tolerance does not by itself establish either exact nonmembership or inconclusiveness. A sourced, precise test convention is required.

assumptions_latex: A standard short-step method maintains its prescribed central neighborhood.
Barrier derivatives and Newton systems are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(\varepsilon)=O\!\left(\sqrt{\nu}\log(1/\varepsilon)\right)

Under the standard exact-oracle short-step assumptions, reducing the normalized gap from a fixed constant scale to \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) has the upper bound \(N(\varepsilon)=O(\sqrt{
u}\log(1/\varepsilon))\). Thus, when the same theorem and constants are applied to barriers with parameters \(
u_0\) and \(

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed cone can receive arbitrarily large representation-induced logarithmic-barrier parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(\mathbb R_+\) by \(q\) duplicate strict inequalities \(x>0\). The associated inequality logarithmic barrier is \(F_q(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^q\log x=-q\log x\), with logarithmic-homogeneity degree and barrier parameter \(q\). The represented cone is independent of \(q\), while the supplied barrier parameter is unbounded as \(q\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating the positive-half-line inequality leaves the cone unchanged but raises the summed logarithmic-barrier parameter to any prescribed positive integer.

Let \(F\) be a \(
u\)-self-concordant logarithmically homogeneous barrier for \(\operatorname{int}K\). A short-step path-following method that reduces the normalized duality gap from a constant to at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(O(\sqrt{

children.title: Nonsymmetric-Cone Scaling Limitations
children.top_down_role: Loss of self-scaled identities and symmetric search directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nonsymmetric cone with usable barrier geometry but no self-scaled geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:y>0,\ y\exp(x/y)\le z\}.
\]
The exponential cone is regular and nonsymmetric. It admits logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier formulations, but it admits no self-scaled barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential cone shows that an effective self-concordant barrier need not provide symmetric-cone or self-scaled geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(K_{\exp}\) is the closed exponential cone defined above.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\exp}\text{ is nonsymmetric and admits no self-scaled barrier}.
review_flags: The precise barrier construction for the exponential cone should receive a source locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Cone Scaling Witness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-level obstruction to Nesterov–Todd self-scaled geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional regular cone \(K\), existence of a self-scaled barrier implies that \(K\) is symmetric. Hence a nonsymmetric regular cone admits no self-scaled barrier, and scaling identities that depend on self-scaled barrier geometry are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A genuinely nonsymmetric regular cone cannot support self-scaled barrier geometry or its associated Nesterov–Todd scaling identities.
assumptions_latex: “Self-scaled barrier” has its standard Nesterov–Todd meaning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsymmetric}\Longrightarrow K\text{ admits no self-scaled barrier}.
review_flags: An authoritative source locator remains desirable for the self-scaled-cone characterization.
knowledge_statements.title: Self-Scaled Barrier Characterization Boundary
Nonsymmetric-Cone Scaling Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of symmetric primal-dual scaling when the cone lacks self-scaled structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior primal-dual pair \((x,s)\in\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^{*}\), a symmetric scaling direction requires a positive-definite self-adjoint map \(W\) that is compatible with the cone geometry and balances the pair, for example \(Wx=W^{-1}s\) under a fixed identification of the space and its dual. If no such cone-compatible \(W\) exists, search directions relying on this scaling identity are undefined; a nonsymmetric-cone method must instead use separate primal and dual barrier metrics or another asymmetric construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no cone-compatible operator symmetrically balances primal and dual interior points, symmetric-cone scaling directions are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists W\ \text{cone-compatible with}\ Wx=W^{-1}s\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{symmetric scaling direction unavailable}\)
review_flags: A precise source for nonsymmetric-cone scaling limitations and the chosen compatibility convention is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but “cone-compatible” is undefined and the displayed scaling convention is not enough to characterize the loss of self-scaled structure on nonsymmetric cones. A precise source and scaling convention are required.

children.title: Expensive or Inexact Barrier Oracles
children.top_down_role: Regimes where derivative-oracle cost or error dominates the method.

assumptions_latex: All component costs use the same arithmetic or runtime convention.
The comparison is taken over the same sequence of path-following iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_N=\sum_{k=1}^N(C_{\mathrm{orc},k}+C_{\mathrm{solve},k}+C_{\mathrm{other},k})

notation.meaning: barrier value, gradient, and Hessian evaluation cost at iteration k
Newton-system solution cost at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact accounting criterion for derivative-oracle domination of path-following work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\) path-following iterations, write \(T_N=\sum_{k=1}^N(C_{\mathrm{orc},k}+C_{\mathrm{solve},k}+C_{\mathrm{other},k})\). Barrier-oracle evaluation asymptotically dominates total non-oracle work precisely when \(\sum_{k=1}^N C_{\mathrm{orc},k}/\sum_{k=1}^N(C_{\mathrm{solve},k}+C_{\mathrm{other},k})\to\infty\). Merely exceeding the linear-solve cost at one iteration does not establish total-work domination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle cost dominates only when its accumulated work asymptotically exceeds the combined solve and remaining work; being larger than one linear solve is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Cost Domination

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (1-\delta)H\preceq\widetilde H\preceq(1+\delta)H,\qquad \|\widetilde p-p\|_H\leq\frac{\delta\|g\|_{H^{-1}}+\eta}{1-\delta}

notation.meaning: relative Hessian-error bound in the exact local metric
gradient-error bound in the exact local dual norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-invariant control of an approximate barrier gradient, Hessian, and Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=\nabla F(x)\), \(H=\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\), \(p=-H^{-1}g\), and \(\widetilde p=-\widetilde H^{-1}\widetilde g\). If \(\|H^{-1/2}(\widetilde H-H)H^{-1/2}\|_2\leq\delta<1\) and \(\|H^{-1/2}(\widetilde g-g)\|_2\leq\eta\), then \((1-\delta)H\preceq\widetilde H\preceq(1+\delta)H\), so \(\widetilde H\succ0\), and \(\|\widetilde p-p\|_H\leq(\delta\|g\|_{H^{-1}}+\eta)/(1-\delta)\). If only \(\delta\geq1\) is known, positive definiteness is not guaranteed; scalar perturbations can make \(\widetilde H\) zero or indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative Hessian error below one preserves the barrier metric and, together with local gradient-error control, bounds the approximate Newton direction; at error one or above, positive definiteness is no longer guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Controlled Gradient and Hessian Oracle Errors
knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Gradient and Hessian Oracle Errors
Expensive or Inexact Barrier Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle cost or error prevents the nominal Newton-step guarantee from applying.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=\nabla F(x)\) and \(H=\nabla^{2}F(x)\succ0\), while an oracle returns \(\widetilde g\) and \(\widetilde H\). If \(\|H^{-1/2}(\widetilde g-g)\|\leq\eta\) and \(\|H^{-1/2}(\widetilde H-H)H^{-1/2}\|_2\leq\delta<1\), then \(\widetilde H\) remains positive definite and defines a controlled approximate local metric. When \(\delta\geq1\), positive definiteness and Newton descent are no longer guaranteed. Even with small errors, an oracle cost exceeding the linear-solve cost can dominate total path-following work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large relative Hessian error destroys the Newton-metric guarantee; costly derivative evaluation can dominate runtime even when oracle errors are controlled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta<1\Rightarrow\widetilde H\succ0;\qquad \delta\geq1\Rightarrow\text{positive definiteness is not guaranteed}\)

children.title: Deficient-Redundant Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Model representations producing singular or oversized Newton systems.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Representations
children.top_down_role: Conic representations whose constraint structure produces deficient system rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity induced by linearly dependent equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(Ax=b\) with \(A:X\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\), suppose \(\operatorname{rank}A<m\). At an interior-point iterate with positive-definite primal metric \(H\succ0\), the normal-equations matrix \(S=AH^{-1}A^{*}\) is positive semidefinite but singular, because \(\ker A^{*}\neq\{0\}\) and \(y^{T}Sy=\|H^{-1/2}A^{*}y\|^{2}\). Thus an unregularized Newton system using \(S\) has no unique multiplier solution; dependent constraints must be removed or the system regularized or solved in a compatible subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the equality operator lacks full row rank, the normal-equations matrix is singular and Newton multipliers are not uniquely determined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=AH^{-1}A^{*}\succeq0\ \text{and}\ \ker S=\ker A^{*}\neq\{0\}\)

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{range}S=\operatorname{range}A,\quad \ker S=\ker A^*,\quad S\Delta y=r\iff r\perp\ker A^*

notation.meaning: Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse of the normal-equations operator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability and multiplier gauge freedom for rank-deficient normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=AH^{-1}A^*\) with \(H\succ0\). Then \(\operatorname{range}S=\operatorname{range}A\) and \(\ker S=\ker A^*\). Consequently, \(S\Delta y=r\) is solvable exactly when \(r\perp\ker A^*\). When it is solvable, every solution has the form \(\Delta y=S^\dagger r+z\) with \(z\in\ker A^*\), and all solutions have the same adjoint image \(A^*\Delta y=A^*S^\dagger r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular normal equation is solvable exactly on the range of the equality operator; multiplier solutions have nullspace freedom, but their adjoint image is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility and Gauge Freedom of Singular Normal Equations
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility and Gauge Freedom of Singular Normal Equations

children.title: Redundant Representations
children.top_down_role: Conic representations containing unnecessary variables, constraints, or cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality descriptions containing constraints implied by the remaining rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An equality representation \(Ax=b\), with rows indexed by \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), is redundant if some index \(i\) satisfies \(A_i=\sum_{j\neq i}\lambda_jA_j\) and \(b_i=\sum_{j\neq i}\lambda_jb_j\) for scalars \(\lambda_j\). Removing row \(i\) then leaves the feasible set unchanged. Such redundancy enlarges the multiplier space and, when it causes failure of full row rank, makes the unregularized normal-equations matrix singular without adding feasible-set information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representation is redundant when one equality is a linear consequence of the others, so deleting it leaves the feasible set unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\) and \(b_i\) denote the rows and components of \(A\) and \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_i=\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_jA_j,\ b_i=\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_jb_j\Rightarrow\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:A_{-i}x=b_{-i}\}\)

children.title: Oversized Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Newton-system growth caused by redundant model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebra growth caused by unnecessary representation dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an equivalent conic formulation introduces \(r\) redundant equality rows, increasing the normal-equations order from \(m\) to \(m+r\) without increasing \(\operatorname{rank}A\). A dense direct factorization then requires \(O((m+r)^3)\) arithmetic and \(O((m+r)^2)\) storage, compared with \(O(m^3)\) and \(O(m^2)\) before augmentation. The enlarged matrix is also singular when all redundant rows are retained without regularization, so the nominal extra work does not supply additional feasible-set information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant formulation rows enlarge dense Newton factorization cost and storage while adding no rank or feasible-set information.
assumptions_latex: The Newton equations are formed as a dense system.
The added \(r\) rows are linear consequences of the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{fact}}=O((m+r)^3),\quad M_{\mathrm{fact}}=O((m+r)^2)\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifted-Variable Growth of Full Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense full-space system growth caused by unnecessary lifted variables and equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an equivalent formulation enlarges an unreduced Newton system from order \(n+m\) to \(n+m+p+r\) by adding \(p\) primal-direction coordinates and \(r\) multiplier coordinates, generic dense factorization requires \[O((n+m+p+r)^3)\text{ arithmetic and }O((n+m+p+r)^2)\text{ storage}.\] These are representation costs rather than new feasible-set information when the added coordinates and equations can be eliminated exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unnecessary lifted variables and equations enlarge dense full-space Newton factorization cubically in work and quadratically in storage.
assumptions_latex: The lift adds \(p\) primal Newton variables and \(r\) equality multipliers.
The unreduced system is handled by dense direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{fact}}=O((n+m+p+r)^3),\qquad M_{\mathrm{fact}}=O((n+m+p+r)^2).
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Variable Growth of Full Newton Systems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse-Fill Boundary of Dimension-Only Cost Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nominal order alone to predict sparse direct factorization cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sparse Newton systems, order alone does not determine factorization work or storage. Added rows or variables confined to small disconnected or low-treewidth blocks may cause little fill, whereas a smaller lift that creates dense separators may cause substantial fill. Thus \(O(N^3)\) work and \(O(N^2)\) storage are dense worst-case order models; sparse cost must be assessed from the filled elimination graph or frontal-matrix sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse Newton cost depends on fill and separators, so nominal dimension alone may overstate or understate lift-induced burden.
assumptions_latex: The Newton matrix is processed by a sparse direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Sparse factorization cost is governed by elimination fill and frontal sizes, not solely by }N.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Fill Boundary of Dimension-Only Cost Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed presolve for dependent equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply a rank-revealing factorization to \(Ax=b\), retain an independent row subsystem when \(\operatorname{rank}[A\ b]=\operatorname{rank}A\), and declare inconsistency when the augmented rank is larger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-revealing presolve removes dependent equality rows or detects an inconsistent right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: Rank decisions are exact or use a declared numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}[A\ b]=\operatorname{rank}A\text{ permits row reduction; unequal ranks imply inconsistency}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Equality Presolve

children.title: Poor Conic Lifts

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\widetilde C=\mathbb R_+,\qquad \widetilde C\cap\operatorname{int}(\mathbb R_+^2)=\varnothing

notation.meaning: feasible set of the displayed lifted system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact conic lift can destroy strict feasibility in the lifted cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(\mathbb R_+\) has the exact lifted representation \(\widetilde C=\{(x,u,v):x=u,\ (u,v)\in\mathbb R_+^2,\ v=0\}\). Its projection onto \(x\) is exactly \(\mathbb R_+\), but no lifted feasible point has \((u,v)\in\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+^2\), since every feasible point has \(v=0\). Thus exactness of a conic lift does not imply lifted Slater feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift can force every lifted feasible point onto the cone boundary even when the projected set has nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Projection Without Lifted Slater Feasibility
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Projection Without Lifted Slater Feasibility
Poor Conic Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lift whose algorithmic burden exceeds that of an available equivalent formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ L(x,z)\in K\}\) be a conic lift, and let \(R\) be another formulation of the same set. Relative to a fixed interior-point implementation and accuracy \(\varepsilon\), call the lift poor when its estimated work \(W_L(\varepsilon)=N_L(\varepsilon)C_L\) exceeds \(W_R(\varepsilon)=N_R(\varepsilon)C_R\), where \(N\) counts Newton steps and \(C\) is per-step oracle and factorization cost. Thus geometric correctness of the projection alone does not make the lift algorithmically favorable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic lift is poor when, at fixed accuracy and implementation, its iteration count times per-step cost exceeds an equivalent formulation's work.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations project to the same closed convex set.
Accuracy and implementation conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_L(\varepsilon)>W_R(\varepsilon)\Rightarrow\text{the lift is poor relative to }R\)

children.title: Sparsity Loss
children.top_down_role: Destruction of exploitable sparsity by lifted conic representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lift can create fill edges among original variables that are absent from the original formulation's filled graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_L\) be the structural sparsity graph of a lifted symmetric Newton matrix, let \(R\) be the original-variable vertex set, and fix an elimination ordering \(\pi\). Suppose an auxiliary vertex \(v\notin R\) is eliminated while distinct vertices \(i,j\in R\) both survive, are adjacent to \(v\), and are not adjacent to each other immediately before eliminating \(v\). Elimination of \(v\) then creates the fill edge \(\{i,j\}\). If \(\{i,j\}\) is absent from the filled graph of the original formulation under the induced ordering, the lift has introduced structural fill among the original variables even though it represents the same projected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted formulation loses sparsity when eliminating an auxiliary variable joins two surviving original variables whose edge is absent from the corresponding filled graph of the original formulation.
assumptions_latex: The lifted Newton matrix is symmetric and has structural graph \(G_L\).
A fixed elimination ordering \(\pi\) is used.
When \(v\) is eliminated, \(i\) and \(j\) are surviving nonadjacent neighbors of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{i,j\}\in E\!\left(G_L^{+}(\pi)|_R\right)\setminus E\!\left(G_R^{+}(\pi|_R)\right)\)

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Burden from Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration cost growth from lifted dimensions and fill-in.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original and lifted Newton systems have orders \(n\) and \(n+r\), and let their Cholesky factors contain \(f_0\) and \(f_L\) nonzeros under specified orderings. Sparse factorization storage is \(O(f_L)\), while arithmetic is governed by the elimination-front sizes and can exceed the original cost when the lift increases fill. In the dense limiting model, the lifted factorization costs \(O((n+r)^3)\) arithmetic and \(O((n+r)^2)\) storage, versus \(O(n^3)\) and \(O(n^2)\) originally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted variables enlarge Newton systems and may increase fill; in the dense model this raises cubic factorization work and quadratic storage.
